### Childhood and schooling: 1874–1895

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Jennie_Churchill_with_her_sons.jpg/250px-Jennie_Churchill_with_her_sons.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jennie_Churchill_with_her_sons.jpg)

[Jennie Spencer Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Randolph_Churchill "Lady Randolph Churchill") with her two sons, [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Strange_Spencer-Churchill "John Strange Spencer-Churchill") (_left_) and Winston (_right_) in 1889

Winston Leonard Spencer Churchill was born on 30 November 1874 at his family's ancestral home, [Blenheim Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blenheim_Palace "Blenheim Palace") in [Oxfordshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfordshire "Oxfordshire").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins20015-3) On his father's side, he was a member of the aristocracy as a descendant of [John Churchill, 1st Duke of Marlborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Churchill,_1st_Duke_of_Marlborough "John Churchill, 1st Duke of Marlborough").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert19911Jenkins20013,_5-4) His father, [Lord Randolph Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Randolph_Churchill "Lord Randolph Churchill"), representing the [Conservative Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)"), had been elected [member of parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament_(United_Kingdom) "Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)") (MP) for [Woodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock_(UK_Parliament_constituency) "Woodstock (UK Parliament constituency)") in February 1874.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert19911Best20013Jenkins20017Robbins20142-5) His mother was [Jennie, Lady Randolph Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Randolph_Churchill "Lady Randolph Churchill"), a daughter of [Leonard Jerome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Jerome "Leonard Jerome"), an American businessman.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBest20014Jenkins20015%E2%80%936Addison20057-6)

In 1876, Churchill's paternal grandfather, [John Spencer-Churchill, 7th Duke of Marlborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Spencer-Churchill,_7th_Duke_of_Marlborough "John Spencer-Churchill, 7th Duke of Marlborough"), was appointed [Viceroy of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viceroy_of_Ireland "Viceroy of Ireland"). Randolph became his private secretary and the family relocated to [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert19911Addison20059-7) Winston's brother, [Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Strange_Spencer-Churchill "John Strange Spencer-Churchill"), was born there in 1880.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert19912Jenkins20017Addison200510-8) For much of the 1880s, Randolph and Jennie were effectively estranged,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins20018-9) and the brothers were cared for by their nanny, [Elizabeth Everest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Everest "Elizabeth Everest").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert19912%E2%80%933Jenkins200110ReaglesLarsen20138-10) When she died in 1895, Churchill wrote "she had been my dearest and most intimate friend during the whole of the twenty years I had lived".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBest20016-11)

Churchill began [boarding school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boarding_school "Boarding school") at [St George's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_School,_Ascot "St George's School, Ascot") in [Ascot, Berkshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascot,_Berkshire "Ascot, Berkshire"), aged 7, but he was not academic and his behaviour was poor.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert19913%E2%80%935Haffner200312Addison200510-12) In 1884, he transferred to [Brunswick School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoke_Brunswick_School "Stoke Brunswick School") in [Hove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hove "Hove"), where his academic performance improved.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert19916%E2%80%938Haffner200312%E2%80%9313-13) In April 1888, aged 13, he passed the entrance exam for [Harrow School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harrow_School "Harrow School").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199117%E2%80%9319-14) His father wanted him to prepare for a military career, so his last three years at Harrow were in the army form.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199122Jenkins200119-15) After two unsuccessful attempts to gain admittance to the [Royal Military College, Sandhurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Military_College,_Sandhurst "Royal Military College, Sandhurst"), he succeeded.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199132%E2%80%9333,_37Jenkins200120Haffner200315-16) He was accepted as a [cadet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadet "Cadet") in the [cavalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavalry "Cavalry"), starting in September 1893.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199137Jenkins200120%E2%80%9321-17) His father died in January 1895.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199148%E2%80%9349Jenkins200121Haffner200332-18)

### Cuba, India, and Sudan: 1895–1899

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_ZZZ5426F.jpg/250px-Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_ZZZ5426F.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_ZZZ5426F.jpg)

Churchill in the military dress uniform of the [4th Queen's Own Hussars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_Queen's_Own_Hussars "4th Queen's Own Hussars") at [Aldershot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldershot "Aldershot") in 1895[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaffner200318-19)

In February 1895, Churchill was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the [4th Queen's Own Hussars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/4th_Queen's_Own_Hussars "4th Queen's Own Hussars") regiment of the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army"), based at [Aldershot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldershot "Aldershot").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199151Jenkins200121-20) Eager to witness military action, he used his mother's influence to get posted to a war zone.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199162Jenkins200128-21) In the autumn, he and friend [Reggie Barnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reginald_Barnes "Reginald Barnes"), went to observe the [Cuban War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_War_of_Independence "Cuban War of Independence") and became involved in skirmishes after joining Spanish troops attempting to suppress independence fighters.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199156,_58%E2%80%9360Jenkins200128%E2%80%9329Robbins201414%E2%80%9315-22) Churchill sent reports to the _[Daily Graphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Graphic "The Graphic")_ in London.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-HGN-23) He proceeded to New York and wrote to his mother about "what an extraordinary people the Americans are!"[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199157-24) With the Hussars, he went to [Bombay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay "Bombay") in October 1896.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199163Jenkins200122-25) Based in [Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore"), he was in India for 19 months, visiting [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta") and joining expeditions to [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad_State "Hyderabad State") and the [North West Frontier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_history_of_the_North-West_Frontier "Military history of the North-West Frontier").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199163Jenkins200123%E2%80%9324-26)

In India, Churchill began a self-education project,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins200123%E2%80%9324Haffner200319-27) reading widely including [Plato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plato "Plato"), [Edward Gibbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Gibbon "Edward Gibbon"), [Charles Darwin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Darwin "Charles Darwin") and [Thomas Babington Macaulay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Babington_Macaulay "Thomas Babington Macaulay").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199167%E2%80%9368Jenkins200124%E2%80%9325Haffner200319-28) The books were sent by his mother, with whom he shared frequent correspondence. To learn about politics, he asked her to send him copies of _[The Annual Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Annual\_Register "The Annual Register")_, the political almanack.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTERoberts201852-29) In an 1898 letter, he referred to his beliefs, saying: "I do not accept the Christian or any other form of religious belief".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199192-30) Churchill had been [christened](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptism "Baptism") in the [Church of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_England "Church of England")[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReaglesLarsen20138-31) but underwent a virulently anti-Christian phase in his youth,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAddison198029ReaglesLarsen20139-32) and as an adult was an agnostic.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaffner200332ReaglesLarsen20138-33) In another letter to a cousin, he referred to religion as "a delicious narcotic" and expressed a preference for [Protestantism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestantism "Protestantism") over [Roman Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholicism "Roman Catholicism") because he felt it "a step nearer Reason".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991102-34)

Interested in parliamentary affairs,[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins200126-35) Churchill declared himself "a Liberal in all but name", adding he could never endorse the [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(UK) "Liberal Party (UK)")'s support for [Irish home rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_home_rule "Irish home rule").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199169Jenkins200127-36) Instead, he allied himself to the [Tory democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tory_democracy "Tory democracy") wing of the Conservatives and on a visit home, gave his first speech for the party's [Primrose League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primrose_League "Primrose League") at [Claverton Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claverton_Down "Claverton Down").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199169,_71Jenkins200127-37) Mixing reformist and conservative perspectives, he supported the promotion of [secular, non-denominational education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secular_education "Secular education") while opposing [women's suffrage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_suffrage_in_the_United_Kingdom "Women's suffrage in the United Kingdom").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199170-38)

Churchill volunteered to join [Bindon Blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bindon_Blood "Bindon Blood")'s [Malakand Field Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malakand_Field_Force "Malakand Field Force") in [its campaign against Mohmand rebels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohmand_campaign_of_1897%E2%80%9398 "Mohmand campaign of 1897–98") in the [Swat Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swat_Valley "Swat Valley") of north-west India. Blood accepted on condition he was assigned as a journalist, the beginning of Churchill's writing career.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199172,_75Jenkins200129%E2%80%9331-39) He returned to Bangalore in October 1897 and wrote his first book, _[The Story of the Malakand Field Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Story\_of\_the\_Malakand\_Field\_Force "The Story of the Malakand Field Force")_, which received positive reviews.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199179,_81%E2%80%9382Jenkins200131%E2%80%9332Haffner200321%E2%80%9322-40) He wrote his only work of fiction, _[Savrola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savrola "Savrola")_, a [Ruritanian romance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruritanian_romance "Ruritanian romance").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAddison198031Gilbert199181Jenkins200132%E2%80%9334-41) To keep occupied, Churchill embraced writing as what [Roy Jenkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Jenkins "Roy Jenkins") calls his "whole habit", especially through his career when he was out of office. Writing was his safeguard against recurring [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_depressive_disorder "Major depressive disorder"), which he referred to as his "black dog".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins2001819-42)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Winston_Churchill_in_uniform%2C_1898.jpg/250px-Winston_Churchill_in_uniform%2C_1898.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Winston_Churchill_in_uniform,_1898.jpg)

Winston Churchill posing in uniform in front of a backdrop depicting the [Egyptian Pyramids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Pyramids "Egyptian Pyramids"), 1898.

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Winston_Churchill_With_the_4th_Hussars_in_India%2C_1899._HU98777.jpg/250px-Winston_Churchill_With_the_4th_Hussars_in_India%2C_1899._HU98777.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Winston_Churchill_With_the_4th_Hussars_in_India,_1899._HU98777.jpg)

Officers involved in the Inter-Regimental Polo Tournament at Meerut, 1899. Winston Churchill is standing second from right.

Using London contacts, Churchill got attached to General [Herbert Kitchener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Kitchener "Herbert Kitchener")'s campaign in the Sudan as a [21st Lancers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st_Lancers "21st Lancers")[subaltern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subaltern_(military) "Subaltern (military)"), while working as a journalist for _[The Morning Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Morning\_Post "The Morning Post")_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199189%E2%80%9390Jenkins200135,_38%E2%80%9339Haffner200321-43) After participating in one of the British Army's last [cavalry charges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavalry_charge "Cavalry charge") in the [Battle of Omdurman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Omdurman "Battle of Omdurman") in September 1898, the 21st Lancers were stood down.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert199191%E2%80%9398Jenkins200139%E2%80%9341-44) In October, Churchill returned to England and began writing _[The River War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_River\_War "The River War")_ about the campaign; it was published in 1899. He decided to leave the army[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins200134,_41,_50Haffner200322-45) as he was critical of Kitchener's actions, particularly the unmerciful treatment of enemy wounded and his desecration of [Muhammad Ahmad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ahmad "Muhammad Ahmad")'s tomb.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAddison198032Gilbert199198%E2%80%9399Jenkins200141-46)

On 2 December 1898, Churchill embarked for India to settle his military business and complete his resignation. He spent much time playing [polo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polo "Polo"), the only ball sport in which he was ever interested. Having left the Hussars, he sailed from Bombay on 20 March 1899, determined to launch a career in politics.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins200141%E2%80%9344-47)

### Politics and South Africa: 1899–1901

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/67/Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_Q113382.jpg/250px-Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_Q113382.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_Q113382.jpg)

Churchill in 1900 around the time of his first election to Parliament[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHaffner2003x-48)

Churchill spoke at Conservative meetings[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins200142-49) and was selected as one of the party's two candidates for the June [1899 Oldham by-election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1899_Oldham_by-election "1899 Oldham by-election").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991103%E2%80%93104Jenkins200145%E2%80%9346Haffner200323-50) While campaigning, he referred to himself as "a Conservative and a Tory Democrat".[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991104-51) Although the seats had been held by the Conservatives, the result was a narrow Liberal victory.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991105Jenkins200147-52)

As a journalist for the _Morning Post_, Churchill anticipated the outbreak of the [Second Boer War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Boer_War "Second Boer War") between Britain and the [Boer republics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boer_republics "Boer republics"), leading him to sail to [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991105%E2%80%93106Jenkins200150-54) In October, he travelled to the conflict zone near [Ladysmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladysmith,_KwaZulu-Natal "Ladysmith, KwaZulu-Natal"), which was under siege by [Boer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boer "Boer") troops, and then headed to [Colenso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colenso,_KwaZulu-Natal "Colenso, KwaZulu-Natal").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991107%E2%80%93110-55) At the [Battle of Chieveley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Chieveley "Battle of Chieveley"), his train was derailed by Boer artillery shelling, and he was captured as a [prisoner of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war "Prisoner of war") (POW) and interned in a [POW camp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POW_camp "POW camp") in [Pretoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretoria "Pretoria").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991111%E2%80%93113Jenkins200152%E2%80%9353Haffner200325-56) Churchill made a formal protest about his internment to the Transvaal [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Secretary_of_the_South_African_Republic "State Secretary of the South African Republic"), asserting his status as a non-combatant journalist, but he was told he had invalidated that by carrying a revolver.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-57) In December, Churchill escaped and evaded his captors by stowing aboard freight trains and hiding in a mine. He made it to safety in [Portuguese East Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_East_Africa "Portuguese East Africa").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991115%E2%80%93120Jenkins200155%E2%80%9362-58) His escape attracted much publicity.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991121Jenkins200161-59)

In January 1900, Churchill briefly rejoined the army as a lieutenant in the [South African Light Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_African_Light_Horse "South African Light Horse") regiment, joining [Redvers Buller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redvers_Buller "Redvers Buller")'s fight to relieve the [Siege of Ladysmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_Ladysmith "Siege of Ladysmith") and take Pretoria.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991121%E2%80%93122Jenkins200161%E2%80%9362-60) He was among the first British troops into both places. With his cousin [Charles Spencer-Churchill, 9th Duke of Marlborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Spencer-Churchill,_9th_Duke_of_Marlborough "Charles Spencer-Churchill, 9th Duke of Marlborough"), he demanded and received the surrender of 52 Boer prison camp guards.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991123%E2%80%93124,_126%E2%80%93129Jenkins200162-61) Throughout the war, he publicly chastised anti-Boer prejudices, calling for them to be treated with "generosity and tolerance",[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991125-62) and afterwards urged the British to be magnanimous in victory.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins200163-63) In July, having resigned his lieutenancy, he returned to Britain. His _Morning Post_ dispatches had been published as _[London to Ladysmith via Pretoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London\_to\_Ladysmith\_via\_Pretoria "London to Ladysmith via Pretoria")_ and sold well.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991128%E2%80%93131-64)

Churchill rented a flat in London's [Mayfair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayfair "Mayfair"), using it as his base for six years. He stood again as a Conservative candidate at Oldham in the [October 1900 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1900_United_Kingdom_general_election "1900 United Kingdom general election"), securing a narrow victory to become a Member of Parliament aged 25.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991135%E2%80%93136-65) In the same month, he published _Ian Hamilton's March_, a book about his South African experiences,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991136-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins200165-67) which became the focus of a lecture tour in November through Britain, America, and Canada. Members of Parliament were unpaid and the tour was a financial necessity. In America, Churchill met [Mark Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain "Mark Twain"), [William McKinley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_McKinley "William McKinley"), and [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt"), who he did not get on with.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991136%E2%80%93138Jenkins200168%E2%80%9370-68) In spring 1901, he gave lectures in Paris, Madrid, and Gibraltar.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991141-69)

## Early political career: 1901–1908

### Conservative MP: 1901–1904

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/20/Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_Q42037.jpg/250px-Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_Q42037.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Winston_Churchill_1874_-_1965_Q42037.jpg)

Churchill in 1904 when he "[crossed the floor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossed_the_floor "Crossed the floor")"

In February 1901, Churchill took his seat in the [House of Commons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Commons_of_the_United_Kingdom "House of Commons of the United Kingdom"), where his [maiden speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maiden_speech "Maiden speech") gained widespread coverage.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991139Jenkins200171%E2%80%9373-70) He associated with a group of Conservatives known as the [Hughligans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hughligans "Hughligans"),[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTERhodes_James197016Jenkins200176%E2%80%9377-71) but was critical of the Conservative government on various issues, especially increases in army funding. He believed additional military expenditure should go to the navy.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991141%E2%80%93144Jenkins200174%E2%80%9375-72) This upset the Conservative [front bench](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Front_bench "Front bench") but was supported by Liberals, with whom he increasingly socialised, particularly [Liberal Imperialists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Imperialists "Liberal Imperialists") like [H. H. Asquith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._H._Asquith "H. H. Asquith").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991144-73) Churchill later wrote that he "drifted steadily to the left".[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991145-74) He privately considered "the gradual creation by an evolutionary process of a Democratic or Progressive wing to the Conservative Party",[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991150-75) or alternately a "Central Party" to unite the Conservatives and Liberals.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991151%E2%80%93152-76)

By 1903, there was division between Churchill and the Conservatives, largely because he opposed their promotion of [protectionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectionism "Protectionism"). As a [free trader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade "Free trade"), he helped found the [Free Food League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_Food_League "Free Food League").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-HGN-23) Churchill sensed that the animosity of party members would prevent him gaining a Cabinet position under a Conservative government. The Liberal Party was attracting growing support, and so his defection in 1904 may have been influenced by ambition.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTERhodes_James197022-77) He increasingly voted with the Liberals.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991162-78) For example, he opposed an increase in military expenditure,[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991153-79) supported a Liberal bill to restore legal rights to trade unions,[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991162-78) and opposed the introduction of import tariffs.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991152,_154-80)[Arthur Balfour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Balfour "Arthur Balfour")'s government announced protectionist legislation in October 1903.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991157-81) Two months later, incensed by Churchill's criticism of the government, the Oldham Conservative Association informed him it would not support his candidature at the next election.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991160Jenkins200184-82)

In May 1904, Churchill opposed the government's proposed Aliens Bill, designed to curb Jewish immigration.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991165-83) He stated that the bill would "appeal to insular prejudice against foreigners, to racial prejudice against Jews, and to labour prejudice against competition" and expressed himself in favour of "the old tolerant and generous practice of free entry and asylum to which this country has so long adhered and from which it has so greatly gained".[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991165-83) On 31 May 1904, he [crossed the floor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossed_the_floor "Crossed the floor") to sit as a member of the Liberal Party.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991165Jenkins200188-84)

### Liberal MP: 1904–1908

Main article: [Winston Churchill's Liberal Party years, 1904–1924](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill's_Liberal_Party_years,_1904%E2%80%931924 "Winston Churchill's Liberal Party years, 1904–1924")

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Churchill_und_Wilhelm_II._%281906%29.jpg/250px-Churchill_und_Wilhelm_II._%281906%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Churchill_und_Wilhelm_II._(1906).jpg)

Churchill and German Kaiser [Wilhelm II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_II "Wilhelm II") during a military manoeuvre near [Breslau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breslau "Breslau"), Silesia, in 1906

As a Liberal, Churchill attacked government policy and gained a reputation as a [radical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radicalisation "Radicalisation") under the influences of [John Morley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Morley "John Morley") and [David Lloyd George](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lloyd_George "David Lloyd George").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-HGN-23) In December 1905, Balfour resigned as prime minister and [King Edward VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Edward_VII "King Edward VII") invited the Liberal leader [Henry Campbell-Bannerman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Campbell-Bannerman "Henry Campbell-Bannerman") to replace him.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991173%E2%80%93174Jenkins2001103-85) Hoping to secure a [working majority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Working_majority "Working majority"), Campbell-Bannerman called a [general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1906_United_Kingdom_general_election "1906 United Kingdom general election") in January 1906, which the Liberals won in a massive landslide.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991174,_176-86) Churchill won the [Manchester North West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_North_West "Manchester North West") seat,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991175Jenkins2001109-87) and [his biography of his father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Randolph_Churchill_(book) "Lord Randolph Churchill (book)") was published,[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTERhodes_James197016Gilbert1991175-88) for which he received an [advance payment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advance_payment "Advance payment") of £8,000.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991171Jenkins2001100-89) It was generally well received.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins2001102%E2%80%93103-90) The first biography of Churchill himself, written by the Liberal [MacCallum Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacCallum_Scott "MacCallum Scott"), was also published around this time.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991172-91)

In the new government, Churchill became [Under-Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under-Secretary_of_State "Under-Secretary of State") for the [Colonial Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonial_Office "Colonial Office"), a [junior ministerial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_minister "Junior minister") position he had requested.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTERhodes_James197023Gilbert1991174Jenkins2001104-92) He worked beneath the [Secretary of State for the Colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_State_for_the_Colonies "Secretary of State for the Colonies"), [Victor Bruce, 9th Earl of Elgin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Bruce,_9th_Earl_of_Elgin "Victor Bruce, 9th Earl of Elgin"),[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins2001104%E2%80%93105-93) and took [Edward Marsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Marsh_(polymath) "Edward Marsh (polymath)") as his secretary; Marsh remained his secretary for 25 years.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991174Jenkins2001105-94) Churchill's first task was helping to draft a constitution for the [Transvaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transvaal_Colony "Transvaal Colony");[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991176Jenkins2001113%E2%80%93115,_120-95) and he helped oversee the formation of a government in the [Orange River Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_River_Colony "Orange River Colony").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991182-96) In dealing with southern Africa, he sought to ensure equality between the British and Boers.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991177-97) He announced a gradual phasing out of the use of Chinese indentured labourers in South Africa; he and the government decided a sudden ban would cause too much upset and might damage the colony's economy.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991177Jenkins2001111%E2%80%93113-98) He expressed concerns about the relations between European settlers and the black African population; after the [Zulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zulu_people "Zulu people") launched their [Bambatha Rebellion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bambatha_Rebellion "Bambatha Rebellion") in [Natal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Natal "Colony of Natal"), Churchill complained about the "disgusting butchery of the natives" by Europeans.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991183-99)

## Asquith government: 1908–1915

Main article: [Winston Churchill's Liberal Party years, 1904–1924](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill's_Liberal_Party_years,_1904%E2%80%931924 "Winston Churchill's Liberal Party years, 1904–1924")

### President of the Board of Trade: 1908–1910

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Winston_Churchill_%281874-1965%29_with_fianc%C3%A9e_Clementine_Hozier_%281885-1977%29_shortly_before_their_marriage_in_1908.jpg/250px-Winston_Churchill_%281874-1965%29_with_fianc%C3%A9e_Clementine_Hozier_%281885-1977%29_shortly_before_their_marriage_in_1908.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Winston_Churchill_(1874-1965)_with_fianc%C3%A9e_Clementine_Hozier_(1885-1977)_shortly_before_their_marriage_in_1908.jpg)

Churchill and his fiancée [Clementine Hozier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clementine_Hozier "Clementine Hozier") shortly before their marriage in 1908

With Campbell-Bannerman terminally ill, Asquith became prime minister in April 1908. He appointed Churchill as [President of the Board of Trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Board_of_Trade "President of the Board of Trade").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTERhodes_James197033Gilbert1991194Jenkins2001129-100) Aged 33, Churchill was the youngest [Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_Kingdom "Cabinet of the United Kingdom") member since 1866.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins2001129-101) Newly appointed Cabinet ministers were legally obliged to seek re-election at a by-election. On 24 April, Churchill lost the [Manchester North West by-election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_Manchester_North_West_by-election "1908 Manchester North West by-election") to the Conservative candidate by 429 votes.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991194%E2%80%93195Jenkins2001130-102) On 9 May, the Liberals stood him in the safe seat of [Dundee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dundee_(UK_Parliament_constituency) "Dundee (UK Parliament constituency)"), where he [won comfortably](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_Dundee_by-election "1908 Dundee by-election").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991195Jenkins2001130%E2%80%93131-103)

Churchill proposed marriage to [Clementine Hozier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clementine_Hozier "Clementine Hozier"); they were married on 12 September 1908 at [St Margaret's, Westminster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Margaret's,_Westminster "St Margaret's, Westminster") and honeymooned in [Baveno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baveno "Baveno"), Venice, and [Veveří Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veve%C5%99%C3%AD_Castle "Veveří Castle") in [Moravia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moravia "Moravia").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991198%E2%80%93200-104)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins2001139%E2%80%93142-105)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-106) They lived at 33 [Eccleston Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eccleston_Square "Eccleston Square"), London, and their first daughter, [Diana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diana_Churchill "Diana Churchill"), was born in 1909.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991204%E2%80%93205-107)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins2001203-108) The success of their marriage was important to Churchill's career as Clementine's unbroken affection provided him with a secure and happy background.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-HGN-23)

One of Churchill's first tasks as a minister was to arbitrate in an industrial dispute among ship-workers and employers, on the [River Tyne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Tyne "River Tyne").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991195-109) He afterwards established a Standing Court of Arbitration to deal with industrial disputes,[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991199-110) establishing a reputation as a conciliator.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991200-111) He worked with Lloyd George to champion [social reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_welfare_reforms "Liberal welfare reforms").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEJenkins2001143-112) He promoted what he called a "network of State intervention and regulation" akin to that in Germany.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991193%E2%80%93194-113)

Continuing Lloyd George's work,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-HGN-23) Churchill introduced the [Mines Eight Hours Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal_Mines_Regulation_Act_1908 "Coal Mines Regulation Act 1908"), which prohibited miners from working more than an [eight-hour day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eight-hour_day "Eight-hour day").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991196-114) In 1909, he introduced the [Trade Boards Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_Boards_Bill "Trade Boards Bill"), creating Trade Boards which could prosecute exploitative employers. Passing with a large majority, it established the principle of a [minimum wage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimum_wage "Minimum wage") and the right to have meal breaks.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991203%E2%80%93204Jenkins2001150-115) In May 1909, he proposed the [Labour Exchanges Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_Exchanges_Act_1909 "Labour Exchanges Act 1909") to establish over 200 Labour Exchanges through which the unemployed would be assisted in finding employment.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991204Jenkins2001150%E2%80%93151-116) He promoted the idea of an unemployment insurance scheme, which would be part-funded by the state.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGilbert1991201Jenkins2001151-117)

Mikhail Sergeyevich Gorbachev[g][h] (2 March 1931 – 30 August 2022) was a Soviet and Russian politician who was the last leader of the Soviet Union from 1985 until the country's dissolution in 1991. He served as General Secretary of the Communist Party from 1985, and additionally as head of state from 1988.[i] Ideologically, he initially adhered to Marxism–Leninism, but moved towards social democracy by the early 1990s.

Born in Privolnoye, North Caucasus Krai, into a peasant family of Russian and Ukrainian heritage, Gorbachev grew up under the rule of Joseph Stalin. In his youth, Gorbachev operated combine harvesters on a collective farm, before joining the Communist Party, which then governed the Soviet Union as a one-party state. Studying at Moscow State University, he married fellow student Raisa Titarenko in 1953 and received his law degree in 1955. Moving to Stavropol, he worked for the Komsomol youth organization and, after Stalin's death, became a keen proponent of the de-Stalinization reforms of Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev. Gorbachev was appointed the first party secretary of the Stavropol Regional Committee in 1970, overseeing the construction of the Great Stavropol Canal. In 1978, Gorbachev returned to Moscow to become a secretary of the party's Central Committee. He joined the governing Politburo (25th term) as a non-voting member the following year and as a voting member in 1980.

Three years after the death of Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev, and following the brief tenures of Yuri Andropov and Konstantin Chernenko in 1985, the Politburo elected Gorbachev as general secretary. Although committed to preserving the Soviet state and its Marxist–Leninist principles, Gorbachev believed significant reform was necessary for its survival. He withdrew troops from the Soviet–Afghan War, and embarked on summits with United States president Ronald Reagan to limit nuclear weapons and end the Cold War. Domestically, Gorbachev's policy of glasnost ("openness") and demokratizatsiya ("democratization") allowed for enhanced freedom of speech and the press, while his perestroika ("restructuring") sought to decentralize economic decision-making to improve its efficiency. Ultimately, his democratization measures and formation of the elected Congress of People's Deputies undermined the one-party state. When various Warsaw Pact countries abandoned Marxist–Leninist governance in 1989, he declined to intervene militarily. Growing nationalist sentiment within constituent republics threatened to break up the Soviet Union, leading hardliners within the party to launch an unsuccessful coup against him in August 1991. In the wake of the coup, the Soviet Union dissolved against Gorbachev's wishes.

After resigning from the presidency, he launched the Gorbachev Foundation, became a vocal critic of Russian presidents Boris Yeltsin and Vladimir Putin, and campaigned for Russia's social-democratic movement. Considered one of the most significant figures of the second half of the 20th century, Gorbachev remains controversial. The recipient of a wide range of awards, including the Nobel Peace Prize, he was praised for his role in ending the Cold War, introducing new political and economic freedoms in the Soviet Union, and tolerating both the fall of Marxist–Leninist administrations in eastern and central Europe and the German reunification. Critics see him as weakening Russia's global influence and precipitating an economic collapse in the country.

Early life and educationedit
1931–1950: Childhood and adolescenceedit
