### 1931–1948: Childhood and adolescence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1931–1948: Childhood and adolescence")]

Boris Nikolayevich Yeltsin was born on 1 February 1931 in [Butka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butka,_Russia "Butka, Russia"), a village in the [Ural Oblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ural_Oblast_(1923%E2%80%931934) "Ural Oblast (1923–1934)") of the [Russian SFSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_SFSR "Russian SFSR") of the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20004Colton200817-10) His family, who were ethnic Russians, had lived in this area of the [Urals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ural_Mountains "Ural Mountains") since at least the eighteenth century.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200814-11)

His father, Nikolai Yeltsin, had married his mother, Klavdiya Vasilyevna Starygina, in 1928.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20004Colton200816-12) Yeltsin always remained closer to his mother than to his father;[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200835%E2%80%9336-13) the latter beat his wife and children on various occasions.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200839-14) The Soviet Union was then under the leadership of [Joseph Stalin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stalin "Joseph Stalin"), who led the [one-party state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Soviet_Union_(1927%E2%80%931953) "History of the Soviet Union (1927–1953)") governed by the [Communist Party of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Communist Party of the Soviet Union") (CPSU). Seeking to transform the country into a [socialist society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socialist_mode_of_production "Socialist mode of production") according to [Marxist–Leninist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxism%E2%80%93Leninism "Marxism–Leninism") doctrine, in the late 1920s Stalin's government had initiated a project of [mass rural collectivisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collectivization_in_the_Soviet_Union "Collectivization in the Soviet Union") coupled with [dekulakization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dekulakization "Dekulakization"). As a prosperous farmer, Yeltsin's paternal grandfather, Ignatii, was accused of being a [kulak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kulak "Kulak") in 1930. His farm, which was in Basmanovo (also known as Basmanovskoye), was confiscated, and he and his family were forced to reside in a cottage in nearby Butka.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20005Colton200814%E2%80%9319-15) There, Nikolai and Ignatii's other children were allowed to join the local [kolkhoz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkhoz "Kolkhoz") ([collective farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_farming "Collective farming")), but Ignatii himself was not; he and his wife, Anna, were exiled in 1934 to [Nadezhdinsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serov_(town) "Serov (town)"),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-16) where he died two years later.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200819%E2%80%9321-17)

As an infant, Yeltsin was christened in the [Russian Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church "Russian Orthodox Church");[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20004Colton200817-10) his mother was devout, and his father unobservant.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200835-18) In the years after his birth, the area was hit by the [famine of 1932–1933](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_famine_of_1932%E2%80%931933 "Soviet famine of 1932–1933");[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200818-19) throughout his childhood, Yeltsin was often hungry.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20006%E2%80%937Colton200838-20) In 1932, Yeltsin's parents moved to [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20005Colton200822%E2%80%9323-21) where Yeltsin attended [kindergarten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kindergarten "Kindergarten").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200837-22) There, in 1934, the [OGPU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_State_Political_Directorate "Joint State Political Directorate") state security services arrested Nikolai, accused him of [anti-Soviet agitation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Article_58_(RSFSR_Penal_Code) "Article 58 (RSFSR Penal Code)"), and sentenced him to three years in the [Dmitrov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmitrov "Dmitrov") labor camp.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20005Colton200823%E2%80%9324,_26-23) Yeltsin and his mother then were ejected from their residence and were taken in by friends; Klavdiya worked at a garment factory in her husband's absence.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200825%E2%80%9326-24) In October 1936, Nikolai returned; in July 1937, the couple's second child, Mikhail, was born.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20006Colton200826-25) That month, they moved to [Berezniki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berezniki "Berezniki"), in [Perm Krai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perm_Krai "Perm Krai"), where Nikolai got work on a [potash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potash "Potash") combine project.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20006Colton200828-26) In July 1944, they had a third child, Valentina.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20007Colton200833-27)

Between 1939 and 1945, Yeltsin received a primary education at Berezniki's Railway School Number 95.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200837-22) Academically, he did well at primary school and was repeatedly elected class monitor by fellow pupils.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20008,_9Colton200841%E2%80%9342-28) There, he also took part in activities organized by the [Komsomol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komsomol "Komsomol") and [Vladimir Lenin All-Union Pioneer Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Lenin_All-Union_Pioneer_Organization "Vladimir Lenin All-Union Pioneer Organization").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200840%E2%80%9341-29) This overlapped with [Soviet involvement in the Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Front_(World_War_II) "Eastern Front (World War II)"), during which Yeltsin's paternal uncle, Andrian, served in the [Red Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Army "Red Army") and was killed.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200840-30) From 1945 to 1949, Yeltsin studied at the municipal secondary school number 1, also known as [Pushkin High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pushkin_High_School "Pushkin High School").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200837,_43-31) Yeltsin did well at secondary school,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200843-32) and there took an increasing interest in sports, becoming captain of the school's volleyball squad.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20009Colton200844-33) He enjoyed playing pranks and in one instance played with a grenade, which blew off the thumb and index finger of his left hand.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron20007%E2%80%938Colton200845%E2%80%9347-34) With friends, he would go on summer walking expeditions in the adjacent [taiga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiga "Taiga"), sometimes for many weeks.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200010-35)

### 1949–1960: University and career in construction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1949–1960: University and career in construction")]

In September 1949, Yeltsin was admitted to the [Ural Polytechnic Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ural_State_Technical_University "Ural State Technical University") (UPI) in [Sverdlovsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yekaterinburg "Yekaterinburg").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200011Colton200853-36) He took the stream in industrial and civil engineering, which included courses in maths, physics, materials and soil science, and draftsmanship.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200856-37) He was also required to study Marxist–Leninist doctrine and choose a language course, for which he selected German, although never became adept at it.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200856-37) Tuition was free and he was provided a small stipend to live on, which he supplemented by unloading railway trucks for a small wage.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200014-38) Academically, he achieved high grades,[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200017Colton200858-39) although temporarily dropped out in 1952 when afflicted with [tonsillitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonsillitis "Tonsillitis") and [rheumatic fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rheumatic_fever "Rheumatic fever").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200017Colton200856-40) He devoted much time to [athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_of_athletics "Sport of athletics"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200859-41) and joined the UPI volleyball team.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200016Colton200864-42) He avoided any involvement in political organizations while there.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200859-41) During the summer 1953 break, he traveled across the Soviet Union, touring the [Volga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volga "Volga"), central Russia, [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byelorussian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic"), [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic"), and [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic"); much of the travel was achieved by hitchhiking on freight trains.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200015%E2%80%9316Colton200862-43) It was at UPI that he began a relationship with [Naina Iosifovna Girina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naina_Yeltsina "Naina Yeltsina"), a fellow student who would later become his wife.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200018Colton200858-44) Yeltsin completed his studies in June 1955.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200017Colton200856-40)

Leaving the Ural Polytechnic Institute, Yeltsin was assigned to work with the Lower Iset Construction Directorate in Sverdlovsk; at his request, he served the first year as a trainee in various building trades.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200020Colton200864-45) He quickly rose through the organization's ranks. In June 1956 he was promoted to foreman (_master_), and in June 1957 was promoted again, to the position of work superintendent (_prorab_).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200021,_23Colton200865-46) In these positions, he confronted widespread alcoholism and a lack of motivation among construction workers, an irregular supply of materials, and the regular theft or vandalism of available materials. He soon imposed fines for those who damaged or stole materials or engaged in absenteeism, and closely monitored productivity.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200021%E2%80%9322-47) His work on the construction of a textile factory, for which he oversaw 1000 workers, brought him wider recognition.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200025%E2%80%9326-48) In June 1958 he became a senior work superintendent (_starshii prorab_) and in January 1960 was made head engineer (_glavni inzhener_) of Construction Directorate Number 13.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200026%E2%80%9327Colton200865-49)

At the same time, Yeltsin's family was growing; in September 1956, he married Girina.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200024Colton200866-50) She soon got work at a scientific research institute, where she remained for 29 years.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200025-51) In August 1957, their daughter Yelena was born, followed by a second daughter, Tatyana, in January 1960.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200032%E2%80%9333Colton200866-52) During this period, they moved through a succession of apartments.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200866,_68-53) On family holidays, Yeltsin took his family to a lake in northern Russia and the [Black Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea "Black Sea") coast.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200034-54)

## CPSU career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: CPSU career")]

### 1960–1975: Early membership of the Communist Party

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1960–1975: Early membership of the Communist Party")]

In March 1960, Yeltsin became a probationary member of the governing Communist Party and a full member in March 1961.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAron200030Colton200868-55) In his later autobiography, he stated that his original reasons for joining were "sincere" and rooted in a genuine belief in the party's socialist ideals.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200886-56) In other interviews he instead stated that he joined because membership was a necessity for career advancement.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200869-57) His career continued to progress during the early 1960s; in February 1962 he was promoted chief (_nachal'nik_) of the construction directorate.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200865-58) In June 1963, Yeltsin was reassigned to the Sverdlovsk House-Building Combine as its head engineer,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200865-58) and in December 1965 became the combine's director.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200865-58) During this period he was largely involved in building residential housing, the expansion of which was a major priority for the government. He gained a reputation within the construction industry as a hard worker who was punctual and effective and who was used to meeting the targets set forth by the state apparatus. There had been plans to award him the [Order of Lenin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Lenin "Order of Lenin") for his work, although this was scrapped after a five-story building he was constructing collapsed in March 1966. An official investigation found that Yeltsin was not culpable for the accident.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200865,_70,_71,_72-59)

Within the local Communist Party, Yeltsin gained a patron in [Yakov Ryabov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakov_Ryabov?action=edit&redlink=1 "Yakov Ryabov (page does not exist)"), who became the first secretary of the party _[gorkom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorkom "Gorkom")_ in 1963.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200872%E2%80%9373-60) In April 1968, Ryabov decided to recruit Yeltsin into the regional party apparatus, proposing him for a vacancy in the _[obkom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obkom "Obkom")_'s department for construction. Ryabov ensured that Yeltsin got the job despite objections that he was not a longstanding party member.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200873%E2%80%9374-61) That year, Yeltsin and his family moved into a four-room apartment on Mamin-Sibiryak Street, downtown Sverdlovsk.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200886-56) Yeltsin then received his second [Order of the Red Banner of Labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Red_Banner_of_Labor "Order of the Red Banner of Labor") for his work completing a cold-rolling mill at the Upper Iset Works, a project for which he had overseen the actions of 15,000 laborers.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200875-62) In the late 1960s, Yeltsin was permitted to visit the West for the first time as he was sent on a trip to France.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200896-63) In 1975, Yeltsin was then made one of the five _obkom_ secretaries in the Sverdlovsk Oblast, a position that gave him responsibility not only for construction in the region but also for the forest and the pulp-and-paper industries. Also in 1975, his family relocated to a flat in the House of Old Bolsheviks on March Street.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200875%E2%80%9376,_86-64)

### 1976–1985: First Secretary of Sverdlovsk Oblast

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1976–1985: First Secretary of Sverdlovsk Oblast")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Leonid_Brezhnev_Portrait_%281%29.jpg/250px-Leonid_Brezhnev_Portrait_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Leonid_Brezhnev_Portrait_(1).jpg)

In 1976, Yeltsin was interviewed by [Leonid Brezhnev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Brezhnev "Leonid Brezhnev"), General Secretary of the Communist Party, who decided that he was an appropriate choice to become First Secretary of the party's Sverdlovsk _obkom_.

In October 1976, Ryabov was promoted to a new position in Moscow. He recommended that Yeltsin replace him as the First Secretary of the Party Committee in Sverdlovsk Oblast.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200876%E2%80%9377-65)[Leonid Brezhnev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Brezhnev "Leonid Brezhnev"), who then led the Soviet Union as [General Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union") of the party's [Central Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Committee_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union"), interviewed Yeltsin personally to determine his suitability and agreed with Ryabov's assessment.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200877-66) At the Central Committee's recommendation, the Sverdlovsk obkom then unanimously voted to appoint Yeltsin as its first secretary. This made him one of the youngest provincial first secretaries in the Russian SFSR, and gave him significant power within the province.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200877%E2%80%9381-67)

Where possible, Yeltsin tried to improve consumer welfare in the province, arguing that it would make for more productive workers.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200894-68) Under his provincial leadership, work started on various construction and infrastructure projects in the city of Sverdlovsk, including [a subway system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yekaterinburg_Metro "Yekaterinburg Metro"), the replacement of its barracks housing, new theaters and a circus, the refurbishment of its 1912 opera house, and youth housing projects to build new homes for young families.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200895-69) In September 1977, Yeltsin carried out orders to demolish the [Ipatiev House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipatiev_House "Ipatiev House"), the location where the [Romanov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Romanov "House of Romanov") royal family [had been killed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_of_the_Romanov_family "Execution of the Romanov family") in 1918, over the government's fears that it was attracting growing foreign and domestic attention. He was also responsible for punishing those living in the province who wrote or published material that the Soviet government considered to be seditious or damaging to the established order.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200889%E2%80%9391-70)

Yeltsin sat on the civil-military collegium of the [Urals Military District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urals_Military_District "Urals Military District") and attended its field exercises.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200880-71) In October 1978, the [Ministry of Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Defense_(Soviet_Union) "Ministry of Defense (Soviet Union)") gave him the rank of [colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel_(Eastern_Europe) "Colonel (Eastern Europe)").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200880-71) Also in 1978, Yeltsin was elected without opposition to the [Supreme Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_the_Soviet_Union "Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200884-72) In 1979 Yeltsin and his family moved into a five-room apartment at the Working Youth Embankment in Sverdlovsk.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200887-73) In February 1981, Yeltsin gave a speech to the [26th CPSU Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/26th_Congress_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "26th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union") and on the final day of the Congress was selected to join the Communist Party Central Committee.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200884-72)

Yeltsin's reports to party meetings reflected the ideological [conformity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conformity "Conformity") that was expected within the authoritarian state.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200889-74) Yeltsin played along with the [personality cult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality_cult "Personality cult") surrounding Brezhnev, but he was contemptuous of what he saw as the Soviet leader's vanity and sloth. He later claimed to have quashed plans for a Brezhnev museum in Sverdlovsk.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200886-56) While First Secretary, his world-view began to shift, influenced by his reading; he kept up with a wide range of journals published in the country and also claimed to have read an illegally printed _[samizdat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samizdat "Samizdat")_ copy of [Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aleksandr_Solzhenitsyn "Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn")'s _[The Gulag Archipelago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Gulag\_Archipelago "The Gulag Archipelago")_.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200895%E2%80%9396-75) Many of his concerns about the Soviet system were prosaic rather than ideological, as he believed that the system was losing effectiveness and beginning to decay.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200896-63) He was increasingly faced with the problem of Russia's place within the Soviet Union; unlike other republics in the country, the RSFSR lacked the same levels of autonomy from the central government in Moscow. In the early 1980s, he and Yurii Petrov privately devised a tripartite scheme for reforming the Soviet Union that would involve strengthening the Russian government, but it was never presented publicly.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200898%E2%80%9399-76)

By 1980, Yeltsin had developed the habit of appearing unannounced in factories, shops, and public transport to get a closer look at the realities of Soviet life.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008100-77) In May 1981, he held a question-and-answer session with college students at the Sverdlovsk Youth Palace, where he was unusually frank in his discussion of the country's problems.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008101-78) In December 1982 he then gave a television broadcast for the region in which he responded to various letters.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008101%E2%80%93103-79) This personalised approach to interacting with the public brought disapproval from some Communist Party figures, such as First Secretary of [Tyumen Oblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyumen_Oblast "Tyumen Oblast"), Gennadii Bogomyakov, although the Central Committee showed no concern.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008103%E2%80%93104-80) In 1981, he was awarded the [Order of Lenin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Lenin "Order of Lenin") for his work.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200893-81) The following year, Brezhnev died and was succeeded by [Yuri Andropov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuri_Andropov "Yuri Andropov"), who in turn ruled for 15 months before his own death;[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton200890-82) Yeltsin spoke positively about Andropov.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008108-83) Andropov was succeeded by another short-lived leader, [Konstantin Chernenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konstantin_Chernenko "Konstantin Chernenko").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008109-84) After his death, Yeltsin took part in the Central Committee plenum which appointed Mikhail Gorbachev the new [General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union"), and thus _de facto_[Soviet leader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_leaders_of_the_Soviet_Union "List of leaders of the Soviet Union"), in March 1985.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008109-84)

### 1985: Relocation to Moscow to become Head of Gorkom

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 1985: Relocation to Moscow to become Head of Gorkom")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/RIAN_archive_850809_General_Secretary_of_the_CPSU_CC_M._Gorbachev_%28crop%29.jpg/250px-RIAN_archive_850809_General_Secretary_of_the_CPSU_CC_M._Gorbachev_%28crop%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RIAN_archive_850809_General_Secretary_of_the_CPSU_CC_M._Gorbachev_(crop).jpg)

Mikhail Gorbachev took office as the General Secretary of the Communist Party in 1985; he soon promoted Yeltsin to a job in Moscow.

Gorbachev was interested in reforming the Soviet Union and, at the urging of [Yegor Ligachyov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yegor_Ligachyov "Yegor Ligachyov"), the organizational secretary of the Central Committee, soon summoned Yeltsin to meet with him as a potential ally in his efforts.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008109-84) Yeltsin had some reservations about Gorbachev as a leader, deeming him controlling and patronizing, but committed himself to the latter's project of reform.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008110,_118-85) In April 1985, Gorbachev appointed Yeltsin head of the Construction Department of the Party's Central Committee. Although it entailed moving to the capital city, Yeltsin was unhappy with what he regarded as a demotion.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008111%E2%80%93112-86)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-87) There, he was issued a [nomenklatura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomenklatura "Nomenklatura") flat at 54 Second Tverskaya-Yamskaya Street, where his daughter [Tatyana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatyana_Yumasheva "Tatyana Yumasheva") and her son and husband soon joined him and his wife.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008112-88) Gorbachev soon promoted Yeltsin to secretary of the Central Committee for construction and capital investment, a position within the powerful [CPSU Central Committee Secretariat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretariat_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Secretariat of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union"), a move approved by the Central Committee plenum in July 1985.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-Leon_Aron_2000._page_739-89)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008112%E2%80%93113-90)

With Gorbachev's support, in December 1985, Yeltsin was installed as the first secretary of the [Moscow gorkom of the CPSU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_City_Committee_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Moscow City Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008113-91) He was now responsible for managing the Soviet capital city, which had a population of 8.7 million.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008115-92) In February 1986, Yeltsin became a candidate (non-voting) member of the [Politburo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Politburo of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008116-93) At that point he formally left the Secretariat to concentrate on his role in Moscow.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008116-93) Over the coming year he removed many of the old secretaries of the gorkom, replacing them with younger individuals, particularly with backgrounds in factory management.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008119%E2%80%93120-94) In August 1986, Yeltsin gave a two-hour report to the party conference in which he talked about Moscow's problems, including issues that had previously not been spoken about publicly. Gorbachev described the speech as a "strong fresh wind" for the party.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008118-95) Yeltsin expressed a similar message at the [27th Congress of the CPSU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/27th_Congress_of_the_CPSU "27th Congress of the CPSU") in February 1986 and then in a speech at the House of Political Enlightenment in April.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColton2008119-96)

### 1987: Resignation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 1987: Resignation")]

On 10 September 1987, after a lecture from hard-liner [Yegor Ligachyov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yegor_Ligachyov "Yegor Ligachyov") at the Politburo for allowing two small unsanctioned demonstrations on Moscow streets, Yeltsin wrote a letter of resignation to Gorbachev who was holidaying on the Black Sea.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-oclery-97) When Gorbachev received the letter he was stunned – nobody in Soviet history had voluntarily resigned from the ranks of the Politburo. Gorbachev phoned Yeltsin and asked him to reconsider.

On 27 October 1987 at the plenary meeting of the Central Committee of the [CPSU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Communist Party of the Soviet Union"), Yeltsin, frustrated that Gorbachev had not addressed any of the issues outlined in his resignation letter, asked to speak. He expressed his discontent with the slow pace of reform in society, the servility shown to the general secretary, and opposition to him from Ligachyov making his position untenable. He then requested that he be allowed to resign from the Politburo, adding that the [City Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_City_Committee_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Moscow City Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union") would decide whether he should resign from the post of [First Secretary of the Moscow Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Secretary_of_the_Moscow_Communist_Party "First Secretary of the Moscow Communist Party").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-oclery-97) Aside from the fact that no one had ever quit the Politburo before, no one in the party had addressed a leader of the party in such a manner in front of the Central Committee since [Leon Trotsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Trotsky "Leon Trotsky") in the 1920s.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-oclery-97) In his reply, Gorbachev accused Yeltsin of "political immaturity" and "absolute irresponsibility". Nobody in the Central Committee backed Yeltsin.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-98)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/RIAN_archive_37106_Boris_Yeltsin_and_Raisa_Gorbachev.jpg/250px-RIAN_archive_37106_Boris_Yeltsin_and_Raisa_Gorbachev.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RIAN_archive_37106_Boris_Yeltsin_and_Raisa_Gorbachev.jpg)

Yeltsin with [Raisa Gorbacheva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raisa_Gorbachova "Raisa Gorbachova")

Within days, news of Yeltsin's actions leaked and rumors of his "secret speech" at the Central Committee spread throughout Moscow. Soon, fabricated _[samizdat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samizdat "Samizdat")_ versions began to circulate – this was the beginning of Yeltsin's rise as a rebel and growth in popularity as an anti-establishment figure.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-99) Gorbachev called a meeting of the Moscow City Party Committee for 11 November 1987 to launch another crushing attack on Yeltsin and confirm his dismissal. On 9 November 1987, Yeltsin apparently tried to kill himself and was rushed to the hospital bleeding profusely from self-inflicted cuts to his chest. Gorbachev ordered the injured Yeltsin from his hospital bed to the Moscow party plenum two days later where he was ritually denounced by the party faithful in what was reminiscent of a [Stalinist show trial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stalinist_show_trial "Stalinist show trial") before he was fired from the post of [First Secretary of the Moscow Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Secretary_of_the_Moscow_Communist_Party "First Secretary of the Moscow Communist Party"). Yeltsin said he would never forgive Gorbachev for this "immoral and inhuman" treatment.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-oclery-97)

Yeltsin was demoted to the position of First Deputy Commissioner for the [State Committee for Construction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Committee_for_Construction "State Committee for Construction"). At the next meeting of the Central Committee on 24 February 1988, Yeltsin was removed from his position as a Candidate member of the Politburo. He was perturbed and humiliated but began plotting his revenge.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-StrangeDeath86-100) His opportunity came with Gorbachev's establishment of the [Congress of People's Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_People's_Deputies_of_the_Soviet_Union "Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-StrangeDeath90-101) Yeltsin recovered and started intensively criticizing Gorbachev, highlighting the slow pace of reform in the Soviet Union as his major argument.

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Boris_Yeltsin_21_February_1989-1.jpg/250px-Boris_Yeltsin_21_February_1989-1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Boris_Yeltsin_21_February_1989-1.jpg)

Yeltsin as candidate for the Congress of People's Deputies in 1989

Yeltsin's criticism of the Politburo and Gorbachev led to a smear campaign against him, in which examples of Yeltsin's awkward behavior were used against him. Speaking at the CPSU conference in 1988, Yegor Ligachyov stated, "[Boris, you are wrong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris,_you_are_wrong "Boris, you are wrong")". An article in _[Pravda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pravda "Pravda")_ described Yeltsin as drunk at a lecture during his visit to the United States in September 1989,[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-102) an allegation which appeared to be confirmed by a TV account of his speech; however, popular dissatisfaction with the regime was strong, and these attempts to smear Yeltsin only added to his popularity. In another incident, Yeltsin fell from a bridge. Commenting on this event, Yeltsin hinted that he was helped to fall by the enemies of [perestroika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perestroika "Perestroika"), but his opponents suggested that he was simply drunk.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-103)

Between 1988 and 1991, Yeltsin established himself as the hero of the [anti-communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communism "Anti-communism") opposition in the Soviet Union.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-ab-104) On 26 March 1989, Yeltsin [was elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_Soviet_Union_legislative_election "1989 Soviet Union legislative election") to the [Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_People's_Deputies_of_the_Soviet_Union "Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union") as the delegate from Moscow district with 92% of the vote,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-Leon_Aron_2000._page_739-89) and on 29 May 1989, he was elected by the [Congress of People's Deputies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_People's_Deputies_of_the_Soviet_Union "Congress of People's Deputies of the Soviet Union") to a seat on the [Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_the_Soviet_Union "Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union"). On 19 July 1989, Yeltsin announced the formation of the radical pro-reform faction in the Congress of People's Deputies, the [Inter-Regional Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter-Regional_Group "Inter-Regional Group") of Deputies, and on 29 July 1989 was elected one of the five co-chairmen of the Inter-Regional Group.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-Leon_Aron_2000._page_739-89) Following these victories, Yeltsin became a renowned leader with a reputation as an anti-communist revolutionary.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-ab-104)

On 16 September 1989, during [a tour of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_visit_by_Boris_Yeltsin_to_the_United_States "1989 visit by Boris Yeltsin to the United States"), Yeltsin toured a medium-sized grocery store ([Randalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randalls "Randalls")) in [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-105) Leon Aron, quoting a Yeltsin associate, wrote in his 2000 biography, _Yeltsin, A Revolutionary Life_ (St. Martin's Press): "For a long time, on the plane to Miami, he sat motionless, his head in his hands. 'What have they done to our poor people?' he said after a long silence." He added, "On his return to Moscow, Yeltsin would confess the pain he had felt after the Houston excursion: the 'pain for all of us, for our country so rich, so talented and so exhausted by incessant experiments'." He wrote that Mr. Yeltsin added, "I think we have committed a crime against our people by making their standard of living so incomparably lower than that of the Americans." An aide, Lev Sukhanov, was reported to have said that it was at that moment that "the last vestige of Bolshevism collapsed" inside his boss.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-106) In his autobiography, _Against the Grain: An Autobiography_, written and published in 1990, Yeltsin hinted in a small passage that after his tour, he made plans to open his line of grocery stores and planned to fill it with government-subsidized goods to alleviate the country's problems.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Presidency of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (1990–1991)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Presidency of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (1990–1991)")]

On 4 March 1990, Yeltsin was elected to the [Congress of People's Deputies of Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_People's_Deputies_of_Russia "Congress of People's Deputies of Russia") representing Sverdlovsk with 72% of the vote.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-107) On 29 May 1990, he was elected chairman of the [Supreme Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_the_Russian_SFSR "Supreme Soviet of the Russian SFSR") of the [Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic") (RSFSR), although Gorbachev personally pleaded with the Russian deputies not to select Yeltsin.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-dob30may-108)

A part of this power struggle was the opposition between the power structures of the Soviet Union and the RSFSR. In an attempt to gain more power, on 12 June 1990, the Congress of People's Deputies of the RSFSR adopted a declaration of sovereignty. On 12 July 1990, Yeltsin resigned from the CPSU in a dramatic speech before party members at the [28th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/28th_Congress_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "28th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union"), some of whom responded by shouting "Shame!"[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-109)

### 1991: Presidential election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 1991: Presidential election")]

Main article: [Boris Yeltsin 1991 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin_1991_presidential_campaign "Boris Yeltsin 1991 presidential campaign")

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Boris_Yeltsin_22_August_1991-1.jpg/250px-Boris_Yeltsin_22_August_1991-1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Boris_Yeltsin_22_August_1991-1.jpg)

Yeltsin on 22 August 1991

During May 1991 [Václav Havel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V%C3%A1clav_Havel "Václav Havel") invited Yeltsin to [Prague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prague "Prague") where the latter unambiguously condemned the Soviet intervention in 1968.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-spero07-110)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-akby-111)

On 12 June Yeltsin won 57% of the popular vote in the democratic [presidential elections for the Russian republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Russian_presidential_election "1991 Russian presidential election"), defeating Gorbachev's preferred candidate, [Nikolai Ryzhkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolai_Ryzhkov "Nikolai Ryzhkov"), who got just 16% of the vote, and four other candidates. In his election campaign, Yeltsin criticized the "dictatorship of the center", but did not suggest the introduction of a market economy. Instead, he said that he would put his head on the railtrack in the event of increased prices. Yeltsin took office on 10 July, and reappointed [Ivan Silayev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Silayev "Ivan Silayev") as [Chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_heads_of_government_of_the_Soviet_Union "List of heads of government of the Soviet Union") of the [Council of Ministers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_the_Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Government of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic") of the Russian SFSR.

On 18 August 1991, a [coup against Gorbachev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Soviet_coup_d'%C3%A9tat_attempt "1991 Soviet coup d'état attempt") was launched by the government members opposed to perestroika. Gorbachev was held in [Crimea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimean_Autonomous_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Crimean Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic") while Yeltsin raced to the [White House of Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_of_Russia "White House of Russia") (residence of the Supreme Soviet of the RSFSR) in Moscow to defy the coup, making a memorable speech from atop the turret of a tank onto which he had climbed. The White House was surrounded by the military, but the troops defected in the face of mass popular demonstrations. By 21 August most of the coup leaders had fled Moscow and Gorbachev was "rescued" from Crimea and then returned to Moscow. Yeltsin was subsequently hailed by his supporters around the world for rallying mass opposition to the coup.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Although restored to his position, Gorbachev had been destroyed politically. Neither union nor Russian power structures heeded his commands as support had swung over to Yeltsin. By September, Gorbachev could no longer influence events outside of Moscow. Taking advantage of the situation, Yeltsin began taking over what remained of the Soviet government, ministry by ministry—including the Kremlin. On 6 November 1991, Yeltsin issued a decree banning all Communist Party activities on Russian soil. In early December 1991, [Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") voted for independence from the Soviet Union. A week later, on 8 December, Yeltsin met Ukrainian president [Leonid Kravchuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Kravchuk "Leonid Kravchuk") and the leader of [Belarus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarus "Belarus"), [Stanislav Shushkevich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanislav_Shushkevich "Stanislav Shushkevich"), in [Belovezhskaya Pushcha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belovezhskaya_Pushcha "Belovezhskaya Pushcha"). In the [Belovezha Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belovezha_Accords "Belovezha Accords"), the three presidents declared that the Soviet Union no longer existed "as a subject of international law and geopolitical reality", and announced the formation of a voluntary [Commonwealth of Independent States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Independent_States "Commonwealth of Independent States") (CIS) in its place.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-112)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-books.google.com-113)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg/250px-RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RIAN_archive_848095_Signing_the_Agreement_to_eliminate_the_USSR_and_establish_the_Commonwealth_of_Independent_States.jpg)

[Leaders of the Soviet Republics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republics_of_the_Soviet_Union "Republics of the Soviet Union") sign the [Belovezha Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belovezha_Accords "Belovezha Accords")

On 17 December, in a meeting with Yeltsin, Gorbachev accepted the _[fait accompli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point\_of\_no\_return "Point of no return")_ and agreed to [dissolve the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union "Dissolution of the Soviet Union"). On 24 December, by mutual agreement of the other CIS states (which by this time included all of the remaining republics except Georgia), the Russian Federation took the Soviet Union's seat in the United Nations. The next day, Gorbachev resigned and handed the functions of his office to Yeltsin.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-114) On 26 December, the [Council of the Republics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_of_Nationalities "Soviet of Nationalities"), the upper house of the Supreme Soviet, voted the Soviet Union out of existence, thereby ending the world's oldest, largest and most powerful Communist state.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-books.google.com-113) Economic relations between the former Soviet republics were severely compromised. Millions of ethnic Russians found themselves in newly formed foreign countries.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-apn.ru-115)

Initially, Yeltsin promoted the retention of national borders according to the pre-existing Soviet state borders, although this left ethnic [Russians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russians "Russians") as a majority in parts of northern [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan"), eastern Ukraine, and areas of [Estonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estonia "Estonia") and [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia "Latvia").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEvans199438%E2%80%9339-116)

## Presidency of independent Russia (1991–1999)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Presidency of independent Russia (1991–1999)")]

Main article: [Presidency of Boris Yeltsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Boris_Yeltsin "Presidency of Boris Yeltsin")

### 1991–1996: First term

#### Radical reforms

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Boris_Yeltsin&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Radical reforms")]

Main article: [Yeltsin–Gaidar government reforms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeltsin%E2%80%93Gaidar_government_reforms "Yeltsin–Gaidar government reforms")

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/RIAN_archive_52076_Leonid_Kravchuk%2C_Stanislav_Shushkevich_and_Boris_Yeltsin.jpg/250px-RIAN_archive_52076_Leonid_Kravchuk%2C_Stanislav_Shushkevich_and_Boris_Yeltsin.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RIAN_archive_52076_Leonid_Kravchuk,_Stanislav_Shushkevich_and_Boris_Yeltsin.jpg)

Yeltsin shortly after signing the [Belovezha Accords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belovezha_Accords "Belovezha Accords") with [Leonid Kravchuk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Kravchuk "Leonid Kravchuk") and [Stanislav Shushkevich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanislav_Shushkevich "Stanislav Shushkevich"), 8 December 1991

Just days after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Yeltsin resolved to embark on a programme of radical economic reform. Surpassing Gorbachev's reforms, which sought to expand democracy in the socialist system, the new regime aimed to completely dismantle socialism and fully implement capitalism, converting the world's largest command economy into a free-market one. During early discussions of this transition, Yeltsin's advisers debated issues of speed and sequencing, with an apparent division between those favoring a rapid approach and those favoring a gradual or slower approach. On 1 February 1992, Yeltsin signed accords with U.S. president [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush"), declaring the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") officially over after nearly 47 years.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-117) A visit to Moscow from Havel in April 1992 occasioned the written repudiation of the Soviet intervention and the withdrawal of armed forces from Czechoslovakia.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-akby-111) Yeltsin laid a wreath during a November 1992 ceremony in [Budapest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest "Budapest"), apologized for the [1956 Soviet intervention in Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_Soviet_intervention_in_Hungary "1956 Soviet intervention in Hungary") and handed over to president [Árpád Göncz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81rp%C3%A1d_G%C3%B6ncz "Árpád Göncz") documents from the Communist Party and [KGB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KGB "KGB") archives related to the intervention.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-akby-111) A treaty of friendship was signed in May 1992 with [Lech Wałęsa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lech_Wa%C5%82%C4%99sa "Lech Wałęsa")'s [Poland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland "Poland"), and then another one in August 1992 with [Zhelyu Zhelev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhelyu_Zhelev "Zhelyu Zhelev")'s [Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria "Bulgaria").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-akby-111)

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/22/President_and_Mrs._Bush_show_Russian_President_Boris_Yeltsin_the_South_Grounds_of_the_White_House_and_stop_at_the..._-_NARA_-_186451.jpg/250px-President_and_Mrs._Bush_show_Russian_President_Boris_Yeltsin_the_South_Grounds_of_the_White_House_and_stop_at_the..._-_NARA_-_186451.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_and_Mrs._Bush_show_Russian_President_Boris_Yeltsin_the_South_Grounds_of_the_White_House_and_stop_at_the..._-_NARA_-_186451.jpg)

Yeltsin with U.S. president [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") and First Lady [Barbara Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Bush "Barbara Bush") at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House"), Washington, D.C., 1992

On 2 January 1992, Yeltsin, acting as his own [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Russia "Prime Minister of Russia"), began a [major economic and administrative reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeltsin%E2%80%93Gaidar_government_reforms "Yeltsin–Gaidar government reforms"), ordering the liberalization of [foreign trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_trade "Foreign trade"), [prices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prices_control "Prices control"), and currency. At the same time, Yeltsin followed a policy of "macroeconomic stabilization", a harsh austerity regime designed to control inflation. Under Yeltsin's stabilization programme, interest rates were raised to extremely high levels to tighten [money](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_rouble "Russian rouble") and restrict [credit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Credit_(finance) "Credit (finance)"). To bring state spending and revenues into balance, Yeltsin raised new taxes heavily, cut back sharply on government subsidies to industry and construction, and made steep cuts to state welfare spending.

In early 1992, prices skyrocketed throughout Russia, and a deep credit crunch shut down many industries and brought about a protracted depression. The reforms devastated the living standards of much of the population, especially the groups dependent on Soviet-era state subsidies and welfare programs.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-Peter_Nolan_1995._pp._17-118) Through the 1990s, Russia's GDP fell by 50%, vast sectors of the economy were wiped out, inequality and unemployment grew dramatically, whilst incomes fell. [Hyperinflation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperinflation "Hyperinflation"), caused by the [Central Bank of Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Bank_of_Russia "Central Bank of Russia")'s loose monetary policy, wiped out many people's personal savings, and tens of millions of [Russians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russians "Russians") were plunged into poverty.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-119)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-120)

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/GDP_of_Russia_since_1989.svg/250px-GDP_of_Russia_since_1989.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GDP_of_Russia_since_1989.svg)

Most of Yeltsin's time as president was plagued by economic contraction.

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b0/Crude_oil_prices_since_1861.png/250px-Crude_oil_prices_since_1861.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Crude_oil_prices_since_1861.png)

Crude oil prices continued to fall during the 1990s, following the trend during the late 1980s.

Some economists argue that in the 1990s, Russia suffered an economic downturn more severe than the United States or [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weimar_Republic "Weimar Republic") had undergone six decades earlier in the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-Peter_Nolan_1995._pp._17-118) Russian commentators and even some Western economists, such as [Marshall Goldman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Goldman "Marshall Goldman"), widely blamed Yeltsin's economic programme for the country's disastrous economic performance in the 1990s. Many politicians began to quickly distance themselves from the programme. In February 1992, Russia's vice president, [Alexander Rutskoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Rutskoy "Alexander Rutskoy") denounced the Yeltsin programme as "economic genocide".[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bor

**Boris Nikolayevich Yeltsin**[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-8)[[i]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Yeltsin#cite_note-9) (1 February 1931 – 23 April 2007) was a Soviet and Russian politician who served as [President of Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Russia "President of Russia") from 1991 to 1999, having previously served as [Chairman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chairman_of_the_Supreme_Soviet_of_the_Russian_SFSR "Chairman of the Supreme Soviet of the Russian SFSR") of the [Supreme Soviet of the Russian SFSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_Russia "Supreme Soviet of Russia") from 1990 to 1991. He was a member of the [Communist Party of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Communist Party of the Soviet Union") (CPSU) from 1961 to 1990. He later stood as a [political independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_politician "Independent politician"), during which time he was viewed as being ideologically aligned with [liberalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism_in_Russia "Liberalism in Russia").

Yeltsin was born in [Butka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Butka,_Russia "Butka, Russia"), Ural Oblast. Growing up in [Kazan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazan "Kazan") and [Berezniki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berezniki "Berezniki"), he worked in construction after studying at the [Ural State Technical University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ural_State_Technical_University "Ural State Technical University"). After joining the Communist Party, he rose through its ranks, and in 1976, he became First Secretary of the party's [Sverdlovsk Oblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sverdlovsk_Oblast "Sverdlovsk Oblast") committee. Yeltsin was initially a supporter of the _[perestroika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perestroika "Perestroika")_ reforms of Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev. He later criticized the reforms as being too moderate and called for a transition to a [multi-party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multi-party_system "Multi-party system")[representative democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representative_democracy "Representative democracy"). In 1987, he was the first person to resign from the [Politburo of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politburo_of_the_Communist_Party_of_the_Soviet_Union "Politburo of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union"), which established his popularity as an anti-establishment figure and after which he earned the reputation of the leader of the [anti-communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communism "Anti-communism") movement.

Elected chair of the [Russian Supreme Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_Russia "Supreme Soviet of Russia") in 1990, Yeltsin was [elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Russian_presidential_election "1991 Russian presidential election") president of the [Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Soviet_Federative_Socialist_Republic "Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic") (RSFSR) in 1991, becoming the first popularly-elected head of state in Russian history. He allied with various non-Russian [nationalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalism "Nationalism") leaders and was instrumental in the formal [dissolution of the Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dissolution_of_the_Soviet_Union "Dissolution of the Soviet Union") in December of that year. With the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the RSFSR became the Russian Federation, an independent state. Through that transition, Yeltsin remained in office as president. He was later re-elected in the [1996 Russian presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Russian_presidential_election "1996 Russian presidential election"), which critics assert was rigged. Yeltsin oversaw [the transition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeltsin%E2%80%93Gaidar_government_reforms "Yeltsin–Gaidar government reforms") of Russia's [command economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_the_Soviet_Union "Economy of the Soviet Union") into a capitalist [market economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_economy "Market economy") by implementing [economic shock therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shock_therapy_(economics) "Shock therapy (economics)"), [market exchange rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exchange_rate "Exchange rate") of the [ruble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_ruble "Russian ruble"), [nationwide privatization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privatization_in_Russia "Privatization in Russia"), and lifting of [price controls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Price_controls "Price controls"). [Economic downturn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Russia "Economy of Russia"), volatility, and [inflation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflation "Inflation") ensued. Amid the economic shift, a small number of [oligarchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_oligarchs "Russian oligarchs") obtained most of the national property and wealth, while international monopolies dominated the market.

A [constitutional crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Russian_constitutional_crisis "1993 Russian constitutional crisis") emerged in 1993 after Yeltsin ordered the unconstitutional dissolution of the [Russian parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet_of_Russia "Supreme Soviet of Russia"), leading parliament to [impeach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_in_Russia "Impeachment in Russia") him. The crisis ended after troops loyal to Yeltsin stormed the [parliament building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_(Moscow) "White House (Moscow)") and stopped an armed uprising; he then introduced a [new constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Russia "Constitution of Russia") which significantly [expanded the powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_Russia "Politics of Russia") of the president. After the crisis, Yeltsin governed the country in a [rule by decree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_by_decree "Rule by decree") until 1994, as the [Supreme Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Soviet "Supreme Soviet") of Russia was absent. Secessionist sentiment in the [Russian Caucasus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Caucasian_Federal_District "North Caucasian Federal District") led to the [First Chechen War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Chechen_War "First Chechen War"), [War of Dagestan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_Dagestan "War of Dagestan"), and [Second Chechen War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Chechen_War "Second Chechen War") between 1994 and 1999. Internationally, Yeltsin promoted renewed collaboration with Europe and signed [arms control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arms_control "Arms control") agreements with the United States. Amid growing internal pressure, he resigned by the end of 1999 and was succeeded as president by his chosen successor, [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin"), whom he had appointed [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Russia "Prime Minister of Russia") a few months earlier. After leaving office, he kept a low profile and was accorded a [state funeral upon his death in 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Boris_Yeltsin "Death and state funeral of Boris Yeltsin").

Domestically, Yeltsin was highly popular in the late 1980s and early 1990s. However, his reputation was severely damaged by the economic and political crises of his presidency, and he left office widely unpopular with the Russian population. He has received praise and criticism for his role in dismantling the Soviet Union, transforming Russia into a representative democracy, and introducing new freedoms to the country. Conversely, he has been accused of economic mismanagement, abuse of presidential power, autocratic behavior, corruption, and of undermining Russia's standing as a major world power.
