Khrushchev (right) speaking at a victory rally of Red Army soldiers in Stalingrad, 4 February 1943

Soon after Stalingrad, Khrushchev met with personal tragedy, as his son [Leonid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Khrushchev "Leonid Khrushchev"), a [fighter pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_pilot "Fighter pilot"), was apparently shot down and killed in action on 11 March 1943. The circumstances of Leonid's death remain obscure and controversial,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2008-69) as none of his fellow fliers stated that they witnessed him being shot down, nor was his plane found or body recovered. One theory has Leonid surviving the crash and collaborating with the Germans, and when he was recaptured by the Soviets, Stalin ordering him shot despite Khrushchev pleading for his life.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2008-69) This supposed killing is used to explain why Khrushchev later denounced Stalin.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2008-69)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003157%E2%80%93158-70) While there is no supporting evidence for this account in Soviet files, some historians allege that Leonid Khrushchev's file was tampered with after the war.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199582-71) In later years, Leonid Khrushchev's wingmate stated that he saw his plane disintegrate, but did not report it. Khrushchev biographer Taubman speculates that this omission was most likely to avoid the possibility of being seen as complicit in the death of the son of a Politburo member.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003158-72) In mid-1943, Leonid's wife, Liuba Khrushcheva, was arrested on accusations of spying and sentenced to five years in a labor camp, and her son (by another relationship), Tolya, was placed in orphanages. Leonid's daughter, Yulia, was raised by Nikita Khrushchev and his wife.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003158%E2%80%93162-73)

After _Uranus_ forced the Germans into retreat, Khrushchev served on other fronts of the war. He was attached to Soviet troops at the [Battle of Kursk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kursk "Battle of Kursk"), in July 1943, which turned back the last major German offensive on Soviet soil.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003171%E2%80%93172-74) Khrushchev related that he interrogated an [SS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS "SS") defector, learning that the Germans intended an attack—a claim dismissed by his biographer Taubman as "almost certainly exaggerated".[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003177%E2%80%93178-75) He accompanied Soviet troops as they took Kiev in November 1943, entering the shattered city as Soviet forces drove out German troops.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003177%E2%80%93178-75) As Soviet forces met with greater success, driving the Nazis westwards towards Germany, Nikita Khrushchev became increasingly involved in reconstruction work in Ukraine. He was appointed Premier of the Ukrainian SSR in addition to his earlier party post, one of the rare instances in which the Ukrainian party and civil leader posts were held by one person.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199581%E2%80%9382-76)

According to Khrushchev biographer William Tompson, it is difficult to assess Khrushchev's war record, since he most often acted as part of a military council, and it is not possible to know the extent to which he influenced decisions. However, Tompson points to the fact that the few mentions of Khrushchev in military memoirs published during the [Brezhnev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Brezhnev "Leonid Brezhnev") era were generally favorable, at a time when it was "barely possible to mention Khrushchev in print in any context".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199573-77) Tompson suggests that these favorable mentions indicate that military officers held Khrushchev in high regard.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199573-77)

## Rise to power

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nikita_Khrushchev&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Rise to power")]

### Return to Ukraine

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nikita_Khrushchev&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Return to Ukraine")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg/500px-Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ruined_Kiev_in_WWII.jpg)

The Ukrainian capital, [Kiev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiev "Kiev"), after the Second World War

Almost all of Ukraine had been occupied by the Germans, and Khrushchev returned to his domain in late 1943 to find devastation. Ukraine's industry had been destroyed, and agriculture faced critical shortages. Even though millions of Ukrainians had been taken to Germany as workers or prisoners of war, there was insufficient housing for those who remained.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199586-78) One out of every six Ukrainians were killed in World War II.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003179-79)

Khrushchev sought to reconstruct Ukraine and complete the interrupted work of imposing the Soviet system on it, though he hoped that the purges of the 1930s would not recur.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003180-80) As Ukraine was recovered militarily, [conscription](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription "Conscription") was imposed; 750,000 men aged between nineteen and fifty were sent to join the Red Army.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003181-81) Other Ukrainians joined partisan forces, seeking an independent Ukraine.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003181-81) Khrushchev rushed from district to district through Ukraine, urging the depleted labor force to greater efforts. He made a short visit to his birthplace of Kalinovka, finding a starving population, with only a third of the men who had joined the Red Army having returned. Khrushchev did what he could to assist his hometown.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003193%E2%80%93195-82) Despite Khrushchev's efforts, in 1945, Ukrainian industry was at only a quarter of pre-war levels, and the harvest actually dropped from that of 1944, when the entire territory of Ukraine had not yet been retaken.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199586-78)

In an effort to increase agricultural production, the _[kolkhozes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkhoz "Kolkhoz")_ (collective farms) were empowered to expel residents who were not pulling their weight. _Kolkhoz_ leaders used this as an excuse to expel their personal enemies, invalids, and the elderly, sending them to the eastern parts of the Soviet Union. Khrushchev viewed this policy as very effective and recommended its adoption elsewhere to Stalin.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199586-78) He also worked to impose [collectivization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collectivization_in_the_Soviet_Union "Collectivization in the Soviet Union") on Western Ukraine. Lack of resources and armed resistance by partisans slowed the process.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199587%E2%80%9388-83) The partisans, many of whom fought as the [Ukrainian Insurgent Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Insurgent_Army "Ukrainian Insurgent Army") (UPA), were gradually defeated, as Soviet police and military reported killing 110,825 "bandits" and capturing a quarter million more between 1944 and 1946.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003195-84) About 600,000 Western Ukrainians were arrested between 1944 and 1952, with one-third executed and the remainder imprisoned or exiled to the east.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003195-84)

The war years of 1944 and 1945 had seen poor harvests, and 1946 saw intense drought strike Ukraine and Western Russia. Despite this, collective and state farms were required to turn over 52% of the harvest to the government.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199591-85) The [Soviet government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_government "Soviet government") sought to collect as much grain as possible to supply communist allies in Eastern Europe.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003199-86) Khrushchev set the quotas at a high level, leading Stalin to expect an unrealistically large quantity of grain from Ukraine.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003199%E2%80%93200-87) Food was rationed—but non-agricultural rural workers throughout the USSR were given no ration cards. The inevitable starvation was largely confined to remote rural regions and was little noticed outside the USSR.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199591-85) Khrushchev, realizing the desperate situation in late 1946, repeatedly appealed to Stalin for aid, to be met with anger and resistance. When letters to Stalin had no effect, Khrushchev flew to Moscow and made his case in person. Stalin finally gave Ukraine limited food aid, and money to set up free [soup kitchens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soup_kitchen "Soup kitchen").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003200%E2%80%93201-88) However, Khrushchev's political standing had been damaged, and in February 1947, Stalin suggested that Lazar Kaganovich be sent to Ukraine to "help" Khrushchev.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199592-89) The following month, the Ukrainian Central Committee removed Khrushchev as party leader in favor of Kaganovich, while retaining him as premier.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003203-90)

Soon after Kaganovich arrived in Kiev, Khrushchev fell ill and was barely seen until September 1947. In his memoirs, Khrushchev indicates he had pneumonia; some biographers have theorized that Khrushchev's illness was entirely political, out of fear that his loss of position was the first step towards downfall and demise.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199593-91) However, Khrushchev's children remembered their father as having been seriously ill. Once Khrushchev was able to get out of bed, he and his family took their first vacation since before the war, to a beachfront resort in [Latvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvia "Latvia").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003203-90) Khrushchev, though, soon broke the beach routine with duck-hunting trips, and a visit to the new Soviet [Kaliningrad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaliningrad "Kaliningrad"), where he toured factories and quarries.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKhrushchev200027-92) By the end of 1947, Kaganovich had been recalled to Moscow and the recovered Khrushchev had been restored to the First Secretaryship. He then resigned the Ukrainian premiership in favor of [Demyan Korotchenko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demyan_Korotchenko "Demyan Korotchenko"), Khrushchev's protégé.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199593-91)

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Nikita_Khrushchev_TASS_Portrait_Trim_Edit.jpg/250px-Nikita_Khrushchev_TASS_Portrait_Trim_Edit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nikita_Khrushchev_TASS_Portrait_Trim_Edit.jpg)

Khrushchev c. 1948

Khrushchev's final years in Ukraine were generally peaceful, with industry recovering,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199595-93) Soviet forces overcoming the partisans, and 1947 and 1948 seeing better-than-expected harvests.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003205-94) Collectivization advanced in Western Ukraine, and Khrushchev implemented more policies that encouraged collectivization and discouraged private farms. These sometimes backfired, however: a tax on private livestock holdings led to peasants slaughtering their stock.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199596-95) With the idea of eliminating differences in attitude between town and countryside and transforming the peasantry into a "rural proletariat", Khrushchev conceived the idea of the "[agro-town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agro-town "Agro-town")".[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199596%E2%80%9397-96) Rather than agricultural workers living close to farms, they would live further away in larger towns which would offer municipal services such as utilities and libraries. He completed only one such town before his December 1949 return to Moscow; he dedicated it to Stalin as a 70th birthday present.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199596%E2%80%9397-96)

In his memoirs, Khrushchev spoke highly of Ukraine:

> I'll say that the Ukrainian people treated me well. I recall warmly the years I spent there. This was a period full of responsibilities, but pleasant because it brought satisfaction... But far be it from me to inflate my significance. The entire Ukrainian people was exerting great efforts... I attribute Ukraine's successes to the Ukrainian people as a whole. I won't elaborate further on this theme, but in principle, it's very easy to demonstrate. I'm Russian myself, and I don't want to offend the Russians.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKhrushchev200616%E2%80%9317-97)

### Stalin's final years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Nikita_Khrushchev&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Stalin's final years")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4b/Mao%2C_Bulganin%2C_Stalin%2C_Ulbricht_Tsedenbal.jpeg/500px-Mao%2C_Bulganin%2C_Stalin%2C_Ulbricht_Tsedenbal.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mao,_Bulganin,_Stalin,_Ulbricht_Tsedenbal.jpeg)

Joseph Stalin (third from right) presiding over a ceremony commemorating his 71st birthday a few years before his death.

From mid-December 1949, Khrushchev served as head of the Party in Moscow city and province. His biographer Taubman suggests that Stalin most likely recalled Khrushchev to Moscow to balance the influence of [Georgy Malenkov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgy_Malenkov "Georgy Malenkov") and security chief [Lavrentiy Beria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lavrentiy_Beria "Lavrentiy Beria"), who were widely seen as Stalin's heirs.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2003210-98) The aging leader rarely called Politburo meetings. Instead, much of the high-level work of government took place at dinners hosted by Stalin for his inner circle of Beria, Malenkov, Khrushchev, Kaganovich, [Kliment Voroshilov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kliment_Voroshilov "Kliment Voroshilov"), [Vyacheslav Molotov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyacheslav_Molotov "Vyacheslav Molotov"), and [Nikolai Bulganin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolai_Bulganin "Nikolai Bulganin"). Khrushchev took early naps so that he would not fall asleep in Stalin's presence; he noted in his memoirs, "Things went badly for those who dozed off at Stalin's table."[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKhrushchev200643-99)

In 1950, Khrushchev began a large-scale housing program for Moscow. Five- or six-story apartment buildings became ubiquitous throughout the Soviet Union.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETompson199599-100) Khrushchev had prefabricated reinforced concrete used, greatly speeding up construction.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaubman2

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986

This article is about the 10th president of the Philippines. For his son, the 17th president, see [Bongbong Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos "Bongbong Marcos"). For other uses, see [Ferdinand Marcos (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos_(disambiguation) "Ferdinand Marcos (disambiguation)").

In this [Filipino name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_name "Filipino name"), the [middle name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_name "Middle name") or maternal [family name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surname "Surname") is _Edralin_ and the surname or paternal family name is _Marcos_.

**Ferdinand Emmanuel Edralin Marcos Sr.**[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-8) (September 11, 1917 – September 28, 1989) was a Filipino lawyer and politician who served as the tenth [president of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines") from 1965 to 1986. From 1972 to 1981, Marcos ruled the Philippines [under martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law_under_Ferdinand_Marcos "Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos"), embracing a policy of "[constitutional authoritarianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos's_cult_of_personality "Ferdinand Marcos's cult of personality")." Following the lifting of martial law in 1981, a wide-ranging economic crisis, and the [assassination of Ninoy Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Ninoy_Aquino "Assassination of Ninoy Aquino"), Marcos was deposed in 1986 by the [People Power Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_Revolution "People Power Revolution") and was succeeded as president by Aquino's widow, [Corazon Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corazon_Aquino "Corazon Aquino"). He was also the father of [Bongbong Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos "Bongbong Marcos"), the incumbent president of the Philippines since 2022.

Marcos was born in [Ilocos Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte "Ilocos Norte") in 1917. His father, [Mariano Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariano_Marcos "Mariano Marcos"), was a lawyer and politician who was later executed by guerillas for [collaboration with the Japanese Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collaboration_with_the_Empire_of_Japan "Collaboration with the Empire of Japan") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). In 1940, Marcos and his father were convicted of assassinating a political rival, [Julio Nalundasan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Nalundasan "Julio Nalundasan"), but the conviction was overturned on appeal. Marcos joined the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army") after the [attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") in 1941 and fought the Japanese, who held him as a [prisoner of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_of_war "Prisoner of war") in 1942. After the war, he practiced law and was elected to represent Ilocos Norte in the [Philippines House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Representatives_of_the_Philippines "House of Representatives of the Philippines") from 1949 to 1959. He was elected to the [Senate of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_of_the_Philippines "Senate of the Philippines") from 1959 to 1965, and served as Senate president from 1963 to 1965. He advanced his political career by exaggerating his military record, fraudulently including claims that he was "the most decorated war hero in the Philippines."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-9)

[In 1965](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Philippine_presidential_election "1965 Philippine presidential election"), Marcos was elected to his first term as president; he was [re-elected in 1969](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Philippine_presidential_election "1969 Philippine presidential election"). His initial policies included massive infrastructure development and construction, which made him popular but were funded by [foreign lending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_debt "External debt").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-10) During his second term, debt and inflation crises and growing Philippine involvement in the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") triggered domestic social unrest.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Balbosas1992-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Cororaton1997-12) In 1972, Marcos declared [martial law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial_law "Martial law"), ruling the country as a dictator until 1981.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-govPhDeclarationMartialLaw-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-fmDeclaresSundayExpress-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-lacsamana1990p189-15) His rule was ratified through a [1973 plebiscite administered and overseen by the military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_Philippine_constitutional_plebiscite "1973 Philippine constitutional plebiscite").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-philippinesReadr-16) During this period, the constitution was revised to empower Marcos, and media outlets and opposition politicians were silenced. The Marcos regime used violence to suppress political opposition, including Muslims and suspected communists, whom he declared a threat to the Philippines.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-17) He referred to his ideology during this period as the "movement for a new society" and founded the political party [Kilusang Bagong Lipunan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilusang_Bagong_Lipunan "Kilusang Bagong Lipunan") to advance his ideas.

After the formal end of martial law in 1981, Marcos was [elected to a third term](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Philippine_presidential_election_and_referendum "1981 Philippine presidential election and referendum"). His popularity suffered in 1983, however, due to [an economic collapse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_history_of_the_Philippines_(1965%E2%80%931986)#Economic_nosedive_and_Marcos_ouster_(1981%E2%80%931986) "Economic history of the Philippines (1965–1986)") and the [assassination of Ninoy Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Ninoy_Aquino "Assassination of Ninoy Aquino"), leader-in-exile of the opposition. Disapproval manifested in the resurgence of the political opposition in the [1984 parliamentary elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Philippine_parliamentary_election "1984 Philippine parliamentary election"). Subsequent investigative reporting on his family's extensive overseas financial holdings[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-18) and false war records led Marcos to call [snap elections in 1986](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986_Philippine_presidential_election "1986 Philippine presidential election"). He was challenged by Aquino's widow, [Corazon Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corazon_Aquino "Corazon Aquino"). Although official results declared Marcos the victor, allegations of mass [electoral fraud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electoral_fraud "Electoral fraud"),[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-19) political turmoil, and [human rights abuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_abuses_of_the_Marcos_dictatorship "Human rights abuses of the Marcos dictatorship") led to the [People Power Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_Power_Revolution "People Power Revolution") of February 1986,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-20) which ultimately removed him from power after two decades.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-21) On advice from United States president Ronald Reagan, the Marcos family fled to Hawaii, where he died in 1989.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-22)

Marcos, who was viewed as a dictator,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Times_Books-23)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-24)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosRiseAndFallDictator-25) remains a controversial figure in the Philippines, with his period of rule widely condemned as a kleptocracy[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosKleptocracy22-26)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-RegimeOfMarcoses22-27)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-28) and infamous for corruption, extravagance, and brutality.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Times_Books-23)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-29) His wife, [Imelda Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imelda_Marcos "Imelda Marcos"), became infamous in her own right for the excesses that characterized their "[conjugal dictatorship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Conjugal_Dictatorship_of_Ferdinand_and_Imelda_Marcos "The Conjugal Dictatorship of Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos")", coining the term _[Imeldific](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Imeldific#English "wikt:Imeldific")_,[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-30) and the family allegedly stole as much as $10 billion from the [Central Bank of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangko_Sentral_ng_Pilipinas "Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas") during his rule.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosKleptocracy22-26)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-RegimeOfMarcoses22-27)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosRiseAndFallDictator-25)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-hartfordMcCoy-31)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-32) Despite his removal from office and death in exile, many members of the Marcos regime remained in politics, including [Fidel Ramos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Ramos "Fidel Ramos"), who succeeded Aquino as president in 1992.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-mccoy-33) His children, [Imee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imee_Marcos "Imee Marcos") and [Bongbong Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos "Bongbong Marcos"), remain active in Philippine politics, with Bongbong [serving as president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Bongbong_Marcos "Presidency of Bongbong Marcos") since 2022. They have denied accusations of human rights violations by their parents.

Further information: [Marcos family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marcos_family "Marcos family")

Ferdinand Emmanuel Edralin Marcos was born in [Sarrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarrat "Sarrat"), [Ilocos Norte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte "Ilocos Norte"), on September 11, 1917. His father, [Mariano Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariano_Marcos "Mariano Marcos") (1897–1945), was a lawyer who represented Ilocos Norte in the House of Representatives of the Philippines from 1925 to 1931.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-34) His mother, Josefa Edralin Marcos (1893–1988), was a schoolteacher.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Steinberg2000pp115-116-35) Marcos was of [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangley "Sangley")[mestizo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_Mestizos "Filipino Mestizos") descendant.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:02-36) He later claimed to be descended from revolutionary hero [Antonio Luna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Luna "Antonio Luna"), a claim since debunked by genealogist Mona Magno-Veluz.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-A.R._Ocampo_2010-37)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-BaguioChronicle2022-38) Marcos also claimed descent from [Limahong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limahong "Limahong") (Chinese: 林阿鳳), a 16th-century pirate who used to raid the coasts of the [South China Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_China_Sea "South China Sea").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-39)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-mijares255-40)

### Education

From 1923 to 1929, Marcos attended Sarrat Elementary School, Shamrock Elementary School (in [Laoag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laoag "Laoag")), and Ermita Elementary School (in Manila). He received his secondary education at University of the Philippines High School and attended [University of the Philippines Manila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Philippines_Manila "University of the Philippines Manila"), studying liberal arts before studying law at [University of the Philippines College of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Philippines_College_of_Law "University of the Philippines College of Law").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-41) At the College of Law, he joined [Upsilon Sigma Phi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upsilon_Sigma_Phi "Upsilon Sigma Phi"), where he first met many of his future colleagues and critics. He excelled in his studies and in extracurricular activities, joining the university's swimming, boxing, wrestling, and rifle teams. He was a national rifle champion and an accomplished [orator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_speaking "Public speaking"), debater, and writer for the student newspaper.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-42)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_][[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-43)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_] Marcos served as a battalion commander in the [Reserve Officers' Training Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserve_Officers'_Training_Corps "Reserve Officers' Training Corps") (ROTC) and was commissioned as a third lieutenant in the Philippine Constabulary Reserve.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosOvercameMurder-44)

In 1939, Marcos took the [bar exam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Bar_Examinations "Philippine Bar Examinations"); he was a top scorer with a score of 92.35 percent and graduated _[cum laude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cum\_laude "Cum laude")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-veraFilesMarcosBarExams-45)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-46)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-47) He was elected to the [Pi Gamma Mu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pi_Gamma_Mu "Pi Gamma Mu") and the [Phi Kappa Phi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Kappa_Phi "Phi Kappa Phi") international [honor societies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honour_society "Honour society").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-48) Marcos received an honorary Doctor of Laws (LL.D.) (_[honoris causa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honorary\_degree "Honorary degree")_) degree in 1967 from [Central Philippine University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Philippine_University "Central Philippine University").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Honorary_Degree_Recipients_from_1905-1980s_-_Central_Philippine_University-49)

### Assassination of Julio Nalundasan

Main article: [Julio Nalundasan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Nalundasan "Julio Nalundasan")

In 1934, Mariano Marcos lost his campaign for re-election to the House of Representatives to [Julio Nalundasan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Nalundasan "Julio Nalundasan"). Mariano Marcos challenged Nalundasan again in the 1935 election but was defeated. On the day after the election, September 21, 1935, Nalundasan was killed by a single rifle shot at his home in [Batac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batac "Batac").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-conjugalAteneo-50) In December 1938, two witnesses accused Ferdinand Marcos, Mariano, and Ferdinand's uncles Pio Marcos and Quirino Lizardo of conspiring to assassinate Nalundasan.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-mijares237-51)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-52) At the time, Ferdinand was still studying law and a national champion as a member of the university rifle team.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosOvercameMurder-44) On the night of the assassination, Ferdinand's rifle was in its rack in the ROTC armory. However, the rifle of team captain [Teodoro Kalaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teodoro_Kalaw#Personal_life "Teodoro Kalaw") was missing, and Ferdinand had access to the armory. A [National Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bureau_of_Investigation_(Philippines) "National Bureau of Investigation (Philippines)") concluded that Kalaw's rifle was the murder weapon.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-conjugalAteneo-50) Ferdinand and his uncle Quirino were convicted of murder, and Ferdinand was sentenced to 10 to 17 years in prison.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-53)

He appealed his conviction to the [Supreme Court of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_Philippines "Supreme Court of the Philippines").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-54) The Supreme Court overturned the lower court's decision on October 22, 1940, acquitting both men of all charges except [contempt of court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contempt_of_court "Contempt of court").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-55)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-puppetPresident-56) Justice [Jose P. Laurel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_P._Laurel "Jose P. Laurel"), who wrote the majority decision, persuaded his colleagues to acquit Marcos. Laurel himself had been convicted of frustrated murder as a young man after he almost killed a rival during a youthful brawl but was acquitted after his own appeal to the Supreme Court.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-conjugalAteneo-50)

## Military service and early political career

### World War II

Main article: [Military career of Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_career_of_Ferdinand_Marcos "Military career of Ferdinand Marcos")

Marcos's military service record, and his alleged exaggeration of it, have been the source of controversy and confusion.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Philstar_-_Imagined_Heroism-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-SubSelfie_-_Truth_or_Dare-58) Near the end of his presidency, researchers found that most stories about Marcos's military service were inaccurate or untrue.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-59)

Following the [attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") and [Japanese invasion of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_campaign_(1941%E2%80%931942) "Philippines campaign (1941–1942)") in December 1941, Marcos was called into service in the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army"). He fought with the United States until April 1942, when he was taken prisoner by the Japanese at the [Battle of Bataan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Bataan "Battle of Bataan"). Official Army records show that he was assigned to the intelligence service in the [21st Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/21st_Division_(Philippines) "21st Division (Philippines)") under [Mateo M. Capinpin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mateo_M._Capinpin "Mateo M. Capinpin").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Philstar_-_Imagined_Heroism-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-SubSelfie_-_Truth_or_Dare-58)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-TheWashPost-60) Despite his later claims of heroism at the battle, there are no contemporaneous records of any awards or decorations received by Marcos, and his commander and other officers did not corroborate his claims. However, official dispatches reference Marcos bringing a wounded officer to the rear and note that the 21st Infantry Division did not receive sufficient recognition for their actions at Bataan.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-WP_-_Dec_18,_1983-61)

After surrendering, Marcos survived the [Bataan Death March](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bataan_Death_March "Bataan Death March").[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMijares1976246%E2%80%93254-62) According to Marcos's own account, he was released by the Japanese on August 4, 1942. This claim later became controversial when it was cited as evidence that Marcos's father had served as a [Japanese collaborator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collaboration_with_the_Empire_of_Japan "Collaboration with the Empire of Japan"), as the Japanese only released prisoners who had severe health problems or whose families had cooperated with Japanese authorities.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-JohnSharkey198601243-63)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-TheWashPost2-64)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMijares1976246%E2%80%93254-62) In 1945, his father was executed by Filipino guerillas by [drawing and quartering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanged,_drawn_and_quartered "Hanged, drawn and quartered") using [carabaos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carabao "Carabao"). His remains were left hanging on a tree.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-JohnSharkey19860124-65)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-66)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-LaphamsRaiders-67) At least one contemporary Japanese official recorded Ferdinand himself as a Japanese propagandist.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-WP_24_Jan_1986-68)

After his release, Marcos claimed to have led a guerrilla force of nine thousand in northern Luzon; these claims have been contradicted and ruled criminal by the United States Army investigators.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-whScottPrehispanic-69)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-McCoy1999-70) According to [Primitivo Mijares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primitivo_Mijares "Primitivo Mijares"), Marcos also filed a fraudulent war reparations claim for millions of dollars in cattle.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-71) Military records show that Marcos rejoined U.S. forces in December 1944 until his discharge with the [rank of major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_(rank) "Major (rank)") in May 1945.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-JohnSharkey198601243-63)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Curtis1948-72)

### Political rise (1949–1965)

After World War II, the Philippines gained political independence from the United States on July 4, 1946.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Wood1986-73)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Dubsky1993-74) Marcos was appointed as one of eleven special prosecutors, tasked to prosecute those accused of collaboration with the Japanese.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-75) Leveraging this appointment and his exaggerated war record, Marcos eventually entered politics as a member of the new [Liberal Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberal_Party_(Philippines) "Liberal Party (Philippines)"). In 1949, Marcos ran for his father's former seat in [Ilocos Norte's 2nd congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilocos_Norte's_2nd_congressional_district "Ilocos Norte's 2nd congressional district"). He won and was re-elected to the House of Representatives twice, serving until 1959.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Ferdinand_Edralin_Marcos-76)

The Liberal Party had split from the [Nacionalista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacionalista_Party "Nacionalista Party") in 1946. Marcos later became the party's economic spokesman and chaired the House Committee on Commerce and Industry. He also served on the committees on Defense, Ways and Means; Industry; Banks Currency; War Veterans; Civil Service; and Corporations and Economic Planning. He was also a member of the Special Committee on Import and Price Controls, the Special Committee on Reparations, and the House Electoral Tribunal.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Ferdinand_Edralin_Marcos-76)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

After serving three terms in the House, Marcos was elected to the Senate [in 1959](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1959_Philippine_Senate_election "1959 Philippine Senate election"). He became minority floor leader in the Senate in 1960 and served as party president from 1961 to 1964. From 1963 to 1965, he was [Senate President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_President_of_the_Philippines "Senate President of the Philippines"). He introduced significant bills, many of which were enacted.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Ferdinand_Edralin_Marcos-76)[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_] During his 1962 campaign, Marcos claimed to be the most decorated Filipino veteran of World War II, having garnered almost every medal and decoration awarded by the American or Philippine government, including the Distinguished Service Cross and Medal of Honor.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-mijares246-77)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-chicagoTribune1-78) The Liberal Party later confirmed that many of the medals were awarded to Marcos in 1962 to aid in his Senate election campaign.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMijares1976-79)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_][[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-80)

### First term (1965–1969)

Main article: [First term of the presidency of Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_term_of_the_presidency_of_Ferdinand_Marcos "First term of the presidency of Ferdinand Marcos")

Further information: [List of cabinets of the Philippines §Ferdinand Marcos (1965–1986)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cabinets_of_the_Philippines#Ferdinand_Marcos_(1965%E2%80%931986) "List of cabinets of the Philippines")

#### 1965 presidential campaign

Main article: [1965 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1965_Philippine_presidential_election "1965 Philippine presidential election")

In 1965, Marcos expected incumbent president [Diosdado Macapagal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diosdado_Macapagal "Diosdado Macapagal") to step aside and support his campaign for president. Marcos had managed Macapagal's 1961 campaign in exchange for Macapagal's support in 1965. Stung by Macapagal's broken promise, Marcos left the Liberal Party to join the [Nacionalista Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nacionalista_Party "Nacionalista Party") and run for president on a populist platform.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:11-81) With the support of Faustino del Mundo, leader of the [Hukbalahap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hukbalahap "Hukbalahap") guerrilla remnants and organized crime in [Pampanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pampanga "Pampanga") and southern [Tarlac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarlac "Tarlac"), Marcos was able to mobilize resources and utilize coercive violence to win [Central Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Luzon "Central Luzon"), which was crucial to the election.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:11-81) On October 13, 1965, at least one person was killed and five wounded in a clash between gangs supporting Macapagal and Marcos.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:11-81)

Marcos won the election and was [inaugurated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_inauguration_of_Ferdinand_Marcos "First inauguration of Ferdinand Marcos") as the [10th](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_presidents_of_the_Philippines "List of presidents of the Philippines")[president of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Philippines "President of the Philippines") on December 30, 1965.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82)

#### Domestic infrastructure and education policies

Main article: [Edifice complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edifice_complex "Edifice complex")

As president, Marcos launched an aggressive program of infrastructure development funded by foreign loans. From 1966 to 1970, Marcos increased infrastructure spending in the Philippines by 70 percent, and as of 2011, Marcos had spent more annually on infrastructure than any other president of the Philippines.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82):128[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-83) Major projects included the construction of the [Cultural Center of the Philippines complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Center_of_the_Philippines_complex "Cultural Center of the Philippines complex"). Critics have referred to the Marcos policy of major construction and infrastructure building to curry public support as an "[edifice complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edifice_complex "Edifice complex")."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-84)

Projects completed during Marcos's rule from 1965 to 1986 included major healthcare infrastructure, including the leading centers for heart, lung, and kidney care in the Philippines, and transportation infrastructure, including the [Marcos Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juanico_Bridge "San Juanico Bridge") between [Leyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyte "Leyte") and [Samar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samar "Samar"), the [Pan-Philippine Highway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Philippine_Highway "Pan-Philippine Highway"), and the [Manila Light Rail Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Light_Rail_Transit_System "Manila Light Rail Transit System").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-85)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:6-86) These projects were typically constructed on a rush basis, often compromising their structural safety.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch12-87):169[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:4-88) Marcos also emphasized educational infrastructure, including public school buildings and roads to connect communities to them, during his first presidential term.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82):128 Ultimately, forty-seven colleges and universities were established during Marcos's term in office from 1965 to 1986.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-89)

Spending during his first term outpaced tax revenues, but Marcos continued to promise "rice, roads, and school buildings" as the cornerstone of his 1969 re-election campaign. Marcos covered the gap with foreign lending, leading to a 72 percent increase in the budget deficit over Macapagal's term in office. Although he remained popular for most of his first term,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Balbosas1992-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Cororaton1997-12)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82) these policies created long-term economic instability and required that Marcos rely on foreign support to preserve his rule.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-theMarcosDebt-90)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-theEdificeComplex-91)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-gma7edifice-92)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Romero2008-93):89

Marcos also used construction projects to advance the political and public profile of his wife, [Imelda Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imelda_Marcos "Imelda Marcos").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch12-87):169 In 1966, he announced the [Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Center_of_the_Philippines_Complex "Cultural Center of the Philippines Complex") by executive order, with Imelda serving as its chair.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-94)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:3-95) Other cultural and heritage cites constructed by Marcos included the [Nayong Pilipino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nayong_Pilipino_Cultural_Park_and_Creative_Hub "Nayong Pilipino Cultural Park and Creative Hub"), [the Philippine International Convention Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_International_Convention_Center "Philippine International Convention Center"), and the [Manila Film Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manila_Film_Center "Manila Film Center"). By 1977–1980, projects in the "conspicuous capital outlays" category had ballooned to account for 20 percent of the Philippines' capital outlays.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Romero2008-93):"88–89"

#### Vietnam War, foreign policy, and militarism

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/The_Marcoses_and_the_Johnsons_dancing.jpg/330px-The_Marcoses_and_the_Johnsons_dancing.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Marcoses_and_the_Johnsons_dancing.jpg)

Marcos (pictured here with [Lady Bird Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Bird_Johnson "Lady Bird Johnson"), his wife Imelda, and [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson")) maintained strong relations with the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") during the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War").

As president, Marcos pursued a close relationship with the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), protecting and maintaining U.S. military bases in the Philippines as part of the ongoing [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") conflict. Marcos relied on the relationship to sustain his regime.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:10-96) Marcos also leveraged U.S. interests to advance his political career; for example, Marcos threatened to search every visiting American naval vessel during his 1969 presidential campaign. However, Marcos secretly assured the United States that he had no desire for American withdrawal; in response, the United States injected millions into the Philippine government's banking system, boosting his popularity and re-election campaign.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-97) Marcos repeatedly took public stands critical of United States influence, leveraging the implied threat to secure increased aid.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:12-98)

Under pressure from the [Lyndon B. Johnson administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Lyndon_B._Johnson "Presidency of Lyndon B. Johnson") in the 1960s, Marcos reversed his prior position by permitting Philippine involvement in the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") in the form of the [Philippine Civic Action Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Civic_Action_Group "Philippine Civic Action Group") (PHILCAG), a [combat engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_engineer "Combat engineer") unit, despite some opposition within the [Philippine Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_the_Philippines "Congress of the Philippines").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-McMahon1999-99)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-showingflag-100)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-agoncillo508-101) PHILCAG were involved from the middle of 1966, growing to a strength of 1,600 troops by 1968. Between 1966 and 1970, over 10,000 Filipino soldiers served in Vietnam, mainly involved in civilian infrastructure projects.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Celoza1997-102):[102–103](https://books.google.com/books?id=Sp3U1oCNKlgC)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-103) Marcos secretly assured the US he had no desire for an American withdrawal. He had received warnings from the Philippine embassy that US aid was at risk in Congress. Marcos returned to the implied threats. In one speech, he stated that the bases were a threat to regional peace and security while reminding the US of its "solemn obligation" to continue aid.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:12-98) In late 1976, the US offered $1 billion of mixed grants and loans to the Philippines, but Marcos rejected the offer.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-104)

Despite his alignment with the United States, Marcos also pursued informal alignment with the Soviet Union within the [Sino-Soviet split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sino-Soviet_split "Sino-Soviet split"). The [Partido Komunista ng Pilipinas-1930](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partido_Komunista_ng_Pilipinas-1930 "Partido Komunista ng Pilipinas-1930") (PKP-1930), which had supported his 1965 election and was Soviet-aligned, was challenged by the [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines"), which was Maoist, in 1968. Although PKP-1930 was officially illegal, Marcos appointed some members to positions within his government as salaried researchers, and they were then used as an informal channel of negotiation with the Soviet Union and the [Eastern Bloc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Bloc "Eastern Bloc").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:16-105)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:17-106)

Despite his general anticommunism and opposition to the [People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") under [Mao Zedong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong"), Marcos softened his tone in 1969, publicly asserting the need for the Philippines to establish a diplomatic relationship with the People's Republic of China.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-107) In his January 1969 State of the Nation Address, he said,[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-108)

> We, in Asia must strive toward a modus vivendi with Red China. I reiterate this need, which is becoming more urgent each day. Before long, Communist China will have increased its striking power a thousand fold with a sophisticated delivery system for its nuclear weapons. We must prepare for that day. We must prepare to coexist peaceably with Communist China.[_[undue weight?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Neutral\_point\_of\_view#Due\_and\_undue\_weight "Wikipedia:Neutral point of view")–[discuss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Ferdinand\_Marcos#undue "Talk:Ferdinand Marcos")_]

During his first term, Marcos developed close relationships with Philippine military officers and significantly expanded the armed forces by allowing loyal generals to remain in their positions past their age of retirement. Loyal officers who did retire were granted positions in his government. He also significantly expanded the military budget, utilizing military personnel for civic projects such as school construction. In an unprecedented move, Marcos chose to concurrently serve as his own [defense secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_National_Defense_(Philippines) "Department of National Defense (Philippines)"), giving him direct control over the military. In 1968, Senator [Ninoy Aquino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ninoy_Aquino "Ninoy Aquino") accused Marcos of trying to establish a "[garrison state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Garrison_State "The Garrison State")."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-GovPh29thNinoyAnniv-109)

#### Jabidah massacre and Moro conflict

Main articles: [Jabidah massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jabidah_massacre "Jabidah massacre") and [Moro conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_conflict "Moro conflict")

In March 1968, Jibin Arula testified that he had been the lone survivor of a group of [Moro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_people "Moro people") army recruits that had been executed _en masse_ on [Corregidor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corregidor "Corregidor") by the [Armed Forces of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_the_Philippines "Armed Forces of the Philippines") on March 18, 1968, which came to be known as the [Jabidah massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jabidah_massacre "Jabidah massacre").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Rappler-110)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-George1980-111) Arula's allegations were the subject of a critical exposé by Ninoy Aquino and became a major catalyst of the [Moro insurgency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_insurgency_in_the_Philippines "Moro insurgency in the Philippines").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-George1980-111)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-sfof-112)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-113) When none of the officers implicated in the massacre were convicted, many [Filipino Muslims](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam_in_the_Philippines "Islam in the Philippines"), especially intellectuals and educated youth, were enraged. They came to believe that the Manila government had little regard for their safety or interests, and efforts at integration and accommodation were abandoned.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-George1980-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Larousse2001-114)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Majul1985-115)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-MuslimPresident1994-116)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_][[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Smith2015-117) Dissent led to the formation of the [Muslim Independence Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslim_Independence_Movement "Muslim Independence Movement") in 1968, which later consolidated with the Bangsamoro Liberation Organization to form the [Moro National Liberation Front](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moro_National_Liberation_Front "Moro National Liberation Front") in October 1972.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-BetweenIntegrationandSecession-118)

### Second term (1969–1972)

Main article: [Second term of the presidency of Ferdinand Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_term_of_the_presidency_of_Ferdinand_Marcos "Second term of the presidency of Ferdinand Marcos")

See also: [1969 Philippine presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Philippine_presidential_election "1969 Philippine presidential election")

Marcos's second term was characterized by social unrest, beginning with the [1969 balance of payments crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Philippine_balance_of_payments_crisis "1969 Philippine balance of payments crisis"), which was triggered by exuberant infrastructure spending.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82) Opposition groups began to form, with moderate opposition calling for political reform and radicals espousing revolutionary ideology.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Passionate-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Daroy1988-120)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-GazetteHistoryProtest-121) A period of unrest and political violence culminated in Marcos's 1972 declaration of martial law, ending his term early and establishing himself as the constitutional dictator of the Philippines.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-govPhDeclarationMartialLaw-13)

#### Assassination plot and social unrest

Main article: [First Quarter Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Quarter_Storm "First Quarter Storm")

Further information: [Diliman Commune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diliman_Commune "Diliman Commune")

Early in Marcos's second term, Philippine and United States government officials alleged that a group composed mostly of retired military officers, headed by Liberal Party official [Terry Adevoso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Adevoso "Terry Adevoso"), had organized a revolutionary junta that sought to discredit and kill Marcos. The plot allegedly included Vice President [Fernando Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Lopez "Fernando Lopez").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-122)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-123)[_[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No\_original\_research#Primary,\_secondary\_and\_tertiary\_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")_][[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-auto1-124)[_[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No\_original\_research#Primary,\_secondary\_and\_tertiary\_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")_]

In addition to private opposition seeking to supplant Marcos, citizens concerned with the economic crisis and Marcos's spending policies challenged his political program.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosMartialLawNeverAgain-125) In addition to the student revolts, political opposition to the Marcos government grew. Opposition senators [Lorenzo Tañada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenzo_Ta%C3%B1ada "Lorenzo Tañada"), [Jovito Salonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jovito_Salonga "Jovito Salonga"), and [Jose W. Diokno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_W._Diokno "Jose W. Diokno") accused Marcos of seeking to exceed the two-term constitutional limitation and of increasing authoritarianism.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Kasaysayan9ch10-82)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosMartialLawNeverAgain-125) Organizations opposing Marcos during this period included the NUS, National Students League, and the [Movement of Concerned Citizens for Civil Liberties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Movement_of_Concerned_Citizens_for_Civil_Liberties "Movement of Concerned Citizens for Civil Liberties") (MCCCL), led by Diokno. The MCCCL staged mass rallies, attracting as many as 50 thousand attendees.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Daroy1988-120)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-GazetteHistoryProtest-121) Media reports classified the various opposition groups as either "moderate" or "radical."[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Daroy1988-120) Moderates included Catholic organizations, civil libertarians, and nationalist politicians who sought political reforms.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Passionate-119) Radicals included labor and student groups who wanted more systemic social and economic reform.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Passionate-119)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-GazetteHistoryProtest-121)

By 1970, campus study sessions on [Marxism–Leninism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxism%E2%80%93Leninism "Marxism–Leninism") in the Philippines had become common, and many students joined organizations associated with the [National Democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Democracy_(Philippines) "National Democracy (Philippines)") movement, including the [Kabataang Makabayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabataang_Makabayan "Kabataang Makabayan") (led by [Jose Maria Sison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Maria_Sison "Jose Maria Sison")), [Samahang Demokratiko ng Kabataan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samahang_Demokratiko_ng_Kabataan "Samahang Demokratiko ng Kabataan"), and [Malayang Pagkakaisa ng Kabataang Pilipino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayang_Pagkakaisa_ng_Kabataang_Pilipino "Malayang Pagkakaisa ng Kabataang Pilipino").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Passionate-119)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-GazetteHistoryProtest-121)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:8-126)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-127)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-128) The Marcos administration often made no distinction between the moderate political opposition and the student revolutionaries.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:1-129) Consistent with the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") geopolitical framework, in which the Philippines was a key regional ally of the United States against the [Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party"), Marcos broadly labeled his opposition as communist or, more specifically, [Maoist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maoism "Maoism"). With the participation of the armed forces, Marcos waged a campaign to eliminate the [Communist Party of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist_Party_of_the_Philippines "Communist Party of the Philippines"). emphasizing it as a threat to Philippine society.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-marcosMartialLawNeverAgain-125)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-RebellionRepressionPh-130):43[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-WorldBank-131)[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-132) According to American foreign policy scholar Richard J. Kessler, Marcos "mythologized the group, investing it with a revolutionary aura that only attracted more supporters."[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-:10-96)

Marcos responded to the civil unrest in his January 26, 1970, State of the Nation address. During the address, the [National Union of Students](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Union_of_Students_of_the_Philippines "National Union of Students of the Philippines") (NUS) organized a protest outside Congress, inviting other students to join. As Marcos and his wife Imelda left the building, the students threw stones, a stuffed alligator, and a coffin at them.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-InquirerRememberingFQS-133) Opposition groups quickly grew on campuses. Students declared a week-long boycott of classes and instead met to organize rallies.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Passionate-119)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Daroy1988-120) Protests led by student groups continued through the end of the university semester in March, and Marcos deployed military force to quell the demonstrators. This period became known as the [First Quarter Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Quarter_Storm "First Quarter Storm").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-GazetteHistoryProtest-121)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-Aureus_1985-134)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos#cite_note-RebellionRepressionPh-130) Another major protest took place on January 30, in front of the presidential palace. Activists rammed through the palace gate with a fire truck and charged the grounds, tossing rocks, pillboxes, and [Molotov cocktails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molotov_cocktails "Molotov cocktails"). From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986

This article is about the 10th president of the Philippines. For his son, the 17th president, see [Bongbong Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bongbong_Marcos "Bongbong Marcos"). For other uses, see [Ferdinand Marcos (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_Marcos_(disambiguation) "Ferdinand Marcos (disambiguation)").

In this [Filipino name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_name "Filipino name"), the [middle name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_name "Middle name") or maternal [family name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surname "Surname") is _Edralin_ and the surname or paternal family name is _Marcos_.
