Indira Gandhi and her father, [Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru "Jawaharlal Nehru") at an [antibiotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antibiotics "Antibiotics") manufacturing facility, [Poona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poona "Poona"), 1956.

In the 1950s, Indira, now Indira Gandhi after her marriage, unofficially served her father as a personal assistant during his tenure as the first [prime minister of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_minister_of_India "Prime minister of India").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-41) Near the end of the 1950s, Gandhi served as the president of the [Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"). In that capacity, she was instrumental in having the [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist "Communist")-led [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Kerala "Government of Kerala") state government dismissed in 1959. That government was India's first elected communist government.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-42) After her father's death in 1964 she was appointed a member of the [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha") (upper house) and served in Prime Minister [Lal Bahadur Shastri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lal_Bahadur_Shastri "Lal Bahadur Shastri")'s cabinet as [Minister of Information and Broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Information_and_Broadcasting "Minister of Information and Broadcasting").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-43) In January 1966, after Shastri's death, the Congress legislative party elected her over [Morarji Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morarji_Desai "Morarji Desai") as their leader. Congress party veteran [K. Kamaraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Kamaraj "K. Kamaraj") was instrumental in Gandhi achieving victory.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-44) Because she was a woman, other political leaders in India saw Gandhi as weak and hoped to use her as a puppet once elected:

> Congress President Kamaraj orchestrated Mrs. Gandhi's selection as prime minister because he perceived her to be weak enough that he and the other regional party bosses could control her, and yet strong enough to beat Desai [her political opponent] in a party election because of the high regard for her father... a woman would be an ideal tool for the Syndicate.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-45)

## Primary years (1966–1984)

Gandhi's first eleven years serving as prime minister saw her evolve from the perception of Congress party leaders as their puppet, to a strong leader with the iron resolve to split the party over her policy positions, or to go to war with Pakistan to assist Bangladesh in the 1971 liberation war. At the end of 1977, she was such a dominating figure in Indian politics that Congress party president [D. K. Barooah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._K._Barooah "D. K. Barooah") had coined the phrase "India is Indira and Indira is India."[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-46)

### First Term (1966–1967)

Gandhi formed her government as the Rajya Sabha member from Uttar Pradesh. She was the first indian prime minister from the Rajya Sabha. At the beginning of her first term as prime minister, she was widely criticised by the media and the opposition as the "_Goongi goodiya_" (Hindi for a "dumb doll") of the Congress party bosses who had orchestrated her election and then tried to constrain her.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-47)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-48) Indira was a reluctant successor to her famous father, although she had accompanied him on several official foreign visits and played a key role in bringing down the first democratically elected communist government in Kerala.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-49) According to certain sources it was the socialist leader [Ram Manohar Lohia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Manohar_Lohia "Ram Manohar Lohia") that first derided her as the "Goongi Goodiya", and it was later echoed by other Congress politicians who were wary of her rise in the party.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-50)

One of her first major actions was to crush the separatist [Mizo National Front uprising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mizo_National_Front_uprising "Mizo National Front uprising") in [Mizoram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mizoram "Mizoram") in 1966.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Fremont-Barnes_2015-51)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Guha_2017_p._136-52)

### Second Term (1967–1971)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/John_Gorton_and_Indira_Gandhi.jpg/250px-John_Gorton_and_Indira_Gandhi.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_Gorton_and_Indira_Gandhi.jpg)

Indira Gandhi with Australian [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Australia "Prime Minister of Australia")[John Gorton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Gorton "John Gorton") in 1968

The first electoral test for Gandhi was the [1967 general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Indian_general_election "1967 Indian general election") for the [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") and state assemblies. The Congress Party won a reduced majority in the Lok Sabha owing to widespread disenchantment over the rising prices of commodities, unemployment, economic stagnation and a food crisis. Gandhi was elected to the Lok Sabha from the [Raebareli constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raebareli_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Raebareli (Lok Sabha constituency)"). She had a rocky start after agreeing to [devalue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devalue "Devalue") the [rupee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_rupee "Indian rupee"), which created hardship for Indian businesses and consumers. The importation of wheat from the United States fell through due to political disputes.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Kapila1-53)

For the first time, the party also lost power or lost its majority in a number of states across the country. After the 1967 elections, Gandhi gradually began to move towards socialist policies. In 1969, she fell out with senior Congress party leaders over several issues. Chief among them was her decision to support [V. V. Giri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V._V._Giri "V. V. Giri"), an independent candidate, rather than the official Congress party candidate, [Neelam Sanjiva Reddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neelam_Sanjiva_Reddy "Neelam Sanjiva Reddy"), for the vacant position of [president of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_India "President of India"). The other was her announcement that the banks would be nationalised without consulting the finance minister, Morarji Desai. These steps culminated in party president [S. Nijalingappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._Nijalingappa "S. Nijalingappa") expelling her from the party for indiscipline.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-54)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-55)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-56) Gandhi, in turn, floated her own faction of the Congress party and managed to retain most of the Congress MPs on her side, with only 65 on the side of the [Congress (O)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_(O) "Congress (O)") faction. The Gandhi faction, called [Congress (R)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_(R) "Congress (R)"), lost its majority in the parliament but remained in power with the support of regional parties such as [DMK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dravida_Munnetra_Kazhagam "Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Rosser-57) The policies of the Congress under Gandhi, before the 1971 elections, also included proposals for the abolition of the [Privy Purse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privy_Purse_in_India "Privy Purse in India") to former rulers of the [princely states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state"). In 1969, the fourteen largest banks in India were nationalised.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-58)

#### Military conflict with China

Main article: [Nathu La and Cho La clashes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathu_La_and_Cho_La_clashes "Nathu La and Cho La clashes")

In 1967, a military conflict alongside the border of the Himalayan [Kingdom of Sikkim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sikkim "Kingdom of Sikkim"), then an Indian [protectorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectorate "Protectorate"), broke out between India and China. India won by repelling Chinese attacks and forced the subsequent withdrawal of Chinese forces from the region.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Chellaney-4) Throughout the conflict, the Indian losses were 88 killed and 163 wounded while Chinese casualties stood at 340 killed and 450 wounded, according to the Indian Defense Ministry.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-59) Chinese sources made no declarations of casualties but alleged India to be the aggressor.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-60)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-61)

In December 1967, Indira Gandhi remarked these developments that "China continues to maintain an attitude of hostility towards us and spares no opportunity to malign us and to carry on anti-Indian propaganda not only against the Indian Government but the whole way of our democratic functioning."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-62) In 1975, Gandhi incorporated [Sikkim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikkim "Sikkim") into India, after [a referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1975_Sikkimese_monarchy_referendum "1975 Sikkimese monarchy referendum") in which a majority of Sikkimese voted to join India.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-himalayan-63) The move was condemned as being a "despicable act of the Indian Government" by China. Chinese government mouthpiece _[China Daily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China\_Daily "China Daily")_ wrote that "the Nehrus, father and daughter, had always acted in this way, and Indira Gandhi had gone further".[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-64)

### Third Term (1971–1977)

[Garibi Hatao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garibi_Hatao "Garibi Hatao") (Remove Poverty) was the resonant theme for Gandhi's 1971 political bid. The slogan was developed in response to the combined opposition alliance's use of the two-word manifesto—"Indira Hatao" (Remove Indira).[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-1971.iz_iz_result-65)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-66)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-IGIN-67) The Garibi Hatao slogan and the proposed [anti-poverty programs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-poverty_programs "Anti-poverty programs") that came with it were designed to give Gandhi independent national support, based on the rural and urban poor. This would allow her to bypass the dominant rural [castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caste_system_in_India "Caste system in India") both in and of state and local governments as well as the urban commercial class. For their part, the previously voiceless poor would at last gain both political worth and political weight.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-IGIN-67) The programs created through Garibi Hatao, though carried out locally, were funded and developed by the Central Government in New Delhi. The program was supervised and staffed by the Indian National Congress party. "These programs also provided the central political leadership with new and vast patronage resources to be disbursed... throughout the country."[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-68)

The Congress government faced numerous problems during this term. Some of these were due to high inflation which in turn was caused by wartime expenses, drought in some parts of the country and, more importantly, the [1973 oil crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_oil_crisis "1973 oil crisis"). Opposition to her in the 1973–75 period, after the Gandhi wave had receded, was strongest in the states of [Bihar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bihar "Bihar") and [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat"). In Bihar, [Jayaprakash Narayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jayaprakash_Narayan "Jayaprakash Narayan"), the veteran leader came out of retirement to lead the protest movement there.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-jstor.org-69)

#### War with Pakistan

Gandhi's biggest achievement following the 1971 election came in December 1971 with India's decisive victory over [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan") in the [India–Pakistan war of 1971](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India%E2%80%93Pakistan_war_of_1971 "India–Pakistan war of 1971"). That victory occurred in the last two weeks of the [Bangladesh Liberation War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War "Bangladesh Liberation War"), which led to the formation of independent [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh"). An insurgency in [East Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Pakistan "East Pakistan") (now [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh")) formed in early 1971, with Bengalis and East Pakistanis revolting against authoritarian rule from the central West Pakistan Government. In response, Pakistani security forces launched the infamous Operation Searchlight, in which Pakistan committed [genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_genocide "Bangladesh genocide") among Bengali Hindus, nationalists and intelligentsia. Gandhi's India was initially restrained from intervening in the insurgency but quickly started to support Bengali rebels through the provision of military supplies. Indian forces clashed multiple times with Pakistani forces in the Eastern border. At one point, Indian forces along with Mukti Bahini rebels allied together and attacked Pakistani forces at Dhalai. The attack, supported and later successfully executed by India, was done to stop Pakistani cross-border shelling. The battle occurred more than a month before India's official intervention in December. Gandhi quickly dispatched more troops to the Eastern border with East Pakistan, hoping to support Mukti Bahini rebels and cease any Pakistani infiltration. Indian forces then clashed again with Pakistani forces after Indian forces crossed the border and secured Garibpur after a one-day battle lasting from 20 November 1971 to the 21st. The next day, on 22 November, Indian and Pakistani aircraft engaged in a dogfight over the Boyra Salient, in which thousands of people watched as four Indian [Folland Gnats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folland_Gnat "Folland Gnat") shot down two Pakistani [Canadair Sabres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadair_Sabre "Canadair Sabre") and damaged another. Both Pakistani pilots that were shot down were captured as prisoners of war. The Battle of Boyra instantly made the four Indian pilots celebrities and created large-scale nationalism as the Bangladesh Liberation War saw more and more Indian intervention and escalation. Other clashes also happened on the same day but did not receive as much media attention as did the battle of Boyra and Garibpur. On 3 December 1971, the Pakistan Air Force launched [Operation Chengiz Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Chengiz_Khan "Operation Chengiz Khan"), which saw Pakistani aircraft attacking Indian airbases and military installations across the Western border in a pre-emptive strike. The initial night-time attack by Pakistani forces was foiled, failing to inflict any major damage on Indian airbases, allowing Indian aircraft to counterattack into West Pakistan. Gandhi quickly declared a state of emergency and addressed the nation on radio shortly after midnight, stating: "We must be prepared for a long period of hardship and sacrifice."

Both countries mobilised for war and Gandhi ordered full-out war, ordering an invasion into East Pakistan. Pakistan's navy had not improved since the 1965 war, while the Pakistani airforce could not launch attacks on the same scale as the Indian airforce. The Pakistan Army quickly attempted major land operations on the Western border, but most of these attacks besides some in Kashmir stalled, and allowed Indian counterattacks to gain land. Pakistan's army lacked wide-scale organisation, contributing to miscommunication and high casualties in the western front.

In the eastern front of the war, Indian generals opted for a [lightning war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning_war "Lightning war"), using mechanised and airborne units to quickly bypass Pakistani opposition and advance rapidly towards the capital of East Pakistan, [Dhaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhaka "Dhaka"). [Jagjit Singh Aurora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagjit_Singh_Aurora "Jagjit Singh Aurora") led the Indian army's Eastern Command. The Indian air force quickly overcame the small contingent of Pakistani aircraft in East Pakistan, achieving air superiority. Indian forces liberated Jessore and several other towns during the Battle of Sylhet between 7 and 15 December 1971, which saw India conduct its first heliborne operation. India then conducted another airdrop on 9 December, with Indian forces led by Major General [Sagat Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagat_Singh "Sagat Singh") capturing just under 5,000 Pakistani POWs and also crossing the Meghna River towards Dhaka. Two days later, Indian forces conducted the largest airborne operation since World War II. 750 men of the [Parachute Regiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parachute_Regiment_(India) "Parachute Regiment (India)") landed in Tangail, defeating Pakistani forces and securing a direct route to Dhaka. Few Pakistani soldiers escaped the battle, with only 900 out of 7000 soldiers successfully retreating to Dhaka. By 12 December, Indian forces reached the outskirts of Dhaka and prepared to besiege the capital. Indian heavy artillery arrived by the 14th, and shelled the city.

As surrender became apparent by 14 December 1971, Pakistani paramilitaries and militia roamed the streets of Dhaka during the night, kidnapping, torturing and then executing any educated Bengali who was viewed as someone who could lead [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh") once Pakistan surrendered.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Over 200 of these people were killed on the 14th. By 16 December, Pakistani morale had reached a low point, with the Indian Army finally encircling Dhaka and besieging the city. On the 16th, Indian forces issued a 30-minute ultimatum for the city to surrender. Seeing that the city's defences paled in comparison to the Mukti Bahini and Indian forces outside the city, Lt-Gen. [A.A.K. Niazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.A.K._Niazi "A.A.K. Niazi") (Cdr. of Eastern Command) and his deputy, V-Adm. [M.S. Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_Shariff "Mohammad Shariff") surrendered the city without resistance. BBC News captured the moment of surrender as Indian soldiers from the Parachute Regiment streamed into the city. As Indian forces and Mukti Bahini rounded up the remaining Pakistani forces, Lieutenant General Jagjit Singh Aurora of India and A.A.K. Niazi of Pakistan signed the Pakistani Instrument of Surrender at 16:31Hrs IST on 16 December 1971. The surrender signified the collapse of the East Pakistan Government along with the end of the war. 93,000 soldiers of the Pakistani security forces surrendered, the largest surrender since World War II. The entire four-tiered military surrendered to India along with its officers and generals. Large crowds flooded the scenes as anti-Pakistani slogans emerged and Pakistani POWs were beaten by the locals. Eventually, Indian officers formed a human-chain to protect Pakistani POWs and Niazi from being lynched by the belligerent locals. Most of the 93,000 captured were Pakistan Army officers or paramilitary officers, along with 12,000 supporters ([razakars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Razakar "Razakar")). Hostilities officially ended on 17 December 1971. 8,000 Pakistani soldiers were killed along with 25,000 wounded; Indian forces suffered only 3,000 dead and 12,000 wounded. India claimed to have captured 3.6k square kilometres of Pakistani land on the Western Front while losing 126 square kilometres of land to Pakistan.

Gandhi was hailed as Goddess [Durga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durga "Durga") by the people as well as the opposition leaders at the time when India defeated Pakistan in the war.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Thakur-70)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-71)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-73)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-74)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-75) In the elections held for State assemblies across India in March 1972, the Congress (R) swept to power in most states riding on the post-war "Indira wave".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-jstor.org-69)

#### Verdict on electoral malpractice

Main article: [State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Uttar_Pradesh_v._Raj_Narain "State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raj Narain")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/Indira_and_Nixon.JPG/250px-Indira_and_Nixon.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indira_and_Nixon.JPG)

Gandhi with U.S. [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[Richard Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon "Richard Nixon"), 1971

On 12 June 1975, the [Allahabad High Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allahabad_High_Court "Allahabad High Court") declared Indira Gandhi's election to the Lok Sabha in 1971 void on the grounds of electoral malpractice. In an election petition filed by her 1971 opponent, [Raj Narain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Narain "Raj Narain") (who later defeated her in the 1977 parliamentary election running in the Raebareli constituency), alleged several major as well as minor instances of the use of government resources for campaigning.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-news.bbc.co.uk-1975-76)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-77) Gandhi had asked one of her colleagues in government, [Ashoke Kumar Sen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashoke_Kumar_Sen "Ashoke Kumar Sen"), to defend her in court.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-78) She gave evidence in her defence during the trial. After almost four years, the court found her guilty of dishonest election practices, excessive election expenditure, and of using government machinery and officials for party purposes.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-news.bbc.co.uk-1975-76)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-79) The judge, however, rejected the more serious charges of bribery, laid against her in the case.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-news.bbc.co.uk-1975-76)

The court ordered her stripped of her parliamentary seat and banned her from running for any office for six years. As the [constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_India "Constitution of India") requires that the Prime Minister must be a [member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Parliament,_Lok_Sabha "Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha") of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, the two houses of the [Parliament of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_India "Parliament of India"), she was effectively removed from office. However, Gandhi rejected calls to resign. She announced plans to appeal to the Supreme Court and insisted that the conviction did not undermine her position. She said, "There is a lot of talk about our government not being clean, but from our experience the situation was very much worse when [opposition] parties were forming governments."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-news.bbc.co.uk-1975-76) She dismissed criticism of the way her Congress Party raised election campaign money, saying all parties used the same methods. The prime minister retained the support of her party, which issued a statement backing her.

After news of the verdict spread, hundreds of supporters demonstrated outside her house, pledging their loyalty. Indian High Commissioner to the United Kingdom [Braj Kumar Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braj_Kumar_Nehru "Braj Kumar Nehru") said Gandhi's conviction would not harm her political career. "Mrs Gandhi has still today overwhelming support in the country," he said. "I believe the prime minister of India will continue in office until the electorate of India decides otherwise".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-80)

#### State of Emergency (1975–1977)

Main article: [The Emergency (India)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Emergency_(India) "The Emergency (India)")

Gandhi moved to restore order by ordering the arrest of most of the opposition participating in the unrest. Her Cabinet and government recommended that then President [Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fakhruddin_Ali_Ahmed "Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed") declare a [state of emergency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_emergency "State of emergency") because of the disorder and lawlessness following the Allahabad High Court decision. Accordingly, Ahmed declared a State of Emergency caused by internal disorder, based on the provisions of Article 352(1) of the Constitution, on 25 June 1975.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-81) At the time of emergency, there was a widespread rumour that Gandhi had ordered her search guards to eliminate firebrand trade unionist and socialist party leader [George Fernandes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Fernandes "George Fernandes"), while he was on a run. Few International organisations and Government officials issued request letters to Indira Gandhi pleading her to relinquish such decrees. Fernandes had called a nationwide railway strike in 1974, that shut the railways for three weeks and became the largest industrial action in Asia. Gandhi had turned furious over him and the strike was massively cracked down.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-82)

#### Rule by decree

Within a few months, [President's rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President's_rule "President's rule") was imposed on the two opposition-party-ruled states of Gujarat and [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"), thereby bringing the entire country under direct Central rule or under the rule of governments led by the Congress party.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-83) Police were granted powers to impose curfews and detain citizens indefinitely, and all publications were subjected to substantial censorship by the [Ministry of Information and Broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Information_and_Broadcasting_(India) "Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (India)"). Finally, the impending legislative assembly elections were postponed indefinitely, with all opposition-controlled state governments being removed by virtue of the constitutional provision allowing for a dismissal of a state government on the recommendation of the state's governor.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-84)

Indira Gandhi used the emergency provisions to change conflicting party members:

> Unlike her father [Jawaharlal Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru "Jawaharlal Nehru") who preferred to deal with strong chief ministers in control of their legislative parties and state party organizations, Mrs. Gandhi set out to remove every Congress chief minister who had an independent base and to replace each of them with ministers personally loyal to her...Even so, stability could not be maintained in the states...[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-85)

President Ahmed issued [ordinances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decree "Decree") that did not require debate in the Parliament, allowing Gandhi to [rule by decree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_by_decree "Rule by decree").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-86)

#### Rise of Sanjay Gandhi

During the emergency Gandhi's younger son, [Sanjay Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Gandhi "Sanjay Gandhi"), entered into Indian politics. He wielded tremendous power during the emergency without holding any government office. According to [Mark Tully](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Tully "Mark Tully"), "His inexperience did not stop him from using the Draconian powers his mother, Indira Gandhi, had taken to terrorise the administration, setting up what was in effect a police state."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-87) It was said that during the emergency Sanjay virtually ran India along with his friends, especially [Bansi Lal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bansi_Lal "Bansi Lal").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-88) It was also quipped that Sanjay had total control over his mother and that the government was run by the [PMH (Prime Minister House)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7,_Race_Course_Road "7, Race Course Road") rather than the [PMO (Prime Minister Office)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister's_Office_(India) "Prime Minister's Office (India)").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-89)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-90)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-The_Life_of_Indira_Gandhi-91)

### In opposition (1977–1980)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Face_detail%2C_Premier_Indira_Gandhi_%28Congrespartij%29%2C_Bestanddeelnr_929-0811_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Face_detail%2C_Premier_Indira_Gandhi_%28Congrespartij%29%2C_Bestanddeelnr_929-0811_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Face_detail,_Premier_Indira_Gandhi_(Congrespartij),_Bestanddeelnr_929-0811_(cropped).jpg)

Gandhi in 1977

In 1977, after extending the state of emergency twice, Indira Gandhi called [elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Indian_general_election "1977 Indian general election") to give the electorate a chance to vindicate her rule. She may have grossly misjudged her popularity by reading what the heavily censored press wrote about her.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-92) She was opposed by the [Janata alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janata_alliance "Janata alliance") of Opposition parties. The alliance was made up of [Bharatiya Jana Sangh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Jana_Sangh "Bharatiya Jana Sangh"), [Congress (O)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_(O) "Congress (O)"), The Socialist parties, and [Charan Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charan_Singh "Charan Singh")'s [Bharatiya Kranti Dal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Kranti_Dal "Bharatiya Kranti Dal") representing northern peasants and farmers. The Janata alliance, with [Jai Prakash Narayan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Prakash_Narayan "Jai Prakash Narayan") as its spiritual guide, claimed the elections were the last chance for India to choose between "democracy and dictatorship". The Congress Party split during the election campaign of 1977; veteran Gandhi supporters like [Jagjivan Ram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagjivan_Ram "Jagjivan Ram"), [Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemvati_Nandan_Bahuguna "Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna"), and [Nandini Satpathy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandini_Satpathy "Nandini Satpathy") were compelled to part ways and form a new political entity, the CFD ([Congress for Democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_for_Democracy "Congress for Democracy")) due primarily to intra-party politicking and the circumstances created by Sanjay Gandhi. The prevailing rumour was that he intended to dislodge Indira Gandhi, and the trio stood to prevent that. The Gandhi's Congress party was soundly crushed in the elections. The Janata Party's democracy or dictatorship claim seemed to resonate with the public. Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi lost their seats, and Congress was reduced to 153 seats (compared with 350 in the previous Lok Sabha), 92 of which were in the South. The Janata alliance, under the leadership of Morarji Desai, came to power after the State of Emergency was lifted. The alliance parties later merged to form the [Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janata_Party "Janata Party") under the guidance of Gandhian leader, Jayaprakash Narayan. The other leaders of the Janata Party were Charan Singh, Raj Narain, [George Fernandes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Fernandes "George Fernandes"), and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-93)

After the humiliating defeat in the election, the [king of Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birendra_of_Nepal "Birendra of Nepal"), through an intermediatory offered to move her and her family to [Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepal "Nepal"). She refused to shift herself, but was open to move her two sons Sanjay Gandhi and [Rajiv Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Gandhi "Rajiv Gandhi"). However, after consulting with [Kao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._N._Kao "R. N. Kao"), she declined the offer altogether keeping in view of her future political career.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-94)

#### In opposition and return to power

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/1984_CPA_5588.jpg/250px-1984_CPA_5588.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1984_CPA_5588.jpg)

1984 [USSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") commemorative stamp

Since Indira Gandhi had lost her seat in the election, the defeated Congress party appointed [Yashwantrao Chavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yashwantrao_Chavan "Yashwantrao Chavan") as their parliamentary party leader. Soon afterwards, the Congress party split again with Gandhi floating her own Congress faction called Congress(I) where I stood for Indira. She won a by-election in the [Chikmagalur Constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chikmagalur_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Chikmagalur (Lok Sabha constituency)") and took a seat in the Lok Sabha in November 1978[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-95)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-96) after the Janata Party's attempts to have [Kannada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada "Kannada") matinee idol [Rajkumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Rajkumar "Dr. Rajkumar") run against her failed when he refused to contest the election saying he wanted to remain apolitical.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-97) However, the Janata government's home minister, Charan Singh, ordered her arrest along with Sanjay Gandhi on several charges, none of which would be easy to prove in an Indian court. The arrest meant that Gandhi was automatically expelled from Parliament. The allegations included that she "had planned or thought of killing all opposition leaders in jail during the Emergency".[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-98) However, the strategy backfired disastrously. In response to her arrest, Gandhi's [supporters hijacked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Airlines_Flight_410 "Indian Airlines Flight 410") an [Indian Airlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Airlines "Indian Airlines") jet and demanded her immediate release.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-99) Her arrest and long-running trial gained her sympathy from many people. The Janata coalition was only united by its hatred of Gandhi (or "that woman" as some called her). The party included right wing [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu "Hindu") Nationalists, Socialists, and former Congress party members. With so little in common, the Morarji Desai government was bogged down by infighting. In 1979, the government began to unravel over the issue of the dual loyalties of some members to Janata and the [Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh "Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh") (RSS)—the [Hindu nationalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_nationalist "Hindu nationalist"),[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Horowitz-100)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Haynes2003-101)[paramilitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramilitary "Paramilitary")[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-McLeod2002-102) organisation. The ambitious Union finance minister, Charan Singh, who as the Union home minister during the previous year had ordered the Gandhi's' arrests, took advantage of this and started courting Indira and Sanjay. After a significant exodus from the party to Singh's faction, Desai resigned in July 1979. Singh was appointed prime minister, by President Reddy, after Indira Gandhi and Sanjay Gandhi promised Singh that Congress (I) would support his government from outside on certain conditions.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Supporting_Charan_Singh-103)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Charan_Singh-104) The conditions included dropping all charges against Indira and Sanjay. Since Singh refused to drop them, Congress (I) withdrew its support and President Reddy dissolved Parliament in August 1979.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-105)

Before the [1980 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Indian_general_election "1980 Indian general election") Indira Gandhi approached the [Shahi Imam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahi_Imam "Shahi Imam") of [Jama Masjid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jama_Masjid,_Delhi "Jama Masjid, Delhi") at the time, [Syed Abdullah Bukhari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syed_Abdullah_Bukhari "Syed Abdullah Bukhari") and entered into an agreement with him on the basis of 10-point programme to secure the support of the [Muslim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muslims "Muslims") votes.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-AgnihotriRay2002-106) In the elections held in January, Congress (I) under Gandhi's leadership returned to power with a landslide majority.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-107)

### Fourth Term (1980–1984)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/Indira-Gandhi-in-Finland-1983.jpg/250px-Indira-Gandhi-in-Finland-1983.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Indira-Gandhi-in-Finland-1983.jpg)

Gandhi on the stairs of the [National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Finland "National Museum of Finland") in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki"), [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland") on 10 June 1983

The Congress Party under Gandhi swept back into power in January 1980.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-108) In this election, Gandhi was elected by the voters of the [Medak constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medak_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Medak (Lok Sabha constituency)").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-109) On 23 June, Sanjay Gandhi was killed in a plane crash while performing an [aerobatic manoeuvre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerobatic_manoeuvre "Aerobatic manoeuvre") in New Delhi.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-110) In 1980, as a tribute to her son's dream of launching an indigenously manufactured car, Indira Gandhi nationalised Sanjay's debt-ridden company, [Maruti Udyog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maruti_Udyog "Maruti Udyog"), for Rs. 43,000,000 (4.34 [crore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crore "Crore")) and invited joint venture bids from automobile companies around the world. [Suzuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzuki "Suzuki") of Japan was selected as the partner. The company launched its first Indian-manufactured car in 1984.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-orfonline69-111)

By the time of Sanjay's death, Indira Gandhi trusted only family members, and therefore persuaded her reluctant son, [Rajiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Gandhi "Rajiv Gandhi"), to enter politics.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Auerbach-1984-38)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-112) Her PMO office staff included [H. Y. Sharada Prasad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._Y._Sharada_Prasad "H. Y. Sharada Prasad") as her information adviser and speechwriter.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-113)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-114)

At the [7th Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7th_Summit_of_the_Non-Aligned_Movement "7th Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement"), held in [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi") in 1983, Gandhi assumed the three-year chairmanship of the organisation, succeeding [Fidel Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-115)

### Operation Blue Star

Main article: [Operation Blue Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Blue_Star "Operation Blue Star")

After the 1977 elections, a coalition led by the [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh")-majority [Akali Dal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akali_Dal "Akali Dal") came to power in the northern Indian state of [Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab "Punjab"). In an effort to split the Akali Dal and gain popular support among the Sikhs, Gandhi's Congress Party helped to bring the orthodox religious leader [Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jarnail_Singh_Bhindranwale "Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale") to prominence in Punjab politics.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Gus2011-116)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Christine2008-117) Later, Bhindranwale's organisation, [Damdami Taksal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damdami_Taksal "Damdami Taksal"), became embroiled in violence with another religious sect called the [Sant Nirankari Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sant_Nirankari_Mission "Sant Nirankari Mission") and he was accused of instigating the murder of [Jagat Narain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lala_Jagat_Narain "Lala Jagat Narain"), the owner of the _[Punjab Kesari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab\_Kesari "Punjab Kesari")_ newspaper.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-William2011-118) After being arrested, Bhindranwale disassociated himself from the Congress Party and joined Akali Dal.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Deol2012-119) In July 1982, he led the campaign for the implementation of the [Anandpur Resolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anandpur_Resolution "Anandpur Resolution"), which demanded greater autonomy for the Sikh-majority state. Meanwhile, a small group of Sikhs, including some of Bhindranwale's followers, turned to militancy after being targeted by government officials and police for supporting the Anandpur Resolution.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Martin2004-120) In 1982, Bhindranwale and approximately 200 armed followers moved into a guest house called the Guru Nanak Niwas near the [Golden Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Temple "Golden Temple").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-itp1-121)

By 1983, the Temple complex had become a fort for many militants.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Satish_Jacob_1985-122)_[The Statesman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Statesman\_(India) "The Statesman (India)")_ later reported that [light machine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_machine_guns "Light machine guns") and [semi-automatic rifles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-automatic_rifles "Semi-automatic rifles") were known to have been brought into the compound.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-123) On 23 April 1983, the Punjab Police Deputy Inspector General [A. S. Atwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._S._Atwal "A. S. Atwal") was shot dead as he left the Temple compound. The next day, Harchand Singh Longowal (then president of Akali Dal) confirmed the involvement of Bhindranwale in the murder.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-124) After several futile negotiations, in June 1984, Gandhi ordered the Indian army to enter the Golden Temple to remove Bhindranwale and his supporters from the complex. The army used heavy artillery, including tanks, in the action code-named [Operation Blue Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Blue_Star "Operation Blue Star"). The operation badly damaged or destroyed parts of the Temple complex, including the [Akal Takht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akal_Takht "Akal Takht") shrine and the Sikh library. It led to the deaths of many Sikh fighters and innocent pilgrims. The number of casualties remains disputed, with estimates ranging from many hundreds to many thousands.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Univ._of_Michigan_Press-125)

Gandhi was accused of using the attack for political ends. Harjinder Singh Dilgeer stated that she attacked the temple complex to present herself as a great hero in order to win the general elections planned towards the end of 1984.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Dilg-126) There was fierce criticism of the action by Sikhs in India and overseas.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-127) There were also incidents of mutiny by Sikh soldiers in the aftermath of the attack.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Univ._of_Michigan_Press-125)

[Shrimati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimati "Shrimati")**Indira Priyadarshini Gandhi**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-2) ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")**Nehru**; 19 November 1917 – 31 October 1984)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-3) was an Indian stateswoman who twice served as the [Prime Minister of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_India "Prime Minister of India") from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her [assassination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Indira_Gandhi "Assassination of Indira Gandhi") in 1984. She was India's first and only female prime minister, and a central figure in Indian politics as the leader of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress") (INC). Gandhi also served as chairperson of the [Non-Aligned Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Aligned_Movement "Non-Aligned Movement") (NAM) from 1983 to 1984, becoming the first Indian to hold the position. She was the daughter of [Jawaharlal Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru "Jawaharlal Nehru"), the first prime minister of India, and the mother of [Rajiv Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Gandhi "Rajiv Gandhi"), who succeeded her as prime minister. Her cumulative tenure of 15 years and 350 days, spanning four terms, makes her the second-longest-serving Indian prime minister after her father and the longest-serving female head of government at the time of her death.

During her father Jawaharlal Nehru's premiership from 1947 to 1964, Gandhi was his hostess and accompanied him on his numerous foreign trips. In 1959, she played a part in the dissolution of the [communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communist "Communist")-led [Kerala state government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala_state_government "Kerala state government") as then-[president of the Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Indian_National_Congress "President of the Indian National Congress"), otherwise a ceremonial position to which she was elected earlier that year. [Lal Bahadur Shastri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lal_Bahadur_Shastri "Lal Bahadur Shastri"), who had succeeded Nehru as prime minister upon [his death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Jawaharlal_Nehru "Death and state funeral of Jawaharlal Nehru") in 1964, appointed her [minister of information and broadcasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Information_and_Broadcasting_(India) "Minister of Information and Broadcasting (India)") in [his government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shastri_ministry "Shastri ministry"); the same year she was elected to the [Rajya Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajya_Sabha "Rajya Sabha"), the upper house of the [Indian Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Parliament "Indian Parliament"). After Shastri's death in January 1966, Gandhi defeated her rival, [Morarji Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morarji_Desai "Morarji Desai"), in the INC's parliamentary leadership election to become leader and also succeeded Shastri as prime minister. With her premiership of India she became the [world's second female prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_elected_and_appointed_female_heads_of_state_and_government "List of elected and appointed female heads of state and government") after her Sri Lankan counterpart [Sirimavo Bandaranaike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirimavo_Bandaranaike "Sirimavo Bandaranaike"). She led the Congress to victory in two subsequent elections, starting with the [1967 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1967_Indian_general_election "1967 Indian general election"), in which she was first elected to the lower house of the Indian parliament, the [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha"). In 1971, her party secured its first [landslide victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landslide_victory "Landslide victory") since her father's sweep in [1962](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_Indian_general_election "1962 Indian general election"), focusing on issues such as poverty.

As prime minister, Gandhi was known for her uncompromising political stances and [centralisation of power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centralised_government "Centralised government") within the [executive branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_branch "Executive branch"). In 1967, she headed a [military conflict with China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathu_La_and_Cho_La_clashes "Nathu La and Cho La clashes") in which India repelled Chinese incursions into the [Himalayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himalayas "Himalayas").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Chellaney-4) In 1971, she went to [war with Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Pakistani_War_of_1971 "Indo-Pakistani War of 1971") in support of the [independence movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_point_movement "Six point movement") and [war of independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War "Bangladesh Liberation War") in [East Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Pakistan "East Pakistan"), which resulted in an Indian victory, the end of the [Bangladeshi genocide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladeshi_genocide "Bangladeshi genocide"), and the independence of [Bangladesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh"), as well as an increase in India's influence to the point where it became the sole [regional power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_power "Regional power") in [South Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Asia "South Asia").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-j653-5) Another military operation against Pakistan, codenamed [Operation Meghdoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Meghdoot "Operation Meghdoot"), occurred during her tenure in 1984, which led to India expanding the territory it effectively controlled in the disputed Kashmir region.

Gandhi also played a crucial role in initiating India's first successful [nuclear weapon test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smiling_Buddha "Smiling Buddha") in 1974. Her rule saw India grow closer to the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") by signing a [friendship treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indo-Soviet_Treaty_of_Friendship_and_Cooperation "Indo-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation") in 1971 to ward off perceived geopolitical threat as a result of the U.S. warming up to China. India received military, financial, and diplomatic support from the Soviet Union during its conflict with Pakistan in the same year.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-6) Though India was at the forefront of the [Non-Aligned Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Aligned_Movement "Non-Aligned Movement"), Gandhi made it one of the Soviet Union's closest allies in Asia, each often supporting the other in proxy wars and at the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-7)

Responding to separatist tendencies and a call for revolution, she instituted a [state of emergency from 1975 to 1977](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Emergency_(India) "The Emergency (India)"), during which she [ruled by decree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_by_decree "Rule by decree") and basic civil liberties were suspended.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-:5-8) More than 100,000 political opponents, journalists and dissenters were imprisoned.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-:5-8) Following the Emergency, the INC lost the [1977 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1977_Indian_general_election "1977 Indian general election") in the midst of massive anti-incumbency sentiment—the first such loss for the INC in the history of the Republic of India. She even lost her own parliamentary constituency. However, due to her portrayal as a strong leader and the weak governance of the [Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janata_Party "Janata Party"), her party won the [next election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Indian_general_election "1980 Indian general election") by a landslide and she returned to the premiership.

She faced the [Sikh separatist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh_separatism "Sikh separatism") movement throughout her fourth premiership; in response, she ordered [Operation Blue Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Blue_Star "Operation Blue Star"), which involved military action in the [Golden Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Temple "Golden Temple") and killed hundreds of [Sikhs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhs "Sikhs"). On 31 October 1984, she was assassinated by two of her bodyguards, both of whom were Sikh nationalists seeking retribution for the events at the temple.

Gandhi was cremated at the site now known as [Shakti Sthal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Sthal "Shakti Sthal") (transl. 'Place of strength'). The site is marked by a large monolithic rock of iron ore commemorating her as the "Iron Lady of India".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-advani-9)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-chopra-10) Gandhi is remembered as one of the most powerful women in the world.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-12) Her supporters cite her leadership during victories over geopolitical rivals China and Pakistan, the [Green Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Revolution_in_India "Green Revolution in India"), [a growing economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_policy_of_the_Indira_Gandhi_government "Economic policy of the Indira Gandhi government") in the early 1980s, and her [anti-poverty campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garibi_Hatao "Garibi Hatao") that led her to be known as Mother Indira among the country's poor and rural population. Critics note her [cult of personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_of_personality "Cult of personality") and authoritarian rule of India during the Emergency. In 1999, she was named "Woman of the Millennium" in an online poll organised by the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-BBCPOLL-13) In 2020, she was named by [_Time_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)") magazine among the 100 women who defined the past century as counterparts to the magazine's previous choices for [Man of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_Person_of_the_Year "Time Person of the Year").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-14)

## Early life and career

Indira Gandhi was born in [British ruled India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") as Indira Nehru, into a [Kashmiri Pandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmiri_Pandit "Kashmiri Pandit") family on 19 November 1917 in Allahabad (present-day [Prayagraj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prayagraj "Prayagraj")) in [Uttar Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank201013-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Indira_Priyadarshini-16) Her father, [Jawaharlal Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru "Jawaharlal Nehru"), was a leading figure in the [Indian movement for independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_movement_for_independence "Indian movement for independence") from [British rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj"), and became the first Prime Minister of the [Dominion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominion_of_India "Dominion of India") (and later [Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India")) of India.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGupte20123-17) Indira was her parents' only surviving child (she had a younger brother who died while young);[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank201031-18) she grew up with her mother, [Kamala Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Nehru "Kamala Nehru"), at the [Anand Bhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swaraj_Bhavan "Swaraj Bhavan"), a large family estate in Allahabad.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank201016-19) In 1930, the Nehru family donated the mansion to the Indian National Congress and renamed it [Swaraj Bhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swaraj_Bhavan "Swaraj Bhavan") (meaning abode of freedom). A new mansion was built nearby to serve as the family residence and given the name of the old [Anand Bhavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand_Bhavan "Anand Bhavan").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank201016-19) Indira had a lonely and unhappy childhood.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank201025-20) Her father was often away, directing political activities or incarcerated, while her mother was frequently bedridden with illness and later suffered an early death from [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank201032-21) Indira had limited contact with her father, mostly through letters.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank201055-22)

She was there in 1940, when [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") rapidly conquered Europe. Nehru tried to return to England through [Portugal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal "Portugal") but was left stranded for nearly two months. She managed to enter England in early 1941, and from there returned to India without completing her studies at Oxford. The university later awarded her an honorary degree. In 2010, Oxford honoured her further by selecting her as one of the ten Oxasians, illustrious [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_people "Asian people") graduates from the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-35)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-degree-1) During her stay in Britain, Nehru frequently met her future husband [Feroze Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feroze_Gandhi "Feroze Gandhi") (no relation to [Mahatma Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi")). In March 1942 they were married in Allahabad according to [Adi Dharm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adi_Dharm "Adi Dharm") rituals, although Feroze belonged to a [Zoroastrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoroastrian "Zoroastrian")[Parsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parsi "Parsi") family of [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-36) The couple had two sons, [Rajiv Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajiv_Gandhi "Rajiv Gandhi") (born 1944) and [Sanjay Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Gandhi "Sanjay Gandhi") (born 1946).[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Auerbach-1984-38)

In September 1942, Indira Gandhi was arrested over her role in the [Quit India Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quit_India_Movement "Quit India Movement"). She was released from jail in April 1943.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Duda_2006-39) "Mud entered our souls in the drabness of prison," she later recalled her time in the jail. She added, "When I came out, it was such a shock to see colors again I thought I would go out of my mind."[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indira_Gandhi#cite_note-Washington_Post1-40)
