An agency to enable Americans to volunteer in [developing countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developing_countries "Developing countries") appealed to Kennedy because it fit in with his campaign themes of self-sacrifice and volunteerism, while also providing a way to redefine American relations with the [Third World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_World "Third World").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBernstein1991259%E2%80%9379-39) His use of war rhetoric for peaceful ends made his appeal for the new idea compelling to public opinion.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-40)

On March 1, 1961, Kennedy signed [Executive Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Order "Executive Order") 10924 that officially started the Peace Corps. He appointed his brother-in-law, [Sargent Shriver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sargent_Shriver "Sargent Shriver"), to serve the agency's first director. Due in large part to Shriver's effective lobbying efforts, Congress approved the permanent establishment of the Peace Corps program on September 22, 1961. [Tanganyika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanganyika_(1961%E2%80%931964) "Tanganyika (1961–1964)") (present-day [Tanzania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanzania "Tanzania")) and [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") were the first countries to participate in the program.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-41) Kennedy took great pride in the Peace Corps, and he ensured that it remained free of CIA influence, but he largely left its administration to Shriver. Kennedy also saw the program as a means of countering the stereotype of the "[Ugly American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugly_American_(pejorative) "Ugly American (pejorative)")" and "[Yankee imperialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_imperialism "Yankee imperialism")," especially in the emerging nations of post-colonial Africa and Asia.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-42) In the first twenty-five years, more than 100,000 Americans served in 44 countries as part of the program. Most Peace Corps volunteers taught English in schools, but many became involved in activities like construction and food delivery.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006155%E2%80%93159-43)

### The Cold War and flexible response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: The Cold War and flexible response")]

Main article: [Flexible response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flexible_response "Flexible response")

Kennedy's foreign policy was dominated by American confrontations with the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union"), manifested by proxy contests in the global state of tension known as the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"). Like his predecessors, Kennedy adopted the policy of [containment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Containment "Containment"), which sought to stop the spread of communism.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008704%E2%80%93705-44) President Eisenhower's [New Look](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Look_(policy) "New Look (policy)") policy had emphasized the use of [nuclear weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapons "Nuclear weapons") to [deter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deterrence_theory "Deterrence theory") the threat of Soviet aggression. By 1960, however, public opinion was turning against New Look because it was not effective in stemming communist-inspired Third World revolutions.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-45) Fearful of the possibility of a global [nuclear war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_war "Nuclear war"), Kennedy implemented a new strategy known as [flexible response](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flexible_response "Flexible response"). This strategy relied on conventional arms to achieve limited goals. As part of this policy, Kennedy expanded the [United States special operations forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_special_operations_forces "United States special operations forces"), elite military units that could fight unconventionally in various conflicts. Kennedy hoped that the flexible response strategy would allow the U.S. to counter Soviet influence without resorting to war.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrinkley201276%E2%80%9377-46) At the same time, he ordered a massive build-up of the nuclear arsenal to establish superiority over the Soviet Union.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008704%E2%80%93705-44)

In pursuing this military build-up, Kennedy shifted away from Eisenhower's deep concern for budget deficits caused by military spending.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatterson1996489%E2%80%93490-47) In contrast to Eisenhower's warning about the perils of the [military-industrial complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military-industrial_complex "Military-industrial complex"), Kennedy focused on rearmament. From 1961 to 1964 the number of nuclear weapons increased by 50 percent, as did the number of [B-52 bombers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-52_bombers "B-52 bombers") to deliver them. The new ICBM force grew from 63 [intercontinental ballistic missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_ballistic_missiles "Intercontinental ballistic missiles") to 424. He authorized 23 new Polaris submarines, each of which carried 16 nuclear missiles. Meanwhile, he called on cities to prepare [fallout shelters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallout_shelters "Fallout shelters") for nuclear war.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-48)

In January 1961, [Soviet Premier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_of_the_Soviet_Union "Premier of the Soviet Union")Nikita Khrushchev declared his support for [wars of national liberation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wars_of_national_liberation "Wars of national liberation"). Kennedy interpreted this step as a direct threat to the "free world."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-49)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-50)

### Decolonization and developing countries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Decolonization and developing countries")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7d/President_John_F._Kennedy_Meets_with_the_President_of_the_Republic_of_Ghana%2C_Osagyefo_Dr._Kwame_Nkrumah_%28JFKWHP-AR6409-A%29.jpg/250px-President_John_F._Kennedy_Meets_with_the_President_of_the_Republic_of_Ghana%2C_Osagyefo_Dr._Kwame_Nkrumah_%28JFKWHP-AR6409-A%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_John_F._Kennedy_Meets_with_the_President_of_the_Republic_of_Ghana,_Osagyefo_Dr._Kwame_Nkrumah_(JFKWHP-AR6409-A).jpg)

Kennedy with [Kwame Nkrumah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Nkrumah "Kwame Nkrumah"), the first president of an independent [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana"), March 1961

Between 1960 and 1963, twenty-four [countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_by_date_of_formation "List of sovereign states by date of formation") gained independence as the process of [decolonization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonization "Decolonization") continued. Many of these nations sought to avoid close alignment with either the United States or the Soviet Union, and in 1961, the leaders of [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India"), [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia"), [Indonesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesia "Indonesia"), [Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt"), and [Ghana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") created the [Non-Aligned Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Aligned_Movement "Non-Aligned Movement"). Kennedy set out to woo the leaders and people of the Third World, expanding economic aid and appointing knowledgeable ambassadors.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008711%E2%80%93712-51) His administration established the [Food for Peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_for_Peace "Food for Peace") program and the [Peace Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_Corps "Peace Corps") to provide aid to developing countries in various ways. The Food for Peace program became a central element in American foreign policy, and eventually helped many countries to develop their economies and become commercial import customers.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-52)

During his presidency, Kennedy sought closer relations with Indian Prime Minister [Jawaharlal Nehru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru "Jawaharlal Nehru") through increased economic aid and a tilt away from [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan"), but made little progress in bringing India closer to the United States.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008712%E2%80%93713-53) Kennedy hoped to minimize Soviet influence in Egypt through good relations with President [Gamal Abdel Nasser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamal_Abdel_Nasser "Gamal Abdel Nasser"), but Nasser's [hostility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Cold_War "Arab Cold War") towards [Saudi Arabia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia") and [Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan "Jordan") closed off the possibility of closer relations.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008713%E2%80%93714-54) In Southeast Asia, Kennedy helped mediate the [West New Guinea dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_New_Guinea_dispute "West New Guinea dispute"), convincing Indonesia and the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") to agree to [a plebiscite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Act_of_Free_Choice "Act of Free Choice") to determine the status of [Dutch New Guinea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands_New_Guinea "Netherlands New Guinea").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006254%E2%80%93255-55)

#### Congo Crisis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Congo Crisis")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/President_John_F._Kennedy_Greets_Prime_Minister_Cyrille_Adoula_of_the_Republic_of_the_Congo_%28Leopoldville%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-President_John_F._Kennedy_Greets_Prime_Minister_Cyrille_Adoula_of_the_Republic_of_the_Congo_%28Leopoldville%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_John_F._Kennedy_Greets_Prime_Minister_Cyrille_Adoula_of_the_Republic_of_the_Congo_(Leopoldville)_(cropped).jpg)

President Kennedy with Congolese Prime Minister [Cyrille Adoula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrille_Adoula "Cyrille Adoula") in 1962

Having chaired a subcommittee on Africa of the U.S. Senate's [Foreign Relations Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_Relations_Committee "Foreign Relations Committee"), Kennedy had developed a special interest in Africa. During the election campaign, Kennedy managed to mention Africa nearly 500 times, often attacking the Eisenhower administration for losing ground on that continent,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-56) and stressed that the U.S. should be on the side of anti-colonialism and self-determination.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-jfklibrary.org-57)

Kennedy considered the [Congo Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congo_Crisis "Congo Crisis") to be one of the most important foreign policy issues facing his presidency.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006239%E2%80%93242-58) The [Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_Congo_(L%C3%A9opoldville) "Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville)") gained independence from Belgian colonial rule on June 30, 1960, and was almost immediately torn apart by what President Kennedy described as "civil strife, political unrest and public disorder."[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-jfklibrary.org-57) Former Prime Minister [Patrice Lumumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrice_Lumumba "Patrice Lumumba") had been murdered early in 1961 despite the presence of a [United Nations peacekeeping force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Operation_in_the_Congo "United Nations Operation in the Congo") (supported by Kennedy);[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006239%E2%80%93242-58)[Moïse Tshombe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mo%C3%AFse_Tshombe "Moïse Tshombe"), leader of the [State of Katanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Katanga "State of Katanga"), declared its independence from the Congo and the Soviet Union responded by sending weapons and technicians to underwrite their struggle. The crisis, exacerbated by Cold War tensions, continued well into the 1960s.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-jfklibrary.org-57)

Kennedy and his incoming advisers were apparently unaware of the CIA's involvement in Lumumba's death.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-ashton116-59) In fact, Kennedy wasn't even aware Lumumba had been killed until February 13, 1961.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-douglass212-60) On October 2, 1962, Kennedy signed United Nations bond issue bill to ensure U.S. assistance in financing United Nations peacekeeping operations in the Congo and elsewhere. Around this time, the Kennedy administration was making private attempts to convince Tshombe to reunite the breakaway Katanga that he led with the Congo, in advance of UN intervention.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-61)

### Cuba and the Soviet Union

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Cuba and the Soviet Union")]

#### Bay of Pigs Invasion

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Bay of Pigs Invasion")]

Main article: [Bay of Pigs Invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion "Bay of Pigs Invasion")

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a4/JFK_Brigade_2506_meeting.jpg/250px-JFK_Brigade_2506_meeting.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JFK_Brigade_2506_meeting.jpg)

President Kennedy and Jacqueline Kennedy greet members of the [2506 Cuban Invasion Brigade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigade_2506 "Brigade 2506") at Miami's [Orange Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Orange_Bowl "Miami Orange Bowl"). c.December 29, 1962

[Fulgencio Batista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fulgencio_Batista "Fulgencio Batista"), a Cuban dictator friendly towards the United States, had been forced out office in 1959 by the [Cuban Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Revolution "Cuban Revolution"). Many in the United States, including Kennedy himself, had initially hoped that Batista's successor, [Fidel Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro") would preside over democratic reforms. Dashing those hopes, by the end of 1960 Castro had embraced [Marxism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxism "Marxism"), confiscated American property, and accepted Soviet aid.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio200650%E2%80%9351-62) The Eisenhower administration had created a plan to overthrow Castro's regime though an invasion of Cuba by a counter-revolutionary insurgency composed of U.S.-trained, anti-Castro Cuban exiles[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchlesinger2002233,_238-63)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-64) led by [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence_Agency "Central Intelligence Agency") paramilitary officers.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves199369%E2%80%9373-65) Kennedy had campaigned on a hardline stance against Castro, and when presented with the plan that had been developed under the Eisenhower administration, he enthusiastically adopted it regardless of the risk of inflaming tensions with the Soviet Union.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-fiftyyearslater-66) Some advisors, including Schlesinger, [Under Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Under_Secretary_of_State "United States Under Secretary of State")[Chester Bowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_Bowles "Chester Bowles"), and former Secretary of State [Dean Acheson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dean_Acheson "Dean Acheson"), opposed the operation, but Bundy and McNamara both favored it, as did the [Joint Chiefs of Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Chiefs_of_Staff "Joint Chiefs of Staff"), despite serious reservations.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio200652%E2%80%9355-67) Kennedy approved the final invasion plan on April 4, 1961.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-68)

On April 15, 1961, eight CIA-supplied [B-26](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_A-26_Invader "Douglas A-26 Invader") bombers left Nicaragua to bomb Cuban airfields. The bombers missed many of their targets and left most of Castro's air force intact.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-69) On April 17, the 1,500 U.S.-trained [Cuban exile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_exile "Cuban exile") invasion force, known as [Brigade 2506](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brigade_2506 "Brigade 2506"), landed on the beach at Playa Girón in the [Bay of Pigs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs "Bay of Pigs") and immediately came under heavy fire.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves199371,_673-70) The goal was to spark a widespread popular uprising against Castro, but no such uprising occurred.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrinkley201268%E2%80%9369-71) Although the Eisenhower administration plan had called for an American airstrike to hold back the Cuban counterattack until the invaders were established, Kennedy rejected the strike because it would emphasize the American sponsorship of the invasion.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatterson1996493%E2%80%93495-72) CIA director Allen Dulles later stated that they thought the president would authorize any action required for success once the troops were on the ground.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves199371,_673-70) The invading force was defeated within two days by the [Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Revolutionary_Armed_Forces "Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces");[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-73) 114 were killed and over 1,100 were taken prisoner.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-74)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-75) Kennedy was forced to negotiate for the release of the 1,189 survivors. After twenty months, Cuba released the captured exiles in exchange for a ransom of $53 million worth of food and medicine.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchlesinger2002268%E2%80%93294,_838%E2%80%93839-76)

Despite the lack of direct U.S. military involvement, the Soviet Union, Cuba, and the international community all recognized that the U.S. had backed the invasion.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatterson1996493%E2%80%93495-72) Kennedy focused primarily on the political repercussions of the plan rather than military considerations.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves199395%E2%80%9397-77) In the aftermath, he took full responsibility for the failure, saying: "We got a big kick in the leg and we deserved it. But maybe we'll learn something from it."[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchlesinger2002290,_295-78) Kennedy's approval ratings climbed afterwards, helped in part by the vocal support given to him by Nixon and Eisenhower.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDallek2003370%E2%80%93371-79) Outside the United States, however, the operation undermined Kennedy's reputation as a world leader, and raised tensions with the Soviet Union.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrinkley201270%E2%80%9371-80) A secret review conducted by [Lyman Kirkpatrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyman_Kirkpatrick "Lyman Kirkpatrick") of the CIA concluded that the failure of the invasion resulted less from a decision against airstrikes and had more to do with the fact that Cuba had a much larger defending force and that the operation suffered from "poor planning, organization, staffing and management".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDallek2003363%E2%80%93366-81) The Kennedy administration [banned all Cuban imports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_embargo_against_Cuba "United States embargo against Cuba") and convinced the [Organization of American States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_of_American_States "Organization of American States") to expel Cuba.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008707%E2%80%93708-82) Kennedy dismissed Dulles as director of the CIA and increasingly relied on close advisers like Sorensen, Bundy, and Robert Kennedy as opposed to the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the CIA, and the State Department.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio200664%E2%80%9365,_68-83)

#### Operation Mongoose

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Operation Mongoose")]

In late-1961, the White House formed the Special Group (Augmented), headed by Robert Kennedy and including [Edward Lansdale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Lansdale "Edward Lansdale"), Secretary Robert McNamara, and others. The group's objective—to overthrow Castro via espionage, sabotage, and other covert tactics—was never pursued.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993264-84) In November 1961, he authorized [Operation Mongoose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Mongoose "Operation Mongoose") (also known as the Cuban Project).[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-eu.usatoday.com-85) In March 1962, Kennedy rejected [Operation Northwoods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Northwoods "Operation Northwoods"), proposals for [false flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_flag "False flag") attacks against American military and civilian targets,[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-1962USJCOS-86) and blaming them on the Cuban government in order to gain approval for a war against Cuba. However, the administration continued to plan for an invasion of Cuba in the summer of 1962.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-eu.usatoday.com-85)

#### Vienna Summit

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Vienna Summit")]

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/John_Kennedy%2C_Nikita_Khrushchev_1961.jpg/250px-John_Kennedy%2C_Nikita_Khrushchev_1961.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:John_Kennedy,_Nikita_Khrushchev_1961.jpg)

Kennedy meeting with [Soviet Premier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Premier "Soviet Premier")Nikita Khrushchev in [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna "Vienna") in June 1961

[Video 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e7/President_Kennedy_in_Vienna%2C_1961%2C_USIA.ogv?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

[U.S. Information Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Information_Agency "U.S. Information Agency") motion picture on the 1961 [Vienna Summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_Summit "Vienna Summit")

In the aftermath of the Bay of Pigs invasion, Kennedy announced that he would meet with Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev at the June 1961 [Vienna summit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_summit "Vienna summit"). The summit would cover several topics, but both leaders knew that the most contentious issue would be that of [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin"), which had been divided into two cities with the start of the Cold War. The enclave of [West Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Berlin "West Berlin") lay within Soviet-allied [East Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany"), but was supported by the U.S. and other Western powers. The Soviets wanted to reunify Berlin under the control of East Germany, partly due to the large number of East Germans who had fled to West Berlin.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrinkley201274,_77%E2%80%9378-87) Khrushchev had clashed with Eisenhower over the issue but had tabled it after the [1960 U-2 incident](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_U-2_incident "1960 U-2 incident"); with the inauguration of a new U.S. president, Khrushchev was once again determined to bring the status of West Berlin to the fore. Kennedy's handling of the Bay of Pigs crisis convinced him that Kennedy would wither under pressure. Kennedy, meanwhile, wanted to meet with Khrushchev as soon as possible in order to reduce tensions and minimize the risk of nuclear war. Prior to the summit, Harriman advised Kennedy, "[Khrushchev's] style will be to attack you and see if he can get away with it. Laugh about it, don't get into a fight. Rise above it. Have some fun."[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio200672%E2%80%9373,_76-88)

On the way to the summit, Kennedy stopped in Paris to meet French President [Charles de Gaulle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_de_Gaulle "Charles de Gaulle"), who advised him to ignore Khrushchev's abrasive style. The French president feared the United States' presumed influence in Europe. Nevertheless, de Gaulle was quite impressed with the young president and his family. Kennedy picked up on this in his speech in Paris, saying that he would be remembered as "the man who accompanied Jackie Kennedy to Paris."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993145-89)

On June 4, 1961, the president met with Khrushchev in Vienna, where he made it clear that any treaty between [East Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Berlin "East Berlin") and the Soviet Union that interfered with U.S. access rights in West Berlin would be regarded as an act of war.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993161%E2%80%93175-90) The two leaders also discussed the situation in Laos, the [Congo Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congo_Crisis "Congo Crisis"), China's [fledgling nuclear program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_and_weapons_of_mass_destruction "China and weapons of mass destruction"), a potential nuclear test ban treaty, and other issues.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio200678%E2%80%9379-91) Shortly after Kennedy returned home, the Soviet Union announced its intention to sign a treaty with East Berlin that would threaten Western access to West Berlin. Kennedy, depressed and angry, assumed that his only option was to prepare the country for nuclear war, which he personally thought had a one-in-five chance of occurring.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993161%E2%80%93175-90)

#### Berlin

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Berlin")]

See also: [Berlin Crisis of 1961](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Crisis_of_1961 "Berlin Crisis of 1961")

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/JFK_speech_Ich_bin_ein_berliner_1.jpg/250px-JFK_speech_Ich_bin_ein_berliner_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JFK_speech_lch_bin_ein_berliner_1.jpg)

Kennedy delivering his June 26, 1963, speech [West Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Berlin "West Berlin"), known as the _[Ich bin ein Berliner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ich\_bin\_ein\_Berliner "Ich bin ein Berliner")_ speech

President Kennedy called Berlin "the great testing place of Western courage and will."[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-Penguin_Publishing_Group-92) In the weeks immediately after the Vienna summit, more than 20,000 people [fled from East Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republikflucht "Republikflucht") to the western sector in reaction to statements from the Soviet Union. Kennedy began intensive meetings on the Berlin issue, where Dean Acheson took the lead in recommending a military buildup alongside NATO allies.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993185-93) In a July 1961 speech, Kennedy announced his decision to add $3.25 billion to the defense budget, along with over 200,000 additional troops, stating that an attack on West Berlin would be taken as an attack on the U.S.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993201-94) On August 13, 1961, the Soviet Union and East Berlin began blocking further passage of East Berliners into West Berlin and erected [barbed wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbed_wire "Barbed wire") fences across the city, which were quickly upgraded to the [Berlin Wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Wall "Berlin Wall").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993213-95) Kennedy acquiesced to the wall, though he sent Vice President Johnson to West Berlin to reaffirm U.S. commitment to the enclave's defense. In the following months, in a sign of rising Cold War tensions, both the U.S. and the Soviet Union ended a moratorium on nuclear weapon testing.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio200685%E2%80%9386-96) A brief stand-off between U.S. and Soviet tanks occurred at [Checkpoint Charlie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkpoint_Charlie "Checkpoint Charlie") in October following a dispute over free movement of Allied personnel. The crisis was defused largely through a backchannel communication the Kennedy administration had set up with Soviet spy [Georgi Bolshakov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgi_Bolshakov "Georgi Bolshakov").[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKempe2011[httpsarchiveorgdetailsberlin1961kenned0000kemppage478_478%E2%80%93479]-97)

In 1963, French President Charles de Gaulle was trying to build a Franco-West German counterweight to the American and Soviet spheres of influence.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-98)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-99)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-100) To Kennedy's eyes, this Franco-German cooperation seemed directed against [NATO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATO "NATO")'s influence in Europe.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-101) To reinforce the U.S. alliance with West Germany, Kennedy travelled to West Germany in June 1963. On June 26, Kennedy toured West Berlin, culminating in his famous "[Ich bin ein Berliner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ich_bin_ein_Berliner "Ich bin ein Berliner")" ("I am a Berliner") speech in front of hundreds of thousands of enthusiastic Berliners. Kennedy used the construction of the Berlin Wall as an example of the failures of communism: "Freedom has many difficulties, and democracy is not perfect. But we have never had to put a wall up to keep our people in, to prevent them from leaving us." In remarks to his aides on the Berlin Wall, Kennedy noted that "it's not a very nice solution, but a wall is a hell of a lot better than a war."[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-Penguin_Publishing_Group-92)

#### Cuban Missile Crisis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Cuban Missile Crisis")]

Main article: [Cuban Missile Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis "Cuban Missile Crisis")

[Video 2](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/52/1962-10-25_The_Cuban_Crisis.ogg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

[Universal Newsreel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Newsreel "Universal Newsreel") about the Cuban Missile Crisis

In the aftermath of the Bay of Pigs invasion, Cuban and Soviet leaders feared that the United States was planning another invasion of Cuba, and Khrushchev increased economic and military assistance to the island.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006203%E2%80%93205-102) The Soviet Union planned to allocate in Cuba 49 [medium-range ballistic missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medium-range_ballistic_missile "Medium-range ballistic missile"), 32 [intermediate-range ballistic missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermediate-range_ballistic_missile "Intermediate-range ballistic missile"), 49 light [Il-28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilyushin_Il-28 "Ilyushin Il-28") bombers and about 100 [tactical nuclear weapons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tactical_nuclear_weapon "Tactical nuclear weapon").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-103) The Kennedy administration viewed the growing [Cuba-Soviet alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba%E2%80%93Soviet_Union_relations "Cuba–Soviet Union relations") with alarm, fearing that it could eventually pose a threat to the United States.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrinkley2012113%E2%80%93114-104) Kennedy did not believe that the Soviet Union would risk placing nuclear weapons in Cuba, but he dispatched CIA [U-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockheed_U-2 "Lockheed U-2") spy planes to determine the extent of the Soviet military build-up.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrinkley2012113%E2%80%93114-104) On October 14, 1962, the spy planes [took photographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_reconnaissance "Aerial reconnaissance") of intermediate-range ballistic missile sites being built in Cuba by the Soviets. The photos were shown to Kennedy on October 16, and a consensus was reached that the missiles were offensive in nature.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993345-105)

Following the Vienna Summit, Khrushchev came to believe that Kennedy would not respond effectively to provocations. He saw the deployment of the missiles in Cuba as a way to close the "[missile gap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missile_gap "Missile gap")" and provide for the defense of Cuba. By late 1962, both the United States and the Soviet Union possessed [intercontinental ballistic missiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_ballistic_missile "Intercontinental ballistic missile") (ICBMs) capable of delivering nuclear payloads, but the U.S. maintained well over 100 ICBMs, as well as over 100 [submarine-launched ballistic missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine-launched_ballistic_missile "Submarine-launched ballistic missile") (SLBMs). By contrast, the Soviet Union did not possess SLBMs, and had less than 25 ICBMs. The placement of missiles in Cuba thus threatened to significantly enhance the Soviet Union's [first strike capability](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_strike_capability "First strike capability") and even the nuclear imbalance.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006205%E2%80%93208-106) Kennedy himself did not believe that the deployment of missiles to Cuba fundamentally altered the strategic balance of the nuclear forces; more significant for him was the political and psychological implications of allowing the Soviet Union to maintain nuclear weapons in Cuba.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006211-107)

Kennedy faced a dilemma: if the U.S. attacked the sites, it might lead to nuclear war with the U.S.S.R., but if the U.S. did nothing, it would be faced with the increased threat from close-range nuclear weapons (positioned approximately 90 mi (140 km) away from the Florida coast). The U.S. would also appear to the world as less committed to the defense of the Western Hemisphere. On a personal level, Kennedy needed to show resolve in reaction to Khrushchev, especially after the Vienna summit.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993245-108) To deal with the crisis, he formed an ad hoc body of key advisers, later known as [EXCOMM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EXCOMM "EXCOMM"), that met secretly between October 16 and 28.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006207%E2%80%93208-109) The members of EXCOMM agreed that the missiles must be removed from Cuba, but differed as to the best method. Some favored an airstrike, possibly followed by an invasion of Cuba, but Robert Kennedy and others argued that a surprise airstrike would be immoral and would invite Soviet reprisals.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006211%E2%80%93212-110) The other major option that emerged was a [naval blockade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockade "Blockade"), designed to prevent further arms shipments to Cuba. Though he had initially favored an immediate air strike, the president quickly came to favor the naval blockade the first method of response, while retaining the option of an airstrike at a later date.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006210,_212%E2%80%93213-111) EXCOMM voted 11-to-6 in favor of the naval blockade, which was also supported by British ambassador [David Ormsby-Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ormsby-Gore,_5th_Baron_Harlech "David Ormsby-Gore, 5th Baron Harlech") and Eisenhower, both of whom were consulted privately.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006215%E2%80%93217-112) On October 22, after privately informing the cabinet and leading members of Congress about the situation, Kennedy announced on national television that the U.S. had discovered evidence of the Soviet deployment of missiles to Cuba. He called for the immediate withdrawal of the missiles, as well as the convening of the [United Nations Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council") and the Organization of American States (OAS). Finally, he announced that the U.S. would begin a naval blockade of Cuba in order to intercept arms shipments.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006217%E2%80%93218-113)

On October 23, in a unanimous vote, the OAS approved a resolution that endorsed the blockade and called for the removal of the Soviet nuclear weapons from Cuba. That same day, Adlai Stevenson presented the U.S. case to the UN Security Council, though the Soviet Union's [veto power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_veto_power "United Nations Security Council veto power") precluded the possibility of passing a Security Council resolution.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006219-114) On the morning of October 24, over 150 U.S. ships were deployed to enforce the blockade against Cuba. Several Soviet ships approached the blockade line, but they stopped or reversed course to avoid the blockade.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006220-115) On October 25, Khrushchev offered to remove the missiles if the U.S. promised not to invade Cuba. The next day, he sent a second message in which he also demanded the removal of [PGM-19 Jupiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGM-19_Jupiter "PGM-19 Jupiter") missiles from [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008721%E2%80%93722-116) EXCOMM settled on what has been termed the "[Trollope ploy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trollope_ploy "Trollope ploy");" the U.S. would respond to the Khrushchev's first message and ignore the second. Kennedy managed to preserve restraint when a Soviet missile unauthorizedly downed a U.S. Lockheed U-2 reconnaissance aircraft over Cuba, killing the pilot [Rudolf Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf_Anderson "Rudolf Anderson").[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-117)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-118) On October 27, Kennedy sent a letter to Khrushchev calling for the removal of the Cuban missiles in return for an end to the blockade and an American promise to refrain from invading Cuba. At the president's direction, Robert Kennedy privately informed Soviet Ambassador [Anatoly Dobrynin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatoly_Dobrynin "Anatoly Dobrynin") that the U.S. would remove the Jupiter missiles from Turkey "within a short time after this crisis was over."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006225%E2%80%93226-119) Few members of EXCOMM expected Khrushchev to agree to the offer, but on October 28 Khrushchev publicly announced that he would withdraw the missiles from Cuba.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006225%E2%80%93226-119) Negotiations over the details of the withdrawal continued, but the U.S. ended the naval blockade on November 20, and most Soviet soldiers left Cuba by early 1963.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006228-120)

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/EXCOMM_meeting%2C_Cuban_Missile_Crisis%2C_29_October_1962.jpg/250px-EXCOMM_meeting%2C_Cuban_Missile_Crisis%2C_29_October_1962.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:EXCOMM_meeting,_Cuban_Missile_Crisis,_29_October_1962.jpg)

The U.S. publicly promised never to invade Cuba and privately agreed to remove its missiles in Italy and Turkey; the missiles were by then obsolete and had been supplanted by submarines equipped with [UGM-27 Polaris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UGM-27_Polaris "UGM-27 Polaris") missiles.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKenney2000184%E2%80%93186-121) In the aftermath of the crisis, a [Moscow–Washington hotline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow%E2%80%93Washington_hotline "Moscow–Washington hotline") was established to ensure clear communications between the leaders of the two countries.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008723-122) The Cuban Missile Crisis brought the world closer to nuclear war than at any point before or since. In the end, "the humanity" of the two men prevailed.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKenney2000189-123) The crisis improved the image of American willpower and the president's credibility. Kennedy's approval rating increased from 66% to 77% immediately thereafter.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993425-124) Kennedy's handling of the Cuban Missile Crisis has received wide praise from many scholars, although some critics fault the Kennedy administration for precipitating the crisis with its efforts to remove Castro.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrinkley2012124%E2%80%93126-125)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHerring2008722%E2%80%93723-126) Khrushchev, meanwhile, was widely mocked for his performance, and was removed from power in October 1964.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPatterson1996506-127) According to Anatoly Dobrynin, the top Soviet leadership took the Cuban outcome as "a blow to its prestige bordering on humiliation."[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-The_Malin_Notes-128)

#### Nuclear Test Ban Treaty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Nuclear Test Ban Treaty")]

Main article: [Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty "Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty")

Further information: [American University speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_University_speech "American University speech")

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/President_Kennedy_signs_Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty%2C_07_October_1963.jpg/250px-President_Kennedy_signs_Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty%2C_07_October_1963.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Kennedy_signs_Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty,_07_October_1963.jpg)

Kennedy signs the [Partial Test Ban Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_Test_Ban_Treaty "Partial Test Ban Treaty"), a major milestone in early [nuclear disarmament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_disarmament "Nuclear disarmament"), on October 7, 1963.

Troubled by the long-term dangers of [radioactive contamination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioactive_contamination "Radioactive contamination") and [nuclear weapons proliferation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_proliferation "Nuclear proliferation"), Kennedy and Khrushchev agreed to negotiate a nuclear test ban treaty, originally conceived in Adlai Stevenson's 1956 presidential campaign.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993552-129) In their Vienna summit meeting in June 1961, Khrushchev and Kennedy had reached an informal understanding against nuclear testing, but further negotiations were derailed by the resumption of nuclear testing.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993227-130) In his address to the United Nations on September 25, 1961, Kennedy challenged the Soviet Union "not to an arms race, but to a peace race." Unsuccessful in his efforts to reach a diplomatic agreement, Kennedy reluctantly announced the resumption of atmospheric testing on April 25, 1962.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty-131) Soviet-American relations improved after the resolution of the Cuban Missile Crisis, and the powers resumed negotiations over a test ban treaty.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006230%E2%80%93231-132) Negotiations were facilitated by the Vatican and by the shuttle diplomacy of editor Norman Cousins.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-133)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-134)

On June 10, 1963, Kennedy delivered a [commencement address](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commencement_address "Commencement address") at the [American University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_University "American University") in Washington, D.C. Also known as "A Strategy of Peace", not only did Kennedy outline a plan to curb nuclear arms, but he also "laid out a hopeful, yet realistic route for world peace at a time when the U.S. and Soviet Union faced the potential for an escalating nuclear arms race."[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-135) Kennedy also made two announcements: 1.) that the Soviets had expressed a desire to negotiate a nuclear test ban treaty, and 2.) that the U.S. had postponed planned atmospheric tests.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993514-136) "If we cannot end our differences," he said, "at least we can help make the world a safe place for diversity." The Soviet government broadcast a translation of the entire speech and allowed it to be reprinted in the controlled Soviet press.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty-131)

The following month, Kennedy sent W. Averell Harriman to Moscow to negotiate a test-ban treaty with the Soviets.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993542-137) Each party sought a comprehensive test ban treaty, but a dispute over the number of on-site inspections allowed in each year prevented a total ban on testing.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006230%E2%80%93231-132) Ultimately, the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union agreed to a limited treaty that prohibited atomic testing on the ground, in the atmosphere, or underwater, but not underground.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReeves1993550-138) The Limited Nuclear Test Ban treaty was signed in Moscow on August 5, 1963, by U.S. Secretary Dean Rusk, Soviet Foreign Minister [Andrei Gromyko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrei_Gromyko "Andrei Gromyko"), and British Foreign Secretary [Alec Douglas-Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alec_Douglas-Home "Alec Douglas-Home"). The U.S. Senate approved the treaty on September 23, 1963, by an 80–19 margin. Kennedy signed the ratified treaty on October 7, 1963.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-Nuclear_Test_Ban_Treaty-131) The treaty represented an important deescalation of Cold War tensions, but both countries continued to build their respective nuclear stockpiles.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006232%E2%80%93234-139) The U.S. and the Soviet Union also reached an agreement whereby the U.S. sold millions of bushels of wheat to the Soviet Union.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_F._Kennedy#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGiglio2006230-140)

**Konstantinos Alexandrou Karamanlis** ([Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language"): Κωνσταντίνος Αλεξάνδρου Καραμανλής; born 14 September 1956), commonly known as **Kostas Karamanlis** (Greek: Κώστας Καραμανλής, pronounced[[ˈkostas karamanˈlis]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Greek "Help:IPA/Greek")), is a Greek former politician who served as [prime minister of Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Greece "Prime Minister of Greece") from 2004 to 2009. He was also the president of the [centre-right](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centre-right_politics "Centre-right politics")[New Democracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Democracy_(Greece) "New Democracy (Greece)") party, founded by his uncle [Konstantinos Karamanlis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konstantinos_Karamanlis "Konstantinos Karamanlis"), from 1997 to 2009, and member of the [Hellenic Parliament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellenic_Parliament "Hellenic Parliament") from 1989 to 2023.

Karamanlis was first elected as a member of the Hellenic Parliament for New Democracy in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_1989_Greek_legislative_election "June 1989 Greek legislative election") and became president of the party in 1997. After leading the opposition in the Hellenic Parliament for seven years and his narrow defeat in the [2000 parliamentary election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Greek_legislative_election "2000 Greek legislative election"), he served as the [181st Prime Minister of Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Prime_Ministers_of_Greece "List of Prime Ministers of Greece") for two consecutive terms, winning the [2004 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Greek_legislative_election "2004 Greek legislative election"), with an all-time record number of votes, and again in [2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Greek_legislative_election "2007 Greek legislative election"). However, he asked for mid-term [general elections in 2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Greek_legislative_election "2009 Greek legislative election"), as his party enjoyed a narrow parliamentary majority that could not guarantee a stable government needed to handle the [Greek financial crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_government-debt_crisis "Greek government-debt crisis"), though two reports published by the [National Intelligence Service](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Intelligence_Service_(Greece) "National Intelligence Service (Greece)") in 2011 suggested a [conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy "Conspiracy") aiming to assassinate him and destabilise the Greek state. Eventually, Karamanlis was defeated and resigned as president of New Democracy after twelve years as the party's leader, being active in politics though as a member of the parliament. On 21 February 2023, it was announced that he would not be a parliamentary candidate and that he would retire from politics after the [2023 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/May_2023_Greek_legislative_election "May 2023 Greek legislative election").

In foreign policy, his government vetoed [North Macedonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Macedonia "North Macedonia")'s entry into NATO in 2008 due to the [Macedonia naming dispute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macedonia_naming_dispute "Macedonia naming dispute"). Infrastructural improvements during his premiership, including the successful preparation for the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics"), the expansion of the [Athens Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens_Metro "Athens Metro") and the beginning of construction for the [Thessaloniki Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thessaloniki_Metro "Thessaloniki Metro"), completion of the Egnatia Odos (A2) boosted his popularity. However, after the Greek financial crisis, which had begun at the tail end of his presidency, his government was accused of perpetuating economic mismanagement, while the lack of transparency regarding corruption cases and state finances were widely criticised. Despite remaining a significant figure for New Democracy after the party's defeat in the 2009 elections, his tenure is assessed unfavourably by academics and the general public. He is often considered one of the worst prime ministers in modern Greek history.

## Political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kostas_Karamanlis&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Political career")]

Kostas Karamanlis, a nephew of former Greek President [Konstantinos Karamanlis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konstantinos_Karamanlis "Konstantinos Karamanlis"), was born in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens") and studied at [University of Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Athens "University of Athens") Law School and at the private [Deree College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deree_College "Deree College"), continuing with postgraduate studies in the [Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fletcher_School_of_Law_and_Diplomacy "Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy") at [Tufts University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tufts_University "Tufts University") ([Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston")) in the United States, where he gained a master's degree and a doctorate in political sciences, international relations and diplomatic history.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-1)

Karamanlis served in New Democracy's organisational and ideological sectors from 1974 to 1979 and from 1984 to 1989. He is the author of a book, _Eleftherios Venizelos and Foreign Relations of Greece, 1928–32_, on the Greek politician [Eleftherios Venizelos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleftherios_Venizelos "Eleftherios Venizelos").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-2) He has also edited and prefaced various historical publications.

Karamanlis was elected a New Democracy deputy for [Thessaloniki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thessaloniki "Thessaloniki") in 1989, but in 2004 he was elected for [Larissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larissa "Larissa"). He was elected party leader in 1997 following New Democracy's defeat in the 1996 election. He defeated the ruling [Panhellenic Socialist Movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panhellenic_Socialist_Movement "Panhellenic Socialist Movement") (PASOK) at the [2004 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Greek_legislative_election "2004 Greek legislative election").

He served as one of the Vice Presidents of the [European People's Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_People's_Party "European People's Party") (EPP) between 1999 and 2006.

Karamanlis was the first Greek Prime Minister to be born after [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). He married [Natasa Pazaïti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natasa_Paza%C3%AFti "Natasa Pazaïti") in 1998 having two children born on 13 June 2003.

### Prime Minister of Greece (2004–2009)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kostas_Karamanlis&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Prime Minister of Greece (2004–2009)")]

Aided by the unpopularity of the incumbent PASOK government led by [Costas Simitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costas_Simitis "Costas Simitis") (a party that had been in power between 1981 and 1989 and from 1993 to 2004) ND defeated the Socialists' [George Andreas Papandreou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Andreas_Papandreou "George Andreas Papandreou") in 2004.

Karamanlis stated that the priorities of his government were [education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education "Education"), [economic policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_policy "Economic policy"), [agricultural policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agricultural_policy "Agricultural policy"), lowering the high level of [unemployment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment "Unemployment") (standing at 11.2%) and a more [transparent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_government "Open government") and effective state administration. Economic policy centered on [tax cuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_cut "Tax cut"), investment incentives, [privatization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privatization "Privatization"), and [market deregulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deregulation "Deregulation"). While early problems included a large [public debt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_debt "Public debt") (about 112% of GDP) and a budget deficit (5.3% of the GDP) in excess of [Eurozone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurozone "Eurozone") stability rules, Karamanlis's government halved the budget deficit to 2.6% by 2006.

Another key issue was the [2004 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics "2004 Summer Olympics") scheduled to be held in Athens in the first year of his government: several key buildings were unfinished at the time of the election, the security budget had increased to €970 million and authorities announced that a roof would no longer be constructed over the main swimming venue. The main [Olympic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Athens) "Olympic Stadium (Athens)"), the designated facility for the opening and closing ceremonies, was completed only two months before the games opened, with the sliding over of a futuristic glass roof designed by Spanish architect Santiago Calatrava. Other facilities, such as the [streetcar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tram "Tram") line linking the city and the airport were largely unfinished just two months before the games. The subsequent pace of preparation, however, made the rush to finish the Athens venues one of the tightest in Olympics history and everything was finished just in time for the Opening Ceremony. At the end, the Games were held exactly as planned and were globally hailed as a spectacular success. Nonetheless and as a result of the delays, large [cost overruns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cost_overruns "Cost overruns") resulted in a deficit in the national accounts above EU stipulations.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-3) The ND government and the previous government of [Costas Simitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costas_Simitis "Costas Simitis") criticized each other for the messy preparations. PASOK criticized the New Democracy government for using the Olympics as a pretext to renege on promises. Under the weight of the huge costs (estimated at €7bn), the deficit shot up to 5.3%. Karamanlis declared that "[Social policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_policy "Social policy") was done with borrowed cash, [military spending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_spending "Military spending") did not show up on the budget, [debts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_debt "Government debt") were created in secret".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-4)

#### Financial audit of 2004

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kostas_Karamanlis&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Financial audit of 2004")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ad/Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Congress_Warsaw_%28922%29.jpg/250px-Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Congress_Warsaw_%28922%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Congress_Warsaw_(922).jpg)

Kostas Karamanlis giving a speech in [Warsaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warsaw "Warsaw"), 2009.

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Summit_1_May_2004_Dublin_%283%29.jpg/250px-Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Summit_1_May_2004_Dublin_%283%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Summit_1_May_2004_Dublin_(3).jpg)

Kostas Karamanlis with [José Manuel Barroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Manuel_Barroso "José Manuel Barroso") in [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin"), 2004.

In March 2004, while PASOK was still in government, Eurostat refused to validate the fiscal data transmitted by the Greek government and asked for a revision, as it had done previously twice in 2002, resulting in a revision which changed the government balance from a surplus to a deficit.

A worse blow came in May 2004, when the European Commission harshly accused Greece of "imprudent" and "sloppy" fiscal policies,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-5) pointing out that since Greek economic growth had been an annual 4% in 2000–2003, a declining fiscal position could only be the result of government mismanagement, including concerns by the EU regarding the 103% [public debt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_debt "Public debt") to GDP ratio which Karamanlis had inherited from the previous PASOK regime. With this report, the Commission effectively called into question the quality of Greek economic data, as Eurostat had done in March.

The New Democracy government under Karamanlis, elected on April of that year, decided to conduct a Financial Audit of the Greek economy, before sending [revised data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revised_data "Revised data") to Eurostat. The audit concluded that the PASOK administration and prime minister Costas Simitis had falsified Greece's macroeconomic statistics, on the basis of which the European institutions accepted Greece to join the Eurozone. PASOK contested the accusations and claimed that 2006 Eurostat changes to the system of defense expenditure calculation[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-6) legitimized the practices of the Costas Simitis government. New Democracy responded that the defense expenditures covered by those changes constituted only a small part of much more substantial expenditures that were fraudulently concealed by the previous PASOK government.

In [social policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_policy "Social policy"), the [retirement age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retirement_age "Retirement age") was raised from 58 to 60 for those with 35 years of insurance, while early retirement went up from 55 to 60 for those who entered the labor market after 1993. [Supplementary pensions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_pension "Social pension") were also cut. In addition, mothers with under-aged children could retire at 55 instead of 50, while [paid maternity leave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parental_leave "Parental leave") was extended to 6 months in the private sector.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-7)

Rising [unemployment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unemployment "Unemployment") and the threat of [inflation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflation "Inflation") undermined Karamanlis's promises to kick-start the economy and sparked [strikes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_action "Strike action"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-11) especially one in 2006 by rubbish collectors,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-12) causing severe disruption in the economy – particularly the one in July 2005 at the height of the tourist season.

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c7/Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Summit_14_December_2006_%284%29.jpg/250px-Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Summit_14_December_2006_%284%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Flickr_-_europeanpeoplesparty_-_EPP_Summit_14_December_2006_(4).jpg)

Kostas Karamanlis with German Chancellor [Angela Merkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Merkel "Angela Merkel") in 2006

In early 2006, it was revealed that the cellular phone of Kostas Karamanlis, as well as those of several other members of the government and officials of the armed forces, had been [wiretapped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiretapping "Wiretapping") for several months during and after the 2004 Athens Olympics.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-13) The investigation into this matter by the Greek organization for communications privacy was closed with the argument that if this investigation would carry on, the information revealed would be dangerous for the [national security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_security "National security") of Greece.

The government has undertaken a €210 million program to bolster broadband internet connectivity in provincial Greece, which was approved by the European Commission in 2006 with the commendation that it constituted "the most ambitious broadband development programme that any EU member has ever undertaken".

In matters of social policy, Karamanlis's government has followed a largely [liberal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism "Liberalism") policy. In the spring of 2006, the Ministry of Education repealed a law continuously in effect from 1936 (including 20 years of socialist rule), which required approval by the local Orthodox Christian Metropolitan for the building of non-Orthodox houses of worship.

At the outset of the year, prime minister Karamanlis announced the initiative of his government for a new amendment to the [Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Greece "Constitution of Greece"). He stated that one of the central issues of this amendment will be the legalisation of [private universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_university "Private university") in Greece, operating on a [non-profit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization "Nonprofit organization") basis. Greece has for years experienced a mass exodus of "educational immigrants" to other countries' Higher Education institutions, where they move to study; this creates a chronic problem for Greece, in terms of loss of capital as well as human resources, since many of those students opt to seek employment in the countries they studied, after getting their degrees (it is characteristic Greece is by far the leading country in the world in terms of students abroad as a percentage of the general population, with 5250 students per million, compared to second Malaysia's 1780 students per million inhabitants). Proponents of non-state owned Universities claim that the State's constitutionally mandated monopoly on [Higher Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertiary_education "Tertiary education") is responsible for these problems.

Attempted changes in [Greek higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education_in_Greece "Higher education in Greece") have encountered fierce opposition from the other parties, as well as from the majority of the academic community, both [professors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor "Professor") and [students](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student "Student"). An attempt to pass several changes concerning the operation of Greek universities resulted in large-scale demonstrations, bringing together tens of thousands of [protesters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protest "Protest"), and, finally, the closure of most institutions by protesting students in the summer of 2006. The semester's exam period was lost and postponed until the fall, while the government shelved the changes and claimed that no bill would be put to a parliamentary vote before a more extensive dialogue had been held with students. However, without any further [dialogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dialogue "Dialogue"), the [legislation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legislation "Legislation") was passed in 2007.

#### 2007 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kostas_Karamanlis&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2007 election")]

Kostas Karamanlis with [Vladimir Putin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin "Vladimir Putin") in [Kremlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kremlin "Kremlin"), 2008.

In the [2007 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Greek_legislative_election "2007 Greek legislative election"), Karamanlis was re-elected with a [diminished](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diminished_responsibility "Diminished responsibility")[majority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majority "Majority"), following the [2007 Greek forest fires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Greek_forest_fires "2007 Greek forest fires") that ravaged much of western [Peloponnese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peloponnese "Peloponnese") and southern [Euboea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euboea "Euboea"). He pledged to continue with his [reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform "Reform") and [privatization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privatization "Privatization") programme as well as to form a new Cabinet.

On 19 September 2007, he presented a new cabinet.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-14)

#### 2009 election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kostas_Karamanlis&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2009 election")]

In the [2009 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Greek_legislative_election "2009 Greek legislative election"), Karamanlis and New Democracy were voted out of the government. He stepped down on 30 November after elections within the New Democracy party for the election of new party leader.

## Criticism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kostas_Karamanlis&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Criticism")]

The prime minister came under criticism during the [wildfires of 2007](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Greek_forest_fires "2007 Greek forest fires").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-15) With hundreds of thousands of acres burning and many deaths, the government had faced growing scrutiny for its response to the fires. In the days following the fires and the seeming lack of a substantial fire-fighting response adequate to stop the blazes, the government suggested the process was not natural and the work of arsonists.

A group of Pakistani men has claimed that they were abducted by Greek and British intelligence agents in the wake of the [7 July 2005 London bombings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7_July_2005_London_bombings "7 July 2005 London bombings"). The governments of Greece, Pakistan, and Britain have denied accusations that they were involved in the alleged detention of 28 Pakistanis for several days in [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens") and Ioannina after the 7 July bombings in London. The prosecutor assigned to the case said he had no evidence of who committed the abductions, but the main opposition party [PASOK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panhellenic_Socialist_Movement "Panhellenic Socialist Movement") called for the resignation of Greek [public order minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_for_Public_Order_(Greece) "Minister for Public Order (Greece)")[Georgios Voulgarakis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgios_Voulgarakis "Georgios Voulgarakis"). An unnamed human rights group (possibly biased) also called for the resignation of the Prime Minister, Kostas Karamanlis over the allegations.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-19)

A number of serious scandals involving Karamanlis's closest ministers and members of his party surfaced during his term, damaging his public image severely. Karamanlis was largely elected in 2004 due to his plea to "clear" public life from corruption.

Another criticism against Karamanlis and his cabinet involved the [2008 riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_civil_unrest_in_Greece "2008 civil unrest in Greece"), which started after the killing of 15-year-old Alexandros Grigoropoulos by a police officer. Police said Grigoropoulos was in a group of four teenagers who used hard language to a few policemen by a car. One officer was charged, and Reuters noted that "Greece has a tradition of violence at student rallies and fire bomb attacks by anarchist groups." [Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") called for a speedy investigation. The death of Grigoropoulos resulted in large demonstrations and widespread riots in major Greek and foreign cities.

After he left office, many in Greece continued to blame the New Democracy governments of Karamanlis for economic difficulties.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-20) Financial markets and Greece's EU partners chastised the country for vastly underestimated budget deficits under his watch.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis#cite_note-21)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Greek politician

This article is about the Prime Minister of Greece between 2004 and 2009. For his uncle, a former Prime Minister and President of Greece, see [Konstantinos Karamanlis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konstantinos_Karamanlis "Konstantinos Karamanlis").

Not to be confused with [Kostas Karamanlis (politician, born 1974)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kostas_Karamanlis_(politician,_born_1974) "Kostas Karamanlis (politician, born 1974)").
